of God, so that daisies are not thrown to swine or what is holy is given to dogs, who prefer to bark persistently rather than search diligently, or do not want to bark or investigate, but rather wallow in the mire of their lusts. When the praises of God are announced in response to good loves, it is given to those who ask, it is declared to those who seek and it is opened to those who call. Or is it that perhaps the gates of death are the senses and the eyes that were opened to man when he tasted the forbidden tree, from which those are exalted who are told not to seek the things that are seen, but those that are not seen, because those that are seen are temporary, and those that are not seen are eternal, and the doors of the daughter of Zion are the sacraments and the beginnings of faith, which open those who knock to come to the hidden things of the Son? No eye has seen, no ear has heard, nor have they entered into the heart of man the things that God prepared for his lovers. Up to this point is the cry of the poor whom the Lord has not forgotten.

14 [v. 14. 15 }. I ask: What is the cry of the poor that God does not forget? Perhaps it is the one who bursts out with these words: Have mercy on me, O Lord!; look at my despondency on the part of my enemies? Why didn't he say, have mercy on us, O Lord! Look at our despondency, coming from our enemies, as if many poor people cried out, but, as if only one cried out, he says: Have mercy on me, O Lord!? Or is it that perhaps it is one who intercedes for the saints, who first became poor for us, being rich, and He is the same who says: You who raise me up from the gates of death so that I may announce all your glories at the gates of the daughter of Zion? Man (Jesus Christ) is exalted for being head of the Church, not only in the one whom he leads, but also each of us is exalted in the remaining members, and, furthermore, man is also exalted by all the perverse desires, which are doors of death, since through them one goes towards death. Death is the same joy that is felt in enjoying when someone obtains what he desperately desired, and evil desire is the root of all evil, and, therefore, it is the door of death, because the widow is dead who lives in delights, which are reached through bad desires as through the doors of death. The gates of the daughter of Zion are all the most excellent affections, by which the vision of peace in the holy Church is reached. In these doors all glories are rightly announced

15 [v. 16]. Then he continues: I will rejoice in your health, that is, I will be preserved with joy because of your health, which is our Lord Jesus Christ, Virtue and Wisdom of God. Then the Church says that it takes hold here and is saved by hope. While the judgment of the Son remains hidden, he says with the same hope: I will rejoice in your health, because now it is mistreated, causing uproar, now with violence, now with the error of the Gentiles. The people sank into the depravity they carried out. Notice how punishment parallel to his sins is reserved for the sinner.

your est; quasi dicerent postea quam audierunt, Memoratus est, Ergo oblitus erat; Non est oblitus, inquit, clamorem pauperum. 14 [v.14.15]. Sed quaero quis clamor pauperum sit quem Deus non obliviscitur. An is this clamor est, cuius haec verba sunt: ​​Miserere mei, Domine, vide humilitatem meam ab inimicis meis? Quare ergo non dixit, Miserere nostri, Domine, vide humilitatem nostram ab inimicis nostris, tanquam multi pauperes clament; sed tanquam unus, Miserere mei, Domine? An quia unus interpellat pro sanctis, qui primus pauper pro nobis factus est, cum esset dives (2 Cor 8,9), et ipse dicit: Who exalts me de portis mortis, ut annuntiem universas laudes tuas in portis filiae Sion? Exaltatur enim homo in illo non solum quem gestat, quod caput Ecclesiae est, sed etiam quisquís nostrum est in caeteris membris; et exaltatur ab ómnibus pravis cupiditatibus, quae sunt portae mortis, quia per illas itur in mortem. Mors autem est iam ipsa laetitia in perfruendo, cum quisque adipiscitur quod perdite concupivit; radix est enim omnium malorum cupiditas (1 Tim 6:10); et propterea porta mortis est, quia mortua est vidua quae in deliciis vivit (Ib. 5,6): ad quas delicias per cupiditates tanquam per portas mortis pervenitur. Sunt autem portae filiae Sion, omnia optimal studia, per quae venitur ad visionem pacis in sancta Ecclesia. In his igitur portis bene annuntiantur universae laudes Dei, ut non detur sanctum canibus, ñeque proiiciantur margaritae ante porcos (Mt 7,6); who malunt

pertinaciter latrare, quam studiose quaerere, aut qui nec latrare nec quaerere, sed in suarum voluptatum coeno volutari. Cum autem in bonis studiis laudes Dei annuntiantur, petentibus datur, et quaerentibus manifestatur, et pulsantibus aperitur. An forte portae mortis sunt corporales sensus et oculi, qui aperti sunt homini cum de ligno vetito gustasset (Gen 3,7), a quibus exaltantur, quibus dicitur ut quaerant non quae videntur, sed quae non videntur; quia quae videntur temporalia sunt, quae autem non videntur aeterna sunt (2 Cor 4:18): et portae sunt filiae Zion, sacramenta et initia fidei, quae pulsantibus aperiuntur, ut perveniatur ad occulta Filii? Non enim oculus vidit, aut auris audivit, aut in cor hominis ascendit, quae praeparavit Deus diligentibus se (1 Cor 2:9). Huc usque est clamor pauperum, quem non oblitus est Dominus. 15 [v.16]. Deinde sequitur, Exsultabo super salutare tuum: id est, cum beatitude continebor a salutari tuo, quod est Dominus noster Iesus Christus, Virtus et Sapientia Dei (Ib. 1,24). Ergo Ecclesia dicit quae hic affligitur, et spe salva est: quamdiu occultum est Filii iudicium, ipsa spe dicit, Exsultabo super salutare tuum; quia never circumstrepente seu vi, seu errore Gentilium atteritur. Infixae sunt gentes in corruptione, quam jecerunt: animadverte quemadmodum servetur poena peccatorj de operibus suis; et quemadmodum qui voluerunt persequi Ecclesiam, in ea corruption

works and in what way those who wanted to persecute the Church are plunged into that depravity that they thought to inflict, since they wanted to kill the bodies, while in this way they died in the soul. In the same mousetrap that they hid, his foot was grabbed. The hidden mousetrap is malicious thinking. Rightly the foot of the soul is understood as love, which when evil is called greed or lust, but when it is good, dilection or charity. Through love he moves to the place where he is going. The place of the soul is not found in the space occupied by the figure of the body, but in the delight where it is glad to have arrived through love. Perverse delight follows greed; the pious, to charity. Therefore greed was called root. It is certainly understood that the root is like the foot of the tree. Root was also called charity where the Lord speaks about the seeds that, falling on rocky places, dry up when the sun rises, because they do not have a deep root. In which he points out those who rejoice in receiving the word of truth, but who bow down in the face of persecution, which can only be resisted with charity. The Apostle also says: Be rooted and grounded in charity so that you may understand. Then the foot of sinners, that is, love, is caught in the mousetrap that they hide, because when the delight has gone in pursuit of a deceitful action, when God gives them over to the filthy desire of their perverse heart, that delight already binds them so that from there they do not decide to detach themselves from love and dare to turn to useful things, because when they try to do so their soul will hurt, as when trying to get their foot, imprisoned by the shackles, and succumbing to such pain, they will not want ne sint fixi, quam se inferre arbitrabantur: nam interficere corpora cupiebant, cum ipsi in anima morerentur. In muscipula ista, quam occultaverunt, comprehensus est pes eorum. Muscipula occulta, est dolosa cogitatio. Pes am'mae recte intelíigítur amor: qui cum pravus est, vocatur cupiditas aut libido; cum autem rectus, dilectio vel chantas. Amore enim movetur tanquam ad locum quo tendit. Locus autem animae non in spatio aliquo est, quod forma occupat corporis, sed in delectatione, quo se pervenisse per amorem laetatur: delectatio autem perniciosa sequitur cupiditatem, fructuosa charitatem.

Unde et radix dicta est cupiditas (1 Tim 6:10). Radix porro tanquam pes arboris intelligitur. Radix dicta est et charitas, ubi de seminibus Dominus loquitur, quae in petrosis locis exurente solé arescunt, quia non habent altam radicem (Mt 13,5). Unde significat eos qui gaudent excipiendo verbum veritatis, sed cedunt persecutionibus, quibus sola chántate resistitur. Et Apostolus dicit: Ut in chántate radicali et jundati possitis comprehendere (Eph 3,17). Pes ergo peccatorum, id est amor, comprehenditur in muscipula quam occultant; quia cum fraudulentam actionem consecuta fuerit delectatio, cum eos tradiderit Deus in concupiscentiam cordis eorum (Rom 1,24), iam illa delectatio alligat eos, ut inde abrumpere amorem et ad utilia conferre non audeant; quia cum conati fuerint, dolebunt animo, tanquam pedem de compede exuere cupientes;

turn away from perverse delights. Then in the mousetrap that they hid, that is, in the deceitful advice, their foot was grasped, that is, love, which through deception leads to vain joy, which is compared to pain. 16 [v. 17]. The Lord is known doing justice. These are the judgments of God: he does not draw from that stillness of his blessedness nor from the secrets of wisdom, in which holy souls are received, iron, or fire, or racks, or anything similar, with which sinners are tormented. How are they tormented and how does the Lord make judgment? In the works of his hands, he says, the sinner became entangled. 17 [v. 18. 21]. Here a pause song is interspersed. It is due, I believe, to a kind of hidden joy at the separation that is now made, not local, but emotional between sinners and just, like the one that exists between grain and chaff on the threshing floor. Let sinners return to hell, that is, let them fall into its hands when they are punished and become entangled in the snare of deadly delight. All people who forget God: because, by not trying to know God, God handed them over to their reprobate feelings. 18. Because the oblivion of the poor will not be until the end, that is, of the one who now seems to be forgotten, judging that sinners campaign for the happiness of this world and the righteous for sufferings; but he adds: The patience of the poor will not perish eternally. Therefore, those who have already given hand to the cui dolori succumbentes, to pernicitis delectationibus nolunt abscedere. In 7iiuscipula ergo quam occultaverunt, id est in fraudulent consilio, comprehensus est pes eorum, amor scilicet qui per fraudm pervenit ad vanam laetitiam, qua comparatur dolor. 16 [v.17]. Cognoscitur Dominus indicia jaciens. Haec sunt iudicia Del: non ab illa tranquillitate beatitudinis suae, nec a secretis sapientiae, quibus recipiuntur beatae animae, profertur ferrum, aut ignis, aut bestia, aut aliquid tale quo crucientur peccatores. Sed quomodo cruciantur, et quomodo facit Dominus iudicium? In operibus, inquit, manuum suarum comprehensus est peccator. 17 [v.18-21]. Hic interponitur, Canticum diapsalmatis: quasi occulta laetitia, quantum existimare possumus, separationis quae nunc fit, non locis, sed affectionibus animorum, inter peccatores et iustos, sicut granorum a paleis adhuc inarea.

Et sequitur, Convertantur peccatores in infemum; Id est, dentur in manus suas, cum eis parcitur, et illaqueentur delectatione mortifera. Otnnes gentes quae obliviscuntur Deum: quia cum non probaverunt Deum habere in notitia, dedit illos Deus in reprobum sensum (Rom 1,28). 18. Quia non in jinetn oblivio ent pauperis: qui videtur nunc in oblivione esse, cum peccatores felicitate huius saeculi florere existimantur, et iusti laborare; sed patientia, inquit, pauperum non periet in aeter-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

pleasures, now, until they are separated in the last judgment, need patience to endure evils. 19. Arise, Lord, let not man prevail. The coming judgment is implored or demanded; But before it arrives, the people will be judged, he says, in your presence. What he says in your presence or before God is the same as in secret, which was understood by few saints and righteous. Constitute, oh Lord!, a legislator for them. It seems to me that in this the antichrist is represented, of whom the Apostle says: When the man of sin is revealed. Let the nations know that they are men, so that those who do not desire to be delivered by the Son of God and do not claim to belong to the son of man and to be sons of men, that is, new men, may serve man, that is, the old sinful man, because they are men.
(In the Hebrew text it is Psalm 10. It does not have a title. The LXX join it to 9)

20 [v. 1-3]. And since it is believed that he (the antichrist) will reach the height of vainglory and will be allowed to execute in all men and in the saints of God so many things that for this reason, without a doubt, many weak people will judge that God neglects human things, interspersing, then, the pause in the song adds as the voice of those who groan and ask why the judgment is deferred: What, O Lord, have you left yourself to? 31. The poor man gave himself to you. This is why he is poor, that is, because he despised all the temporal goods of this world so that you are his only hope. You will be the protection of the orphan, that is, of him for whom this world has died, his father, by whom he was carnally begotten, and can now say: The world is crucified for me, and I for the world. God becomes the father of all orphans, since the Lord teaches his disciples to become orphans when he tells them: Do not call anyone on earth your father. He himself gave an example of this before everyone, saying: Who is my mother or who are my brothers? From this certain evil heretics try to affirm that he had no mother, and they do not see that, if they pay attention to these words, we will deduce that his disciples did not have parents either, because in the same way that he said: Who is my mother?, he also said to the disciples: Do not call anyone your father on earth.

33 [v. 17]. The Lord heard the desire of the poor: that desire in which they burned when they longed for the day of the Lord among the anguish and tribulations of this world. Your ear heard the disposition of his heart. This is the disposition of the heart of which is sung in another psalm: My heart is prepared, O God! My heart is prepared. Of this disposition of the heart the Apostle says: 5 / We hope for what we do not see, we wait patiently. Commonly we must understand by the ear of God not a corporeal member, but the power with which he hears; and thus it is convenient to understand, so as not to repeat it frequently, that of any kind of members that are spoken of when referring to God, which in us are visible and corporeal, in God they are nothing more than the power to act. It is not licit to think that what the Lord God hears is corporeal, since he does not hear the sound of the voice, but rather the disposition of the heart.

To be placed above them will be the man of whom it is now written: So that from now on man may not seek to exalt himself on the earth, that is, when the Son of Man comes to judge in favor of the orphan, who stripped himself of the old man and, therefore, in this way came as it were to exalt the Father. 35. Then, after the hidden things of the Son, about which many things were said in this psalm, will come the obvious things, of which few were recorded at the end of the same psalm. The psalm was titled after most of the things it contains. The day of the Lord's coming can also rightly be counted among the hidden things of the Son, although the future presentation of the Lord itself must be manifest. About that day it was said that no one knows, not the angels, not the virtues, not the Son of Man. What is more hidden than what was said to be hidden from the judge himself, not in terms of knowing it, but in terms of manifesting it? If anyone does not want to understand that what is being spoken of is the Son of God when we say "about the hidden things of the Son," but rather the son of David himself, to whose name the entire Psalter is attributed, since they are called psalms of David, listen to those words in which it is said to the Lord: Have mercy on us, Son of David; and so also in this way understand here the same Lord Christ, for whose hidden things this psalm was titled. It is also said by the angel: God will give him the throne of his father David. This understanding is not opposed by that sentence by which the Lord asked the Jews: If Christ is the Son of David, Sed etiam ille qui eodem loco intelligitur poní super eos, homo erit, de quo nunc dicitur, Uí non apponat ultra magnificare se homo super terram: cum venent scilicet Filius hominis iudicare pupillo, qui se exuit veterera hominem, atque hoc modo tanquam extulit Patrem. 3">. How does the Lord call him in spirit, saying: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet? This was said to the ignorant, who, although they were waiting for the coming Christ, nevertheless were waiting for him as a man, but not as the Virtue and Wisdom of God. Then there Christ teaches us the true and sincere faith, that is, that he is Lord of King David because he is the Word in the Beginning, God in God, by whom all things were made, and also a son, because he was born of the lineage of David according to the flesh. It does not say: Christ is not the son of David, but if you already know that he is his son, learn how he is also his Lord, and if you know that Christ, because he is the son of man, is the son of David, know that Christ is the Son of God, since he is Lord of David.
TRUST OF JUST IN HIM

1 [v. 1. 2 }. This title needs no new exposition, as there has been quite a bit of talk about what it means for the end. Let us look at the same text of the psalm, which seems to me to be sung against the heretics, who, presenting and exaggerating the sins of many who belong to the Church, as if all or almost all heretics were just, strive in order to remove us Domino meo, Sede ad dexteram meam, doñee ponam mimicos tuos sub pedibus tuis (Mt 22,44). Dictum est enim imperitis, qui quamvis venturum Christum sperarent, secundum hominem tamen eum exspectarent, non secundum quod Virtus et Sapientia Dei est. Docet ergo ibi fidem verissimam et sincerissimam, ut et Dominus sit regis David, secundum quod est Verbum in principle, Deus apud Deum, per quod facta sunt omnia (lo 1,1); et filius, secundum quod factus est ei ex semine David secundum carnem (Rom 1:3). Non enim dicit, Non est filius David Christus; sed, Si iam tenetis quod filius sit éius, discite quomodo sit Dominus eius; nec teneatis in Christo quod filius hominis est, ita enim filius David est; et relinquatis quod Filius Dei est, ita enim Dominus eius est. and tear us from the breasts of the only true mother Church, affirming that Christ is with them, and they admonish us with pity and utmost diligence that we pass over to Christ by passing to them, who lie when they say that they have him. It must be noted that Christ in the prophecy is metaphorically implied with various names, and among them with that of mountain. Therefore, we must respond and say to these: I trust in the Lord; Why do you say to my soul: Like a bird it transmigrates to the mountains? I have only one mountain in which I trust; Why do you say that it happens to you, as if there were many Christs? Or if you, regarding pride, say that you are mountains, then it is fitting that it be a bird endowed with the wings of the virtues and precepts of God; But these same ones prevent us from flying to these mountains and placing hope in arrogant men. I have a house to rest in, because I trust in the Lord, since the bird found a home for itself, and the Lord became a refuge for the poor. Then let us say with complete certainty, so as not to lose Christ if we look for him in the heretics: I trust in the Lord; Why do you say to my soul: Like a bird it transmigrates to the mountains? 2 [v. 3 }. For behold, the sinners have drawn the bow, prepared their arrows in the quiver, in order to shoot the upright in heart in the dark moon. These are the threats of those who command us to go over to them, as from sinners to righteous. Behold, they say, the sinners bent the bow. I believe in Scripture, which, carnally interpreted by them, serves to launch poisonous sentences from there. They prepared saequasi pie studioseque admonentes, ut ad eos transendo transmigremus ad Christum, quem se habere mentiuntur. Notum est autem Christum in prophetia, cum multis nominibus allegorice insinuaretur, etiam montem appellatum. Respondendum est itaque istis, et digandum: In Domino confido, quomodo dicitis anitnae meae: Transmigra in montes sicut passer? unum montem teneo in quo confido, quomodo dicitis ut ad vos transeam, tanquam multi sint Christi? Aut si vos montes esse dicitis per superbiam, oportet quidem esse passerem pennatum virtutibus et praeceptis Dei; sed ea ipsa prohibent fly in these mountains, et in superbis hominibus spem collocare. Habeo domum ubi requiescam, quia in Domino confido: nam et passer invenit sibi domum (Ps 83,4), et factus est Dominus refugium pauperi (Ps 9,10).

Dicamus ergo tota fiducia, ne dum Christum apud haereticos quaerimus, amittamus: In Domino confido; quomodo dicitis animae meae: Transmigra in montes sicut passer? 2 [v.3]. Quoniam ecce peccatores intenderunt arcum, paraverunt saginas suas in pharetra, ut sagittent in obscura luna rectos corde. Terrores isti sunt comminantium nobis de peccatoribus, ut ad se tanquam ad iustos transeamus. Ecce, inquiunt, peccatores intenderunt arcum: credo, Scripturas, quas illi carnaliter interpreting, venenatas inde sententias emittunt. Paraverunt sagittas suas in pharetra: eadem verba §cilicet, quae Scriptu-

They were in the quiver, that is, they prepared in the secret of the heart the very words that are to be fired based on the authority of Scripture. To shoot the upright in heart with arrows in the dark moon, so that, perceiving that they cannot be discovered because the light of the Church has been darkened due to the multitude of impious and carnal people, they corrupt good customs with bad colloquium; but against all these threats it must be said: I trust in the Lord. 3. I remember having promised to explain in this psalm how the moon conveniently represents the Church. Two are the most probable opinions about the moon. Which is the true one of them? I think that man will hardly or never be able to know it. When it is asked where it comes from having light, some say that it has its own, but that only half of its sphere shines and that the other half is dark; but, as it moves on itself in its orbit, the same part that shines little by little turns towards the earth so that it can be seen by us, and therefore first appears as horned. If you build a little sphere with half a white part and half a black part and place the black part before your eyes, you will not see anything of the white part; but if you start to turn the white part towards your eyes and do it slowly, you will first see white horns; then little by little it grows until the entire white part is presented to the eyes and the blackness of the other part is completely no longer visible. If you continue turning it slowly again, the blackness begins to appear and the whiteness diminishes, until rarum auctoritate iaculaturi sunt appears again, in cordis occulto paraverunt. Ut sagittent in obscura luna rectos corde: ut cum senserint, Ecclesiae lumine propter multitudinem imperitorum et carnalium obscurato, non se posse convinci, corrumpant bonds mores colloquiis malis (1 Cor 15,33). Be contra omnes istos terrors digandum est: ln Domino confido. 3. Luna vero quam congruenter significet Ecclesiam, memini me promisisse in hoc psalmo consideraturum. Duae sunt de luna probable opinions: harum autem quae vera sit, aut non omnino, aut difficillime arbitrar posse hominem scire.

Cum enim quaeritur unde lumen habeat, alii dicunt suum habere, sed globum eius dimidium luzre, dirmdium autem obscurum esse; dum autem movetur in circulo suo, eamdem partem qua luzet, paulatim ad terras convertedí, ut videri a nobis possit, et ideo prius quasi corniculatam apparere. Nam et si facías pilam ex dimidia parte candidam, et ex dimidia obscuram; si eam partem quae obscura est ante oculos habeas, nihil candoris vides, et cum coeperis illam candidam partem ad oculos convertere, si paulatim facías, primo cornua candoris videbis, deinde paulatim crescit, doñee tota pars candens opponatur oculis, et nihil obscurae alterius partís videatur: quod si perseveres adhuc paulatim convertere, incipit obscuritas apparere, et candor minui, doñee iterum ad cornua redeat, et desserto totus ab oculis avertatur, ac rursus obscura illa pars

with horns, and finally the whole thing is hidden from the eyes, only the dark part being able to be seen again. This, they say, happens when the light of the moon is seen to grow until the fifteenth date of the moon; then it decreases to the thirtieth, and appears again with horns until the light completely disappears from it. According to this opinion, the moon allegorically symbolizes the Church, because the Church shines as regards its spiritual part and is dark as regards its carnal part. Sometimes the spiritual part appears to men in good works, other times it is hidden in the conscience, and is only known by God when it is only shown in the body to men, as happens when we pray inside the heart and appear as if we were doing nothing, that is, when we execute what we are ordered: to have our hearts not on the earth, but on high towards the Lord. Others say that the moon does not have its own light, but receives it from the sun, but that, when it is next to it, it has in front of us the part that is not illuminated, and that is why no light can be seen in it, but when it begins to separate from it it is illuminated by the part that faces the earth, and necessarily begins with horns until it sets in front of the sun on the fifteenth moon; then, as the sun sets, it appears, so that whoever has observed the setting of the sun, when it begins to disappear, turning his gaze to the east, will see the moon rise; From here, when you begin to approach it from the other side, you will observe that the other unilluminated part begins to return towards us until the horns begin again, and from here it disappears completely, because then the part that is illuminated looks up towards the sky, and towards the earth that which cannot ilusola possit videri: quod fieri dicunt, cura lumen lunae videtur crescere usque ad quintamdecimam lunam, et rursus usque ad tricesimam minui, et rediré ad cornua, doñee penitus nihil in ea lucís appareat.

Secundum hanc opinionem luna in allegoria significat Ecclesiam, quod ex parte spirituali luzet Ecelesia, ex parte autem carnali obscura est: et aliquando spiritualis pars in bonis operibus apparet hominibus; aliquando autem in conscientia latet, ac Deo tantummodonota est, cum solo corpore apparet hominibus; sicut contingit, cum oramus in corde, et quasi nihil agere videmur, dum non ad terram, sed sursum corda habere iubemur ad Dominum. Alli autem dicunt non habere lunam lumen proprium, sed a solé illustrari; sed quando cum illo est, eam partem ad nos habere qua non illustratur, et ideo nihil in ea lucís videri; cum autem incipit ab illo recedere, illustrari ab ea etiam parte quam habet ad terram, et necessario incipere a cornibus, doñee fiat quintadecima contra solem; tune enim sole occidente oritur, ut quisquís occidente solem observaverit, cum eum coeperit non videre, conversus ad Orientem, lunam surgere videat; arco inde ex alia parte cum ei coeperit propinquare, illam partem ad nos convertere, qua non illustratur, doñee ad cornua redeat atque inde omnino non appareat; quia tune pars illa quae illustratur, sursum est ad caelum, ad terram autem illa quam radiare sol

undermine the sun Therefore, according to this sentence, the moon also represents the Church, because it does not have its own light, but receives it from the only begotten Son of God, who in many places in Scripture is allegorically called the sun. Some heretics, neither knowing nor being able to distinguish this sun, try to direct the feelings of the simple to the corporeal and visible sun, whose light is common to the flesh of man and to that of flies, and turn away the thoughts of many, who, not being able to contemplate with their minds the inner light of truth, are not content with the simple Catholic faith, which is for infants the only salvation and through whose only milk one reaches with a certain strength the firmness of more solid food. Therefore, whichever of these two opinions is true, the moon is conveniently taken in an allegorical sense by the Church. If it is not pleasant to exercise the mind in these dark things and rather painful than fruitful, or there is no time, or the mind cannot discuss it, it is enough to contemplate the moon with vulgar eyes and not look for embarrassing reasons, but to perceive with everyone its increase, its fullness and its decrease. Which, if it is renewed because it decays, also reveals to the same ignorant multitude the symbolism of the Church, in which the resurrection of the dead is represented. 4. The moon is dark in many ways, because it can be said that the moon is dark when the monthly race ends, when its radiance is interfered with by non potest. Quem nescientes et cerneré non valentes haeretici quidam, ad istum solem corporeum et visibilem, quod commune lumen est carnis hominum atque muscarum, sensus simplicium conantur avertere, et nonnullorum avertunt, qui quamdiu non possunt interiorem lucem veritatis mente contueri, simplici fide catholica contenti esse nolunt, quae una parvulis salus est, et quo uno lacte ad firmitatem solídioris cibi certain robore pervenitur.

Quae si propterea deficit ut renovetur, etiam ipsi imperitae multitudini demonstrat Ecclesiae figuram, in qua creditur resurrectio mortuorum. 4. Deinde quaerendum est quid in hoc psalmo accipiatur obscura luna, in qua peccatores sagittare paraverunt rectos corde. the sky is cloudy and when it is not full. The fact that they wanted to shoot the upright in heart with arrows in the dark moon can be understood from the persecutors of the martyrs. The moon could not be seen clearly, that is, the Church: already in its beginnings, because it had not yet shone in a large part of the earth nor had it overcome the darkness of gentile superstitions; now when the earth is covered as with fog by the language of blasphemers and slanderers of the Christian name; Also due to the death of the martyrs themselves and so much outpouring of blood, since due to this despondency and darkness with which the moon appeared to show its bloody face, the weak turned away from the Christian name, in the midst of whose terror the sinners launched fallacious and sacrilegious words to also pervert the upright in heart. Therefore I trust in the Lord, and I do not listen to those who say to my soul: Fly like a bird to the mountains. For behold, the sinners prepared the bow to shoot the upright in heart in the dark moon. Or if the moon is now dark for them too, because they want to consider the Catholic Church as uncertain and try to blame it for the sins of carnal men, which contains not a few, priest moon.

Potest ergo et de persecutoribus martyrum inteiligi, quod sagittare voluerint in obscura luna rectos corde: sive adhuc in Ecclesiae novitate, quia nondum terris maior effulserat, et gentilium superstitionum tenebras vicerat: sive linguis blasphemorum et chrjstianum nomen male diffamantium, quasi nebulis cum terra obtegeretur, videri perspicua luna non poterat, id est Ecclesia: sive ipsorum martyrum caedibus et tanta effusione sanguinis, tanquam illo defectu et obscuratione qua cruentam faciem luna videtur ostendere, a nomine christiano deterrebantur infirmi; in quo terrore verba dolosa et sacrilega iaculabantur peccatores, ut etiam rectos corde perverterent. Potest et de his peccatoribus inteiligi, quos Ecclesia continet, quod tune inventa occasione huius lunae obscurae, tumba commiserint, quae nobis opprobria nunc obiiciuntur ab haereticis, cum eorum auctores ea facisse dicantur. Sed quoquo modo se habeat quod in obscura luna factum est, nunc catholico nomine toto orbe diffuso atque celebrato, quid mihi est incognitis disturb? What does it matter to him who rightly says: I trust in the Lord? By this expression each one manifests that he is wheat and patiently holds the straws until the time of the fork. 5. I trust, therefore, in the Lord. Let those be afraid who put their hope in man and who cannot deny that they are of man's party, since they swear by their gray hair, and when asked in conversation to what communion they belong, unless they say to that of man's party, Donato, they cannot be known. Tell what these do when they are reminded of the countless daily sins and crimes of theirs, with which such a society is filled. Can you say: I trust in the Lord? What is it to say: What I give is holy, but put your hope in me? What if you are not holy? At least show me your heart to prove it; but if you cannot, where will I see that you are holy? Perhaps you will tell me that it was written: By their works you will know them. Do I certainly see the marvelous works: the daily violence of the circumcelions, who move from here to there under the command of the bishops and preconjito? Qua voce se quisque et frumentum esse otendit, et usque ad ventilationis tempus paleas tolerabiliter sustinet. 5. In Domino ergo conjido. lili timeant qui confidunt in nomine, et de parte hominis se esse deniale non possunt, per cuius canos iurant: et cum in sermone ab eis quaeritur, cuius communionis sint, nisi de parte illius se esse dicant, non possunt agnosci. bitters, and I see the terrible Israelite batons appear, which the men who currently live see and feel every day. If in the times of Macarius, where your hatred comes from, which many did not see and which now no one sees, any Catholic who witnessed them could say, wanting to be a servant of God: I trust in the Lord, he will also be able to say it now, when he sees in the Church many things that he does not want to happen, whoever feels himself still swimming among those nets full of good and bad fish until he comes to the shore of the sea where the good are separated from the bad. What will these respond if the one whom they baptize says to one of them: Why do you command me to suppose or presume? Because if merit comes from the one who gives and the one who receives, God is the giver, and my conscience is the one who receives; These two things are not uncertain to me, since I know his goodness and my faith. Why do you intervene, about whom I cannot know anything true? Let me say: I trust in the Lord. Because, if I trust you, what reason will I have to trust that you didn't do anything wrong tonight? Finally, if you want me to believe in you, can I believe anything else outside of you? How, then, can I trust that those with whom you communicated yesterday, today you communicate and tomorrow you will communicate have not committed any evil in this triduum? But if neither you nor I are stained by what we do not know, what is the reason for you to rebaptize those who did not know the times of delivery (of the holy books to the Gentiles) and Macarian hatred? What is the reason why you dare to rebaptize and say that Christians who come from Mesopotamia, who have not even remotely heard of the names of Caecilian and Donatus, are not Christians? If the sin that they ignore stains them, it will hold you accountable for everything that was vivunt, quotidie vident et sentiunt. Macariana vero tempora, de quibus invidiam faciunt, et plurimi non viderunt, et nemo nunc videt: et quisquís ea vidit catholicus, potuit dicere, si Dei servus esse vellet, ln Domino conjido; quod et nunc dicit, cummula quae non vult, in Ecclesia videt, qui se intra illa retía plena piscibus bonis et malis (Ib. 13,47) natare adhuc sentit, doñee ad finem maris veniatur, ubi mali segregentur a bonis. commits daily in Donato's part, ignoring it, you, who in vain impute to the Catholics the decrees of the emperors, when in your camps the sticks and private fires are carried out in this way. Let the Catholic say: I trust in the Lord; Why do you say to my soul: Transmigrate like a bird to the mountains? For behold, the sinners have drawn the bow, they have prepared their arrows in their quivers to shoot at the upright in heart in the dark moon; and direct this speech of theirs to the Lord and say: Because they destroyed the things which you perfected. 1. Having asked God to cleanse us from our hidden sins and to forgive his servants from those of others, we must understand what we say so as not to sing with the voice of birds, but with human reason. Because blackbirds, parrots, crows, woodpeckers and birds of this species are also taught by men to pronounce what they do not know. Singing knowing was granted by divine will to the nature of man. We know and we lament that many perverse and lustful people thus sing things worthy of their own ears and hearts; Therefore, they are all the worse because they cannot ignore what they sing. They know that they sing infamies, and yet they sing them with all the more pleasure the more filthy they are, since they believe themselves to be happier the more clumsy they are. We, who learned to sing the divine words in the Church, must at the same time urge that what is written be fulfilled: Blessed are the people who understand the joy of voices. Therefore, dearest ones, what we have sung with harmonious voices we must know and contemplate in the stillness of our hearts. In this song each of us prayed to the Lord and said to God: Purify me, O Lord, from my hidden crimes and forgive your servant from those of others. This appears evident, because in the text of the psalm it is written: And he as a husband came out of his marriage bed. Who is the husband but he to whom that virgin was granted in marriage by the Apostle, the Church, whom with chaste fear the chaste friend of the husband fears that, just as the serpent deceived Eve with his cunning, in the same way the senses of this virgin bride of Christ are also corrupted, in the purity that is in Christ? Then in this Lord and Savior of ours, Jesus Christ, is deposited the excellency and fullness of grace, of which the apostle Saint John says: And we saw his glory, glory as of the Only Begotten Son of the Father, full of grace and truth. This is the glory that the heavens announce; The heavens are the saints, who, elevated above the earth, carry the Lord. Although the glory of Christ was also sung in a certain way by heaven. When did you sing it? When, having been born the Lord himself, the new star that had never been seen before appeared. His echo resounds throughout the earth and his words resonate throughout all the ends of the globe. Who is it about if not the heavens? Whose? Of the apostles. They announce to us the glory of God, deposited in Christ Jesus by grace for the remission of sins. All are justified for nothing by His blood. And since they are justified for nothing, that is why they are justified by grace. There is no grace if it is not free. Since previously we had done nothing good for which we deserved such an excellent gift, with more reason, since the punishment was not imposed gratuitously, the good was given for nothing; nothing was in our possessions other than the deficit for which we had to be condemned. He saved us not by our righteousness, but by his mercy, through the washing of regeneration. This is, I say, the glory of God; this the heavens counted; This, I repeat, is God's glory, not yours. You did nothing good, and yet you received such immense good. Then, if you belong to the glory that the heavens proclaimed, say to the Lord God: O my God, your mercy is ahead of me. It anticipates you; He undoubtedly anticipates you because he found nothing good in you. You anticipated his punishment by becoming arrogant, but he anticipates your punishment by erasing the sin. Just as you were justified from a sinner, made godly from the wicked, and taken into the kingdom from the condemned, say to the Lord your God: Not to us, Lord; not to us, but give glory to your name. Let's say no to us. But who would he give it to if he only focused on us? Let's say, I will repeat, not to us, because, if he did it according to what is owed to us, he would only impose punishments on us. Not to us, but give glory to his name, because he did not deal with us according to our iniquities. By saying repeatedly: Not to us, Lord; not to us, confirm what was said. Not to us, Lord, but give glory to your name. This was known to those heavens that announced the glory of God.

3. And the firmament announces the works of his hands. What was said: The glory of God, is now repeated when saying: The works of your hands. What are the works of his hands? We must not think what some judge: that God with his word made all things, and man, as more excellent than all, he made with his hands. You don't have to think like that; This opinion is weak and is not commonly accepted, since He did all things by the word. Because, given that various works of God are narrated, among which is man, made in his image, nevertheless, they were all done by Him, and without Him nothing was made. What belongs to the hands of God was also said of the heavens: And the heavens are the works of your hands; And lest you think that the holy heavens were consigned there, the psalmist adds: They will perish, you will remain. Therefore not only men, but also the heavens, which will perish, were made by the hands of God, to whom it was said: The heavens are the works of your hands. The same thing was also said about the land: His is the sea and He Himself made it, and His hands formed the dry land, the land. Therefore if he made the heavens and the earth with his hands, he did not only make man with his hands, and if with his word he made the heavens and the earth, then he also made man with the same word. What he does with the word he does with the hand, and what he does with the hand he does with the word. The greatness of God is not divided into human members, who is everywhere and is not confined in any place. What he did with the word he did with wisdom, and what

Inde erat illa vox, membrorum ipsius vox erat, non capitis; sic et hic, Per diem et noctem clamavi, et non exaudies.

Clamavit Paulus ut auferretur ab eo stimulus carnis, et non est exauditus ut auferretur; et dictum est ei: Sufficit tibí gratia mea, nam virtus in infirmitate perficitur (2 Cor 12,9). Ergo non est exauditus; sed non ad insipientiam, sed ad sapientiam: ut intelligat homo medicum esse Deum, et tribulationem medicamentum esse ad salutem, non poenam ad damnationem. Medical sub-
Complaints of the persecuted righteous

treatment, you are burned, slashed, and you scream; But the doctor does not attend to desire, but to health. 5 [v. 4]. And you dwell in the sanctuary, glory of Israel. You dwell in those whom you sanctified, whom you make understand that you do not listen to some for their usefulness, and yet you listen to others for their punishment. In regard to usefulness, Paul was not heard; Looking at the punishment, the devil was heard. He asked permission to tempt Job, and it was granted. The demons asked to enter the swine, and they were heard. The demons were heard and the Apostle was not; but they were for punishment, and the Apostle was not for his health: Because you do not attend to my ignorance. You dwell in the sanctuary, glory of Israel. Why don't you at least listen to your people? Why do I say these things? Always say: Deographies. There is a great crowd here, and those who do not usually come came; I say to everyone that the Christian placed in tribulation is tested if he does not abandon God. When a man does well, he forgets that he is a Christian. A fire was lit in the furnace, and the goldsmith's furnace is a great mystery; there is gold, there is straw; there the fire works inside. That fire is not different and works in a different way; It turns straw into ashes and strips gold of impurity. In those who live with God, without a doubt, in tribulation they become better by being tested like gold. If perhaps the enemy devil asks to test a man and is granted testing him either with some bodily pain, or with some earthly damage, or with the loss of his own, let his heart be fixed on the promento positus ureris, secaris, clamas: non audit medicus ad voluntatem, sed audit ad sanitatem. 5 {v.4]. Tu autem in sancto habitas, laus Israel. Jn illis habitas, quos sanctificasti, et quos facis intelligere quia ad utilitatem quosdam non exaudís, et ad damnationem quosdam exaudís. Ad utilitatem non est exauditus Paulus, ad damnationem exauditus est diabolus. Petitit Iob ad tentandum, et concessum est (Iob 1,11). Daemones petierunt will go in porcos, et exauditi sunt (Mt 8,31). Daemones exaudiuntur, Apostolus non exauditur: sed illi exaudiuntur ad damnationem, Apostolus non exauditur ad salutem: quia non ad insipientiam mihi. Tu autem in sancto habitas, laus Israel. Quare non exaudis et tuos? Quare dico ist? Mementote semper dici, Deoografías.

Et magna est hic multitudo, et qui non solent vinore, venerunt: omnibus dico, quia in tribulatione positus christianus probatur, si non dereliquit Deum suum. Nam quando bene est homini, desertus est sibi christianus. Ignis intrat in fornacem, et fornax aurifícis magni sacramenti res est. Ibi est aurum, ibi est palea, ibi ignis in angusto operatur. Ignis ille non est diversus, et diverse agit: paleam in cinerem vertit, auro sordes tollit. In quibus autem habitat Deus, utique in tribulatione meliores fiunt, tanquam aurum probati. Et si forte petierit inimicus diabolus, et concessum illi fuerit: sive aliquo dolore corporis, sive aliquo damno, sive amissione suorum, fixum cor habeat in illo qui se

based on Him who does not depart from him, for if he seems to turn away his ear from the one who cries, yet he offers his mercy to the one who supplicates. He who made us knows what he must do; He knows it and restores us. The architect who built the house is excellent; If something has been destroyed there, he knows how to repair it. 6 f_v.5j. And listen to what it says: Our fathers waited for you, they waited and you delivered them. We know and read that God delivered many of our fathers who trusted in Him. He brought the people of Israel out of the land of Egypt; He delivered the three young men from the fiery furnace; He freed Daniel from Lion Lake; He freed Susana from slander; They all called on him and were delivered. Did he abandon his Son, so that he did not hear him when he was hanging on the cross? How is it that now the same one who said, Our fathers waited for you and you delivered them, is not delivered? 7 [ v - 7 ] - I am a worm and not a man. Worm and not man. Man is also a worm; but he is a worm and not a man. How is he not a man? Because it is God. But why does he stoop to calling it a worm? Is it because the worm is born from the flesh without copulation, as Christ was born from the Virgin Mary? He is wormy, yet he is not a man. Why is it worm? Because it is mortal, because it was born of the flesh, because it was not born from copulation. Why is he not a man? For in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God. 8. Opprobrium of men and contempt of the plebs. See how much he suffered! To talk about passion and to bring us closer to one another; et si quasi subtrahit aurem ploranti, sed apponit misericordiam deprecanti. Novit quid agat qui nos fecit, novit et reficere nos. Bonus est structor qui aedificavit domum; et si aliquid ibi ceciderit, novit I will compensate. 6 [v.5]. Et vide quid dicat: ln te speraverunt paires nostri: speraverunt, et eruisti eos. Et novimus, et legimus quam multos patres nostros sperantes in se eruit Deus. Eruit ipsum populum Israel de terra Aegypti (Ex 12:51); eruit three ignis path gates (Dan 3); eruit Danielem de lacu leonum (Ib. 14); eruit Susannam of false crimine (Ib. 13). Omnes invokeverunt, et eruti sunt. Numquid defecit ad Filium suum, ut in intersection pendentem non exaudiret? Quare autem ipse non eruitur moda, qui dixit: ln te speraverunt patres nostri, et eruisti eos? 7 [v.7].

Ego autem sum rertnis, et non homo. Vermis, et non bomo: nam est et homo vermis; sed ille, Vermis, et non homo. Unde non homo? Quia Deus. Quare ergo sic se abiecit ut diceret, Vermis? An quia vermis of flesh sine concubitu nascitur, sicut Christus de Mana virgine? Et vermis, et tamen non homo. Quare vermis? Quia mortalis, quia de carne natus, quia sine concubitu natus. Quare non homo? Quia in principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum. 8. Opprobrium hominum et abiectio plebis: videte quanta passus est! Iam ut dicamus passionem, et ad illam maiori gemitu veniamus, vi-

Let us look at her with greater feeling, see first how much she suffered now, and then you will see why. What is the fruit? Behold, our fathers waited and were brought out of the land of Egypt. And, as I said, many others also called, and immediately they were delivered regarding this temporal life, not regarding the eternal one. Job himself, who was handed over to the devil to be tempted at his request, nevertheless recovered his health in this life and received double what he lost. The Lord was scourged, and no one helped him; He was disfigured with saliva, and no one protected him; He was crowned with thorns, and no one protected him; He was crucified, and no one unnailed him; He cries out saying: My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?, and no one helps him. Why this, my brothers? Because? What is the cause of such great suffering? All he suffered is wages. Let's recite and see what it says that passion is salary. First let us investigate what he suffered, then why he suffered it, and see how great enemies of Christ are those who confess that he suffered such great sufferings and do not want the reason to be known. We hear it all in this psalm: what he suffered and why. Hold onto these two things: what and why. Now I will explain what he suffered. Let us not stop, and thus you will better perceive the very words of the psalm. Listen, Christians; See what things the Lord suffers: disgrace from men and contempt from the masses. 9 [v. 8. 9]. Everyone who saw me was wet with me; They grimaced with their lips and shook their heads. He waited on the Lord; let him free; May he save him if he loves him. Why did they speak déte quanta moda patitur, et deinde videte quare! Quis enim fructus? Ecce speraverunt patres nostri, et eruti sunt de terra Aegypti. Et sicut dixi, tam multi invokeverunt, et statim ad tempus, non in future vita, sed continuo liberati sunt. Ipse Iob diabolo petenti concessus est, putrescens vermibus: tamen in hac vita recuperavit salutem, double accepit quae perdiderat (lo 42,10): Dominus autem flagellabatur, et nenio subveniebat; sputis deturpabatur, et nemo subveniebat; colaphis caedebatur, et nemo subveniebat; spinis coronabatur, nemo subveniebat; levabatur in ligno, nemo eruit; clamat, Deus meus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti? non subvenitur (Mt 27). Quare, fratres mei? Quare? what mercedes so much passus is? Omnia ista quae passus est, pretium est.

Cuius rei pretio tanta passus est, recitemus, videamus quae dicat. Primum quaeramus quae passus sit, deinde quae: et videamus quam sint hostes Christi, qui confitentur quia tanta passus est, et tollunt quare. Hinc audiomus totum in isto psalmo, et quae passus sit, et quare. Have this duo, quid et quare. Ipsum mode quid explicem. Non ibi immoremur, et melius ad vos perveniunt ipsa verba Psalmi. Videte quae patitur Dominus, attendite Christiani: Opprobrium hominum et abiectio plebis. 9 [v.8.9]. Omnes qui videbant me, subsannabant me, locuti sunt labiis, et moveunt caput. Speravit in Dominum, eruat eum; salvum fa-

So? Because, having become a man, they said it as against a man. 10 [v. 10]. Because you are the one who took me out of the womb. Would they say such things that in the beginning was the Word and the Word was in God? For the Word, by which all things were made, was not taken out of the womb, but in that the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Why you? You took me out of the womb, oh my God, from my mother's breasts. Before the centuries you are my Father; From my mother's breasts you are my God. 11 [v. l l ]. From the womb I was established in you, that is, so that you alone would be my hope, now as a man, now as weak, now as a Word made flesh. From my mother's womb you are my God: not from you are you my God, because from you you are my Father, but from my mother's womb you are my God. 12 [v. 12]. Do not walk away from me, because the tribulation is near and there is no one to help. See it abandoned; and woe to us if He Himself abandons us!, because there is no one to help. 13 [v. l 3 J. Many bulls surrounded me; Fatted bulls surrounded me: the people and the princes; the people are symbolized in the bulls; the princes, on the fatted bulls. 14 [v. 14]. They opened their mouths against me like a lion that beats and roars. Let us hear his roar in the Gospel: Crucify him, cipher him.

ciat eum, quoniam vult eum: sed quare dicebant ista? Quia homo factus erat, dicebant tanquam in hominem. 10 [v.10]. Quoniam tu es qui extraxisti me de ventre: numquid dkerent talia in illud quod in principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum? Verbum enim illud per quod facta sunt omnia, non extractum est de ventre, nisi quia Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Quoniam tu extraxisti me de ventre: Deus meus, ab uberibus matris meae: nam ante saecula Pater meus, ab uberibus matris meae Deus meus. 11 [v. l l ]. In te iactatus sum ex uterus: id est, ut mihi tu solus esses spes, iam tanquam homo, iam tanquam infírmus, iam Verbum caro factum. De ventre matris meae Deus meus es tu: non de te Deus meus; nam de te Pater meus: sed de ventre matris meae, Deus meus. 12 [v.12]. Ne discedas a me: quoniam tribulatio proxima est, quoniam non est qui aditivet: videte desertum; et vae nobis, si ipse nos deserat, quoniam non est qui adiuvet. 13 [v.13]. Circumdederunt me vituli multi, tauri pingues obsederunt me: populus et principes; populus, vituli multi; princes, tauri pingues. 14 [v.14]. Aperuerunt supev me os suum, sicut leo rapiens et rugiens: audiamus rugitum ipsorum in Gospel, Crucifige, Crucijige! (19.6).
Complaints of the persecuted righteous

15 [v. 15 }. I was poured out like water and all my bones were dislocated. He calls his bones his firm ones. The bones are the foundations of the body. When did you dislocate your bones? When he said to them: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep in the midst of wolves. God persevered his firm ones and poured them out like water. Water, when spilled, either washes or waters. Christ was poured out like water, then the filth was washed away; minds were watered. My heart became like melted wax in my bowels: he calls his womb or bowels the weak that are in his Church. How was his heart made like wax? His heart is his Scripture, that is, his wisdom, which is found in the Scriptures. The Scripture was closed, no one understood it; The Lord was crucified and liquefied like wax, so that all the weak could understand the Scripture. Hence the veil of the temple was torn, since what was hidden was revealed. 16 [v. 16]. My strength dried up like a clay pot. He said magnificently: My name became stronger because of tribulation. For just as the vessel is soft before the fire and strong after passing through it, so the name of the Lord was despised before the passion, but after it it is glorified. And my tongue clung to my jaws: since in us this member only serves to speak, this is why he said that his preachers, that is, his tongue, adhered to his jaws to extract the wisdom of the interiorities of Christ. And you reduced me to the dust of death. 15 [v.15]- Sicut aqua effusus sum, et disperse sunt omnia ossa mea: ossa sua, firmos suos dicit; ossa enim firma sunt in corpore. When dispersit ossa sua? When he said lilis: Ecce ego mitto vos velut agnos in medio luporutn (Mt 10,16; Ix 10,3). Firmos suos dispersit, et sicut aqua effusus est: aqua enim quando effunditur, aut abluit, aut irrigat; effusus est Christus sicut aqua, abluti sunt sordentes, rigatae sunt mentes. Factum est cor meum tanquam cera liquescens, in medio ventris mei: ventrem suum dicit infirmos in Ecclesia sua. Quomodo cor ipsius factum est sicut cera? Cor ipsius Scriptura ipsius, id est, sapientia ipsius quae erat in Scripturis. Clausa enim erat Scriptura; nemo illam intelligebat: crucifixus est Dominus, et liquefacta est sicut cera, ut omnes infirmi intelligerent Scripturam; nam inde et velum templi scissum est, quia quod velabatur revelatum est. 16 [v.16].

Exaruit velut testa virtus mea: magnifice quod dixit, Firmius factum est nomen meum de tribulatione. Quomodo enim testa ante ignem mollis est, post ignem fortis; sic Domini nomen ante passionem contemnebatur, post passionem honorificatur. Et lingua mea adhaesit jaucibus meis: quomodo membrum illud in nobis non valet nisi ad loquendum; sic praedicatores suos, linguam suam, dixit adhaesisse faucibus suis, ut de interioribus eius caperent sapientiam. Et in pulverem mortis deduxisti me.
Ennarrations on the Psalms

17 [v.17]. Because many dogs surrounded me; I was surrounded by a council of ill-intentioned people. Read the Gospel: They pierced my feet and my hands. Then the wounds were made, of which the recalcitrant disciple felt the signs and, doubting, said: Unless I put my fingers into the signs of his wounds, I will not believe. But when the Lord said to him: Come, put your hand in, O unbeliever!, and he put in his hand and exclaimed: My Lord and my God, then the Master said to him: Because you saw me, you believed; blessed are those who do not see and believe. They drilled my feet and my hands. 18 [v.18]. They counted all my bones when it was spread out hanging from the log. He could not better describe the extent of the body on the tree than by saying: They counted all my bones. 19 [v.19]- They themselves looked at me and observed me: they looked and did not understand; They observed and did not see. They directed their eyes to the flesh, but not their thoughts to the Word. They divided my garments among themselves: their garments, that is, their sacraments. Listen, brothers. Their garments, that is, their sacraments, were divided by heresies; but there was a dress that no one divided. And they cast lots for my tunic. There was the tunic, says the evangelist, woven from top to bottom without a seam. Then it came from heaven, from the Father, from the Holy Spirit. What is this robe, if it is not charity, which no one can divide? What is this robe, if it is not unity? Lots are cast on it; no one divides it. The heretics could divide the sacraments, but they did not divide charity 17 [v.17]. Quoniam circumdederunt me canes multi, concilium malignanlium circttmdedit me: etiam videte Evangelium. Foderunt manas meas et pedes meos. Tune facta sunt vulnera, quorum vulnerum scars dubitans discipulus contrectavit, ille qui dixit: Nisi misero digits meos in scars vulnerum eius, non credam. Quando ei dixit, Veni, mitte manum tuam, incredule; et misit manum suam, et clamavit: Dominas meus et Deus meus! Et ille: Quia vidisti me, credidisti; beati qui non vident et credunt (lo 20,25.27.28). Foderunt manas meas et pedes meos. 18 [v.18], Dinumeraverunt omnia ossa mea: quando pendens extentus erat in ligno. Non potuit melius described extensio corporis in ligno, quam ut diceret: Dinumeraverunt omnia ossa mea. 19 [v.19]. lpsi vero consideraverunt, et conspexerunt? ne: consideraverunt, et non intellexerunt; conspexerunt, et non viderunt. Usque ad carnem oculos, non usque ad Verbum cor habuerunt.

Divisorunt sibi ropa mea: ropa sua, sacramenta ipsius. Attend, brothers. Vestimenta ipsius, sacramenta ipsius potuerunt dividí per haereses: sed erat ibi vestimentum quod nemo divisit. And super vestimentum meum miserunt sortem. Erat ibi tunic, dicit evangelista, desuper texta (lo 19,23). Ergo de cáelo, ergo a Patre, ergo a Spiritu sancto. Quae est ista tunic, nisi charitas, quam nemo potest dividere? What is this tunic, don't you imitate it? In ipsam sors mittitur, nemo illam dividit. sacramenta sibi
Complaints of the persecuted righteous

They divided. And because they could not divide it, they separated; then she remains whole. Luck for some. Whoever owns it is safe. No one moves it from the Catholic Church, and if anyone begins to possess it outside, it is put inside like the olive branch was put into the ark by the dove. 20 [v.20]. And you, oh Lord, do not take your help away from me. And it came to pass that after three days he rose again. Come to my defense. 21 [v.21]. And deliver my soul from the sword, that is, from death. The jramea is a sword, and by the sword he wanted to imply death. And from the dog's paw to my only one: to my soul, to my only one, that is, to the head and the body. He calls the Church unique, and frees her from the paw, that is, from the power of the dog. Who are the dogs? Those who bark out of canine habit and don't know to whom. Nothing is done to them, and they bark. What do you do to the dog when passing by on the street?; and yet he barks. Those who bark blindly, without thinking against whom or in favor of whom, are certainly dogs. 22 [v.22]. Save me from the lion's mouth: you already know who the lion is that roars and prowls around looking for someone to devour. And from the horns of unicorns to my humility: he calls the proud unicorns, and therefore adds to my humility. 23 [v.23]. You heard what he suffered and what he prayed to be free from them. Let us now see why he suffered. Now see, brothers, why he who does not belong to the haeretici dividere potuerunt, charitatem non diviserunt is not a Christian. Et quia dividere non potuerunt, recesserunt: illa autem manet integra. Sorte obvenit quibusdam: qui habet hanc, securus est; nemo illum movet de Ecclesia catholica, et si foris illam incipiat habere, intromittitur, quomodo ramus olivae a columba (Gen 8:11). 20 [v.20]. Tu autem, Domine, ne longe feceris auxilium tuum. Et factum est: post triduum resurrexit. In defense meam aspice. 21 [v.21]. Erue a jramea animam meam: id est a morte; framea enim gladius est, et per gladium mortem intelligi voluit. Et de manu canis unicam meam. Animam meam, unicam meam, caput et corpus: Unicam dixit, Ecclesiam: de manu, id est de potestate canis. Who sunt canes? Qui canino more latrant, nec intelligunt contra quos. Nihil illis fit, et latrant. Quid fecit cani transiens viam suam? Tamen ille latrat. Qui latrant caecis oculis, non discernentes contra quos aut pro quibus, canes sunt. 22 [v.22]. Save me fac de ore leonis: leo rugiens nostis quis sit, circumiens et quaerens quem devoret (1 Petr 5,8).

Et a cornibus unícornium humilitatem meam: unicornes non diceret, nisi superbos; ideo subiecit, humilitatem meam. 23 [v.23]. Audistis quae passus est, et quid oravit, ut eruatur ab istis: attendamus moda quare passus est. Mode iam videte, fratres, qui
Ennarrations on the Psalms

inheritance for which Christ suffered. Ea, let us remember what he suffered: he was mocked, all his bones were dislocated and counted, his clothes divided; Furthermore, lots were cast for his tunic, furious and cruel men surrounded him; We have heard this in the psalm and we read it in the Gospel. Let's see why. Oh Christ, son of God, if you had not wanted, you would not have suffered!: show us the fruit of your passion. He answers, he hears the fruit: I am not silent, but men are deaf. Pay attention, he says, to the fruit for which I suffered all these things: I will announce your name to my brothers. Let's see if he announces the name of God to his brothers in just one place. I'll announce you, right? name my brothers; In the midst of the Church I will praise you. This is how it happens. But let's see what this Church is. Because he said: In the midst of the Church I will praise you. Let us understand that it is the Church for which he suffered. 24 [v. 24]. You who fear the Lord, praise him. Wherever God is feared and praised, there is the Church of Christ. Beware, my brothers, if in these days it is said without cause throughout the earth: "So be it, hallelujah." Is God not feared there? Is God not praised there? Donato introduces himself and says: There is no fear at all; everyone perished. Without reason you say that everyone perished. So only a small part of Africa was saved? Will Christ not say anything to stop these mouths? Will he not say anything to tear out the tongues of those who utter these words? Let's see, lest perhaps we find it. We are still told: In the midst of the Church. It's about ours. Those who fear the Senon est in ea sorte, propter quam passus est Christus, quare christianus est? Ecce, intelligimus quae passus est: dinumerata sunt ossa eius, irrisus est, insignia sunt ropa eius, insuper missa est sors super vestem ipsius, circumdederunt illum furentes et saevientes, et dispersa sunt omnia ossa eius, et hic audimus et in Evangelio legimus. Videomus quare. O Christe Fili Dei, si nolles, non patereris, ostende nobis fructum passionis tuae. Áudi, inquít, fructum: ego non taceo, sed surdi sunt nomines. Audi, inquit, fructum quare passus sum ista omnia. I narrate nomen tuum fratribus meis. Videamus si in parte narrat nomen Dei fratribus suis.

Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis: in medio Ecclesiae cantabo te. Fit hoc mode. Sed videoamus ipsa Ecclesia quae est. Nam dixit: In medio Ecclesiae cantabo te. Ecclesiam videamus, propter quam passus est. 24 [v.24]. Qui tirnetis Dominum, laúdate eum: ubicumque timetur Deus et laudatur, ibi est Ecclesia Christi. Videte, fratres mei, si his diebus per totum orbem terrarum sine causa dicitur, Amen et Alleluia. Non ibi timetur Deus? Non ibi laudatur Deus? Exivit Donatus, et ait: Prorsus non timetur, totus mundus periit. Sine causa dicis: Totus mundus periit. Ergo modica pars remansit in Africa? Ergo non dicit aliquid Christus, unde obturet is now? non dicit aliquid, unde eradicet linguas ista dicentium? Videamus, ne forte inveniamus. Adhuc nobis dicitur, In medio Ecclesiae: de Ecclesia nostra dicit. Qui tirnetis Dominum, laúdate eum: videamus si illi laudant Dominum, et intelligamus si de ipsis dicit, et si in

Lord, praise him. Let's see if they praise the Lord and we will understand if he speaks about them and if he is praised in the midst of his Church. How do those who say: Christ lost the entire world praise Christ; The devil took away the whole world and Christ was only the owner of part? But let's see still: cry out louder, speak more clearly; There is nothing to interpret, nothing to doubt. All the lineage of Jacob glorify him. Perhaps they will still say: We are Jacob's offspring. Let's see if they are. 25 [v. 25]. Let all the people of Israel fear him. They will say again: we are the offspring of Israel. Let them say it. Because he did not disdain or despise the supplication of the poor. Of what poor? Not those who boast about themselves. Let's see if those who say: We are just are poor. Christ cries out: The words of my crimes are far from my health. But still say what you want. Nor did he turn his face away from me, and when I called him he heard me. What did you hear him say, for what matter? 26 [v. 26]. Before you be my praise: in God he placed his praise, he taught not to put trust in man. Still say what you want; They have undoubtedly begun to burn, the fire is beginning to approach, there is no one who can escape its heat. But say again: We have placed our praise in Him and have not placed our trust in ourselves, say it again. In the great Church I will confess to you: I already think that here the secret begins to be seen. What, brothers, is the great Church? Is a small part of the world the great Church? The great Church is the entire world. Now, if anyone wants to contradict Christ, tell us, then Ecclesiae ipsorum laudatur. Quomodo laudant Christum, qui dicunt: Perdidit totum orbem terrarum, diabolus illi totum abstulit, et in parte ipse remansit? Sed adhuc videamus, apertius dicat, apertius loquatur: non sit quod interpret, non sit quod suspicari. Universum semen lacob, magnify yourself eum. Forte adhuc dicunt: Nos sumus semen lacob. Si sint ipsi, videoamus. 25 [v.25]. Timeat eum omne semen Israel. Adhuc dicant: We sumus semen Israel; permittamus, dicant. Quoniam non sprevit ñeque despexit precem pauperum: quorum pauperum? Non de se praesumentium. Videamus si pauperes sunt, qui dicunt: Nos sumus iusti. Christus clamat, Longe a salute mea verba deliclorum meorum. Sed adhuc dicant quod volunt. who gave his blood. But what do you say? I gather for Him: W that does not gather with me, says the Lord, scatters. You tear the unit; you claim possession. And why does this one have the name of Christ? Because you placed the title of Christ on it to defend your possession. Isn't this what many do with their home? Some place the title of a potentate on their frontispiece, a false title, to prevent another from invading the house. He wants to be a possessor, and to do so he wants the frontispiece of his house to be protected with a foreign title, so that, having read the title, feared by the authority of the name, anyone who tries to invade it will refrain from invading it. The Donatists did the same thing when they condemned the Maximianists. They appeared before the judges and read the letters of their council (Bagaitano), as if presenting a title to be considered bishops. Then the judge asked: Who is this other bishop who belongs to Donatus' party? The officer or magistrate responded: We only know the Catholic Aurelio. They, fearing the laws, only spoke of a single bishop. Then, to be heard by the judge, they presented the name of Christ and placed the title of Christ in their possession. The Lord is good; may he forgive them; but where you find your title, claim that as your possession. Powerful is His mercy to do this with them, that is, to gather those He finds who have the name of Christ engraved on them. But what does the divine oracle tell him? I reserved for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed their knees before the idol of Baal. He did not say, "You have two or three other men like you," but, "Do not think that you are alone. There are seven thousand others, and you think you are alone! So, as I said at the beginning, I briefly exhort you. Let your fraternal holiness pay attention to what I say and let the mercy of God reside in your hearts, so that it may be understood by you in such a way that it bears fruit and works in you. Listen moment: whoever is still bad does not judge that there is no one good; He who is good does not think that only he is good. Have you understood it? I repeat, look at what I say: everyone who is bad, when he questions his conscience and it tells him that he is bad, does not think that anyone is good; He who is good does not judge that he alone is good, and do not fear being mixed among the bad, because the time will come when he will be separated from there. That is why today we have sung: Don't lose my soul to the wicked and my life to bloodthirsty men. What does it mean do not lose to the wicked? Don't condemn us together. Why do you fear that I will condemn you to the same time with the wicked? I observe that it was said to God: Since you now tolerate us being together, do not cause those whom you tolerate to be together to perish at the same time. This is the idea contained in the entire psalm, which I wish to comment briefly on with your holiness, because it is short.

In another place he clearly says about this judgment of separation: Judge me, Lord, and separate my cause from unholy people. Explain what he meant by saying judge, lest anyone think that the good and the bad would go, without judgment, into eternal fire, since now the good and the bad are entering the Church. Judge me, Lord. Because? For I have walked in my innocence, and waiting on the Lord I will not be moved. What does it mean and waiting on the Lord? He who does not trust in the Lord hesitates among the wicked; From here it happened that the schisms were born. They foundered among the bad, not wanting to remain good among the bad, while they were worse. Oh, if they had been wheat, they would have tolerated the chaff on the threshing floor until the time of the fork! But since they were straw, the wind blowing before the fork itself, dragged the straw from the threshing floor and threw it between the fences or brambles. Certainly the chaff was thrown from there; But is what remained only wheat? Only the chaff is winnowed before the fork, but wheat and straw remain in the heap; All the chaff will be winnowed when the time for the fork arrives. This is what he said: I walked in my innocence and, trusting in the Lord, I will not be moved. If he had trusted in man, perhaps he would have seen the same man who at some time lived badly, not following that good path that the Church learned and teaches, but that taught by the devil; and as my hope was founded on man, when man wavers my hope will falter, and when man falls

If what was given can be taken away, the giver is defeated. Therefore, not even the same things that we have temporarily received can be taken from us by anyone, my brothers, but only He who gave them. The spiritual things he gives he will not take away if you do not abandon them; the carnal and temporal He Himself removes them, because, even if someone else removes them, He removes them having granted him power. We know this and we read it in the book of Job, because not even the devil, who seems to be invested with maximum power in time, can do anything if he is not allowed. He received power over the low and lost the highest and highest. This power is not that of an angry man, but rather the punishment of a condemned man. Therefore not even he has any power if it is not granted to him. In the aforementioned book you can read at length what I commemorated, and in the Gospel the Lord says: Satan has asked tonight to sift you like wheat, and I prayed for you, oh Peter!, meus, quem timebo? Dominus protector vitae meae, a quo trepidabo? Protegitur imperator scutatis, et non timet; protegitur a mortalibus mortalis, et securus est: protegitur mortalis ab immortali, et timebit et trepidaba? 5 [v.3]. Quanta autem fiducia debeat esse in eo qui ista dicit, audite: Si consistant adversum me castra, non timebit cor meum. Castra munita sunt, sed quid munitaius Deo? If exsurgat in me bellum. Quid mihi facit bellum? Potest mihi auferre spem meam? potest mihi auferre quod dat Omnipotens? Sicut non vincitur qui dat, sic non aufertur quod dat. Si auferri potest datum, vincitur dator.

Ergo nec ipsa quae temporaliter accipimus, auferre nobis quisquam potest, fratres mei, nisi solus ille qui dedit. Spiritualia quae donat, non auferet, nisi tu dimiseris: carnalia vero et temporaria ipse aufert; quia et quisquís alius aufert, ipso donor potestatem, aufert. Novimus hoc, et legimus in libro Iob, quia nec ille qui videtur quasi maximam habere potestatem ad tempus diabolus, potest aliquid nisi permissus (lo 1). Accepit potestatem in Ínfima, et amisit maxima et summa. Et non est ista potestas irati, sed poena damnati. Nec ipse ergo potest habere aliquam potestatem, nisi permissus. And in this book you have commemorated, and in the Gospel Dominus he says: Hac nocte postulavit Satan, ut vos cribra-

so that your he does not fail. It is allowed either for our punishment or to test us. Then, since no one can take from us what God gives us, let us only fear God. No matter how much he may roar, no matter how much he may be arrogant against us, let our hearts not fear. 6 [v. 4]. If war arises against me, I will hope in it. In what? One thing, he says, I asked the Lord. He named a certain benefit with the feminine gender, that is, a request. In this way we usually say, for example, in conversation: Duas habes, you have two things, and we do not say duo, two objects; Thus the Scripture used this way of speaking: One thing, it says, I asked of the Lord, and this will I seek. Let's see what Quenada Teme asks for. Great security of heart! Don't you want to fear anything? Ask for this one thing, which is the only thing that is asked by someone who is not afraid or who asks for it so as not to fear anything. One thing, he says, I asked the Lord; I will look for this one. This is done here for those who walk righteously. What is this? That one thing, what is it? May I dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life. This is the only thing. A house is called the one in which we always remain. In this pilgrimage it is called a house, but in the proper sense it should be called a tent; tent of pilgrims and like soldiers fighting against the enemy. When there is a tent in this life, it is evident that there is also an enemy there, because finding many tents gathered together is a sign that there are "conspiratorial" soldiers camped there, and you know that that is what those who are militant are called. Then here is reí sicut triticum, et ego logavi pro te, Petre, ne dejiciat jides tua (Luke 22,31). Permittitur autem aut ad poenam nostram, aut ad probationem. Ergo quia nobis nano potest auferre quod dat Deus, non timeamus nisi Deum: quidquid aliud fremuerit, quidquid aliud superbierit adversus nos, non timeat cor nostrum. 6 [v.4}. Si exsurgat in me bellum, in hac ego sperabo. In what? Unam, inquito, petii to Domino. Feminino generate appellavit quoddam beneficium, tanquam diceret, Unam petitionem. Et quomodo solemus loquentes dicere, verbi gratia, Duas habes; non dicimus Duo, hoc more loquendi uses this Scriptura: Unam, inquit, petii a Domino, hanc requiram. Videoamus quid petit qui nihil timet. Magna securitas cordis. Vultis nihil timere? Hanc unam petite, quam unam petit qui nihil timet, aut quam petit ut nihil timeat?

Unam, inquit, petii i Domino, hanc requiram. Hoc hic agitur ab eis qui bene ambulant. Quid est hoc? What is one? Ut inhabitem in domo Domini omnes dies vitae meae. Haec est una: domus enim ea dicítur ubi semper manebimus. In this peregrinatione dicitur domus, sed proprie tabernaculum appellatur: tabernaculum peregrinantium, et quodammodo militantium, et adversus hostem pugnantium est. Quando ergo tabernaculum est in hac vita, manifestum est quia est et faostis: nam simul habere tabernacula, hoc est esse contubernales; et nostis hoc nomen esse militantium. Ergo hic tabernaculum, ibi domus. Sed et hoc tabernaculum
