the store; there the house. But this tent is also sometimes, through abuse of similarity, called a house; Likewise, the house, according to the same law of abuse, is sometimes called a shop; However, in the proper sense it is a house; this, store. 7. What should we do in that house? Another psalm expressed it clearly, saying: Blessed are those who dwell in your house; They will praise you forever and ever. This one, so to speak, burning with such desire and burning with such love, longs to dwell all the days of his life in the house of the Lord; dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of his life, days without end, but eternal. Here the days are spoken of in the same way as it was said of the years where it was written: And your years will not pass away. Because the days of eternal life are a single day without sunset. Then he said to the Lord: I desired this thing; I asked for one thing; I will look for this one. And as if we were saying to him: And what are you going to do there? What should be your joy there? What is your fun at heart? What pleasures must be those for which joys are enough? You wouldn't stay there if you weren't happy. Where does that happiness come from? We have here various kinds of human happiness, and each one is called unhappy when what he loves is taken away from him. Since men love different things, when it seems to someone that he possesses what he loves, he considers himself happy. But he is truly happy not because he has what he loves, but because he loves what should be loved. For many are more miserable having what they love than if they lacked it. Loving harmful things they are unfortunate; possessing them are entirely interdum per abusionem vicinitatis dicitur domus, et domus aliquando secundum eumdem modum dicitur tabernaculum: proprie tamen illa domus, hoc tabernaculum. 7. Quid autem acturi simus in illa domo, habes evidentor expressisse alium psalmum: Beati qui habitant in domo tua, in saecula aeculorum laudabunt te (Ps 83,5). >Hac iste, si dicendum est, cupiditate ardens, et amore isto aestuans, desiderat omnes dies vitae suae in domo Domini habitare: in domo Domini omnes dies vitae suae, non quasi fíniendos, sed aeternos. Sic enim dicuntur dies, quomodo anni, de quibus dktum est, et anni tui non dejicient (Ps 101,28). Nam dies vitae aeternae unus dies est sine occasu. Hoc ergo dixit ad Dominum, Concupivi hanc, Unam petii, Hanc requiram.

Et quasi díceremus ei, Et quid ibi facturus es? quae ibi delectado tua? quod avocamentum cordis? quae illae deliciae, unde gaudia suppetent? Non enim ibi perdurabis, nisi felix eris. Congratulations on your success? Habemus enim hic congratulates diverse generis humani, et miser quisque dicitur quando illi subtrahitur quod amat. Amant ergo homines diverse res; et quando quisque quod amat habere videtur, felix vocatur. Veré autem felix est, non si id habeat quod amat; sed si id amet quod amandum est. Multi enim miseri magis habendo quod amant, quam carendo: loving enim res noxias miseri, habendo sunt miseriores. Et propitius Deus, cum male amamus, negat quod amamus: iratus autem dat

most unfortunate way. The Lord shows himself favorable when, loving badly, he denies us what we love, and angry, when he grants the lover what he loved badly. The Apostle says this very clearly: The Lord gave them over to the desires of their heart. He gave them what they loved, but condemning. On the contrary, we find a request denied: Therefore three times I prayed to the Lord, says the same Apostle, to remove the thorn of the flesh from me, and he said to me: My grace is sufficient for you, because virtue is perfected in weakness. See how he gave them over to the desires of his heart, and how he denied the apostle Saint Paul what he asked for; To them he gave it to perdition, to this one he denied it to health. When we love what God wants us to love, let us not doubt that he will give it to us. This is the only thing that should be loved: to dwell in the house of the Lord for all the days of our life, 8. Since in these earthly dwellings men recreate themselves with various delights and pleasures, and since each one wants to dwell in that dwelling where he finds nothing that displeases his spirit and finds many things that delight him, and since, if the delightful things are taken away from him, he intends to emigrate to any other place, let us ask as if with curiosity and he will tell us what we have to do and what he has to do in that house that he desires and longs for. Wish and ask the Lord only this: you live in her all the days of her life. I ask you: What are you doing there, what do you want? Hear what: perceive the beauty of the Lord. Here's what I love. See here what I love, this is why I want to dwell in the house of the Lord during all the days of my amanti quod male amat. Habes evidentor dicentem Apostolum: Tradidit tilos Deus in concupiscentiam cordis eorum (Rom 1:24). Dedit ergo quod amarant, sed damnando. Habes rursum negantem petitum: Propter quod ter Dominum rogavi, inquit, ut aujerret eum a me (stimulum videlicet carnis), et dixit mihi: Sufficit tibi gratia mea; nam virtus in infirmitate perjicitur (2 Cor 12,8.9). Ecce illos dedit in concupiscentiam cordis eorum; Paulo apostólo negavit quod oravit: lilis dedit ad damnationem, huic negavit ad sanitatem. Cum autem id amamus quod vult Deus ut amemus, procul dubio daturus est nobis. Haec est illa una, quae debent amari, ut habitemus in domo Domini per omnes dies vitae nostrae. 8.

Et quia in istis terrenis habitationibus, diversis deliciis et voluptatibus homines oblectantur, et unusquisque in ea vult domo habitare, ubi non habeat quod offendat animum, et habeat fine quae delectent; si autem subtrahantur ea quae delectabant, vult homo undecumque migrare: interrogemus quasi curiosius, et dicat iste, quid nos ipsi, quid acturus est in illa domo, ubi cupit et optat, desiderat et hoc unum petit a Domino, habitare m ea omnes dies vitae suae. Quid ibi agis, quaeso te? What is what you want? Audi crux: Ut contempler delectationem Domini. Ecce quod amo, ecce quare voló inhabite in domo Domini per omnes dies vitae meae. Habet ibi magnum spectaculum, delectationem ipsius Domini contem-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

life. There you have a sublime spectacle: contemplating the beauty of God himself. He wants, once his night is over, to adhere to its light. Then the morning will come for us, after the night; for in another place the psalmist says: In the morning I will stand before you and see you. That's why I don't see now, because I fell; then I will stand firm and see you. This voice is human: the man fell, and if he had not fallen, he who would rise would not have been sent. We fell, He descended; He ascends, we are lifted up, because no one ascends except he who descends. He who falls is lifted up; he who goes down, goes up. But let's not despair because He only goes up. He lifts up those who, being fallen, he came down to lift, and that is why we will stand and contemplate and rejoice in the immense beauty. You see that I said this, and you exclaimed from the desire for a certain kind of vision not yet perceived. Let your heart rise above all ordinary things, let your reflection surpass all your sublime thoughts born of the flesh and derived from the senses, by which you forged I know not what phantoms or illusions. Throw away everything from your soul; deny entry to all who approach; know the weakness of your heart, and the moment anything occurs to you that you can think of, say: This is not it; If it were this, it wouldn't have occurred to me. Thus you will desire a singular good. What kind of good? The good of all good, from which all good comes, good for which it is not asked what the same good is. It is said: The man is good, the field is good, the house is good, the animal is good, the tree is good, the body is good, the soul is good; How many times you spoke, you added: well. There is a very simple good: the same good for

plari. Vult finita nocte sua haerere in luz ipsius. Tune enim erit mane nostrum nocte transacta: unde alio loco psalmus dicit: Mane astabo tibi, et contemplabor (Ps 5,5). Mode ideo non contemplor, quia cecidi: tune astabo, et contemplabor. Haec vox humano est. Cecidit enim homo, et non mitteretur qui erigeret, nisi cecidissemus. Nos cecidimus, ille descendit. Ule ascendít, nos levamur: quia nemo ascendit, nisi qui descendit (lo 3,13). Qui ruit, levatur; who descended, ascended. Et non ideo desperemus, quia ille solus ascendit. Levat enim nos, ad quos cadentes descendit: et stabimus, et contemplabimur, et magna delectatione perfruemur. Ecce dixi hoc, et exclamastis desiderio cuiusdam speciei nondum visae. Excedat cor vestrum omnia usitata, et excedat intentio universas cogitationes vestras solemnes ex carne, educías a sensibus carnis, et imaginantes nescio quae phantasmata, Totum ab animo reiicite, quidquid oceurrerit negate: cognoscite infirmitatem cordis vestri, et quia vel oceurrit quod cogitare possetis, dicite: Non est illud; non enim si illud esset, mihi iam oceurrisset. Ita desiderabitis quoddam bonum. What bonus? Omnis boni bonum, unde omne bonum, bonum cui non additur quid sit ipsum bonum. Dicitur enim bonus homo, et bonus ager, et bona domus, et bonum animal, et bona arbor, et bonum Corpus, et bona anima: adiunxisti, quoties dixisti, Bonum. est bonum
Confidence of the righteous in danger

who all things are good; the same good from which all things being good comes; This is the beauty of the Lord; we will contemplate this. See now, brothers, that if we are delighted by these good things that are called good, that if we are delighted by good things that are not good in themselves, and if all changeable things are not good in themselves, what will be the contemplation of the immutable, eternal good that always remains in the same way? As these things that are called good would not delight us in any way unless they were good, so neither would they be good if they were not good for him who is very simply good. 9. This is why I want to dwell, he says, in the house of the Lord all the days of my life. I told you the reason: In order to contemplate the beauty of the Lord. So that I always contemplate it and that no discomfort comes upon me when contemplating it, nor does any suggestion separate me, nor do any power separate me from it, nor any enemy support in contemplation, and, therefore, I may safely enjoy the delights, in the Lord God himself or; what will it do to me? It will protect me. I not only want, he says, to contemplate the beauty of the Lord, but also for his temple to be protected. So that He protects me as His temple, I will become His temple and I will be protected by Him. Is the temple of God like the temples of the simulacra? The idols of the Gentiles are defended by their temples; The Lord our God defends his temple, and so I will be safe. I will contemplate looking after beauty and I will be protected regarding health. To the extent that this contemplation is simplex, ipsum bonum quo cuneta sunt bona, ipsum bonum ex quo cuneta sunt bona: ipsa est delectatio Domini; hanc contemplabimur. Iam videte, fratres, si nos delectant bona ista quae appellantur bona, si nos delectant bona quae non sunt per se bona (omnia enim mutabilia non sunt per se bona), qualis erit contemplatio incommutabilis boni, aeterni, semper eodem moda manentis? Quandoquidem ista quae dicuntur bona, nullo Pacto nos delectarent, nisi essent bona, nec alio Pacto essent bona, nisi ab illo essent qui simpliciter bonus est. 9. Ecce quare habitare flew, inquit, in domo Domini per omnes dies vitae meae. Dixi vobis quare: Ut contempler delectationem Domini.

Ut autem semper contempler, et nulla bother me contingat contemplantem, nulla suggestio avertat, nulla auferat alicuius potentia, nullum inimicum patiar in contemplando, et perfruar deliciis securus, ipso Domino Deo meo, quid fiet mihi? Protect me. Non solum ergo contemplan voló delectationem Domini, ait, sed etiam protegí templum eius. Ut templum suum me protegat, ero templum eius, et protegar ab eo. Numquid tale est templum Dei, qualia templa sunt simulacrorum? Simulacra gentium templis suis proteguntur: Dominus Deus noster templum suum proteget, et securus ero. Contemplabor ad delectationem, et protegar ad salutem. Quam erit illa contemplatio Perfect, tam ista Perfect Protectio; et quam illud perfectum gaudium contemplandi, tam perfection etiam incorruptio sanitatis.
Ennarrations on the Psalms

perfect, in the same will be the protection, and to the extent that the joy of contemplation is perfect, in the same will be the incorruption of health. These two words that he said: contemplate the beauty of the Lord and protect his temple, refer to those other two with which Psalm 1 begins: The Lord is my light and my health, whom shall I fear? It is my light because I will contemplate the beauty of the Lord; It is my health because it protects me, who am its temple. 10 [v. 5 j. Why will he give us this at last? For he hid me in his tabernacle in the day of my troubles. Then I will dwell in the house all the days of my life to contemplate the beauty of the Lord and so that He may protect his temple. What do I rely on to promise myself that I will get there? In that he hid me in his tabernacle in the day of my troubles. Then there will be no bad days, because he protected me in the days of my evils. He who had compassion on me when I was far away, how happy he will make me when placed next to him! Therefore, I was not rash in asking for that one thing. Nor did my heart say to me: What do you ask for or from whom do you claim? But do you dare ask God for anything being a wicked sinner; Do you dare, sinner, to hope that you will attain the contemplation of God, being yourself weak and of an unclean heart? I dare, he says, leaning not on myself, but on the delight of the Lord; not by one's own presumption, but by His grace. Will He who gave such a great gift to the pilgrim, reject him who approaches Him? He hid me in his tabernacle in the day of my troubles. The day of my evils is this life. In one way the wicked have bad days and in another the faithful Quia contemplabor delectationem Domini, illuminatio mea est: quia protet me templum suum, salutaris meus est. 10 [v.5]. Quare autem nobis hoc praestat in finem? Quoniam abscondit me in tabernacle suo, in die malorum meorum. Erit ergo mihi in domo habitatio per omnes dies vitae meae, ad hoc ut contempler delectationem Domini, et protegar templum eius. Ut autem illuc perveniam, unde mihi promised? Quoniam abscondit me in tabernacle suo, in die malorum meorum. Tune non erunt dies malorum meorum, sed vidit me in diebus malorum meorum.

Qui ergo me longe positum misericorditer respexit, secum positum quomodo beabit? Propterea ergo non impudenter unam illam petivi; nec mihi dixit cor meum: Quid petis, aut a quo petis? Audes enim a Deo aliquid petere, peccator inique? audes sperare aliquam contemplationem Dei te habiturum, infirme, immundo corde? Audeo, inquit, non de me, thirst for ipsius delectatione; non de mea praesumptione, thirst for illius pignore. Qui tantum pignus dedit peregrinanti, deseret pervenientem? Quoniam abscondit me in tabernacle suo, in die malorum meorum. Ecce dies malorum nostrorum, vita ista est. Dies malorum aliter habent impii, aliter fideles. Nam etiam credentes, sed adhuc pilgrims

them. We believers, but we are still on a pilgrimage towards God, because while we are in this body we are strangers to the Lord, according to the Apostle said, if we did not have bad days, what is the purpose of the Sunday request deliver us from evil, which supposes that we have bad days? But the bad days endured by those who have not yet believed are very different; although He does not look down on these either. Indeed: Christ died for the wicked. Then the human soul dares to show off and ask for that unique thing; will have it safe; he will surely possess it. If the warp is so loved, the beautiful how it will shine! For he hid me in his tabernacle in the day of my troubles; He sheltered me in the hidden depths of your tabernacle. What is hidden in his tabernacle? What does this mean? Outwardly many divisions are seen in the tabernacle. But it exists as a tabernacle that is called the most secret room, which is the most intimate part of the temple. And which one is this? The place where only the priest entered. Perhaps also the priest himself is the hidden part of the tabernacle of God, since he received the flesh from this tabernacle and became for us the hidden part of the tabernacle, so that all his members, who believe in Him, are his* tabernacle, and He is the hidden part of the tabernacle, for the Apostle says: you died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. 11 [v. 6]. Do you want to know why he says this? The stone is Christ. Hear what follows: He hid me in his tabernacle in the day of my troubles; He sheltered me in the hidden depths of his tabernacle. You asked what was hidden in his store; listen to Domino (Quamdiu enim sumus in hoc corpore, peregrinamur a Domino [2 Cor 5,6], hoc Apostolus dixit), si dies malorum non agunt, unde vox Dominicae orationis, Libera nos a malo (Mt 6,13), si non sumus in diebus malorum? sed longe discretius dies malorum agunt qui adhuc non crediderunt: nec ipsos ille despexit. Etenim Christus pro impiis mortuus est (Rom 5,6). Audeat ergo praesumere anima humano, et unam illam petere; secura habebit, secura possidebit. Tantum dilecta est foeda, pulchra quomodo fulgebit! Quoniam abscondit me in tabernacle suo, in die malorum meorum: protect me in abscondito tabernaclei sui. Quid est absconditum tabernaculi ipsius? What is this? Fine enim quasi membra tabernaculi forinsecus videntur. Et est quasi adytum, quod dicitur penetrale secretum (Hebr 9,3), interius templi.

Et quid est hoc? quod solus sacerdos intrabat. Et forte ipse sacerdos est absconditum tabernaculi Dei. Accepit enim de isto tabernacle carnem, et fecit nobis absconditum tabernaculi: ut tabernaculum eius alia membra ipsius credentes in eum sint, absconditum autem tabernaculi ipse sit. Mortui enim estis, ait Apostolus, et vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo (Col 3,3). 11 [v.6]. An vis nosse quia inde dicit? Petra nempe est Christus (1 Cor 10,4). Audite quid sequitur: Quoniam abscondit me in tabernacle suo, in die malorum meorum: protectxit me in abscondito tabernaculi sui.

What follows: He raised me on a stone. Then in Christ he exalted me. Because you humbled yourself to the dust, he exalted you above the stone. But Christ is above, you are still below. Or and e the following: And now he exalted my head above my enemies. And now, before arriving at that house where I want to live all the days of my life, before I arrive at that contemplation of the Lord, he exalted my head above my enemies. I still endure the enemies of the body of Christ, I have not yet been exalted above my enemies, but my Head is exalted above my enemies. Yami Cabeza, Christ, is in heaven; our enemies can still rage against us; We have not yet been exalted over them, but our Head is already there. Therefore he said, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? He said that He was below in us, but we are also above with Him, because even now He has exalted my head above my enemies. See what endorsement we have, for we by faith, hope and charity are in heaven eternally with our Head, and He Himself by divinity, goodness and unity is with us on earth until the consummation of the world. 12. I went around and sacrificed in his tabernacle a victim of rejoicing. We sacrifice a victim of rejoicing, we sacrifice a victim of joy, a victim of congratulation, a victim of thanksgiving, a victim that cannot be expressed in words. We sacrifice, but where? In his own tabernacle, in the holy Church. What do we sacrifice? The abundant and inexpressible joy, which is not expressed Quaerebas quid sit absconditum tabernaculi, audi quod sequitur: In petra exaltavit me. Ergo in Christo exaltavit me. Quia in pulvere humiliasti you, in petra exaltavit you. Sed Christus sursum est, tu autem adhuc deorsum. Audi sequence: Et nunc exaltavit caput meum super inimicos meos. Et nunc, antequam veniam ad illam domum, ubi voló habitare per omnes dies vitae meae, antequam veniam ad illam contemplationem Domini, Et nunc exaltavit caput meum super inimicos meos. Adhuc patior inimicos corporis Christi, adhuc non sum exaltatus super inimicos; sed caput meum exaltavit super inimicos meos. Iam caput nostrum Christus in cáelo est, adhuc inimici nostri possunt in nos saevire: nondum sumus exaltati super illos; sed caput nostrum iam ibi est.

Unde hoc he said: Saule, Saule, why are you after me? (At 9A)- Se dixit in nobis esse hic deorsum: ergo et nos in illo sumus ibi sursum, quia et nunc exaltavit caput meum super inimicos meos. Ecce quale pignus habemus, unde et nos fide et spe et chántate cum capite nostro sumus in cáelo in aeternum: quia et ipsum divinitate, bonitote, unitate nobiscum est in terra usque in consummationem saeculi (Mt 28,20). 12. Circumivi, et immolavi in ​​tabernacle eius hostiam iubilationis: immolamus hostiam iubilationis, immolamus hostiam laetitiae, hostiam gratulationis, hostiam gratiarum actionis, quae verbis explicai non potest. Immolamus autem. ubi? In ipso tabernacle eius, in sancta Ecclesia. Quid ergo immolamus? Abundantissimum et inenarrabile gaudium, nullis

on my account. If we know from the Holy Scriptures who our enemies are, we will know the meaning of this song; But if human prudence deceives us, so that we do not know who we are fighting against, then already at the very beginning of the psalm we would encounter a question that is impossible to resolve. Whose voice do we believe is the one who praises God, gives thanks and rejoices, saying: I will praise you because you protected me and did not allow my enemies to rejoice on my account? First, let us look at the Lord as a man, since, because he deigned to be a man, he could rightly apply these words to himself, based on the previous prophecy; Because he was a man he was weak, and because he was weak he prayed. What we recently heard when reading the Gospel can also be applied to the Lord as a man, namely: how, separating from his disciples, he headed into the desert, where, following him, they found him praying. Then the disciples who found him said to him: Men are looking for you. He answers them: Let's go preach to other places and villages, because that's why I came. If we pay attention in this passage to the divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ, we will ask: Who prays, to whom and why do they pray? Does God pray? Do you pray like this? What reason does He have to pray, always blessed, always omnipotent, always immutable, eternal and co-eternal to the Father? Considering what through Saint John, as through his cloud, He Himself thundered saying: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God; all things

They were made by Him, and without Him nothing was made. What was made, in Him is life, and the life was the light of men, and the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not know it; Considering, I repeat, everything said up to this point, we find no prayer, no reason to pray, no need, no desire to pray; but as soon after he adds: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, you already have the majesty to whom you pray, you already have the humanity that prays for you. The Apostle also said this even after the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ when he wrote: He who sits at the right hand of God is the one who also intercedes for us. Why do you intercede? Because he deigned to be a mediator. What is it to be a mediator between God and men? He is not a mediator between the Father and men, but between God and men. What is God? The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. What are men? Sinners, wicked, mortals. Between that Trinity and the weakness and iniquity of men, a man who is not wicked, but weak, became mediator, so that, because he was wicked, he would unite you to God, and because he was weak, he would approach you, and in this way a Mediator would exist between man and God, the Word made flesh, that is, the Word made man. Men are called under the name of flesh; hence that: And all flesh will see the salvation of God. It was said all flesh for all men. The apostle Saint Paul also says: We do not fight against flesh and blood, that is, against men, but against the principalities and the powers and the rulers of this world of darkness.

Ubi est ergo ista vox, Exaltabo te, Domine, quoniam suscepisti me, nec iucundasti inimicos meos super? ne? 5. Fortasse non est ista vox Domini nostri Iesu Christi, sed ipsius hominis, sed universae Ecclesiae populi christiani: quia omnis homo in Christo unus homo est, et unitas Christianorum unus homo. Fortasse ipse homo, id est, unitas Christianorum ipsa dicit: Exaltabo te, Domine, quoniam suscepisti me, nec iucundasti inimicos meos super me. Quomodo et hoc verum est de illis? Non sunt comprehensi Apostoli, non sunt caesi, non sunt flagellati, non sunt occisi, non sunt crucifixi, non sunt incensi

alive, were not those whose festivities we celebrate thrown to the beasts? When men performed these things with them, did they not rejoice at their expense? Then how can the Christian people also say: I will praise you, O Lord, because you protected me and did not allow my enemies to rejoice on my account? 6 [v. l]. We will understand this if we first of all understand the title of the psalm. This is how it goes: Psalm of David, for the end, song of the dedication of the house. In this title is contained all the hope and all the secret of the solution of this question. The house that is being built now will be dedicated or consecrated later. Now the house is being built, that is, the Church; later it will be dedicated. At the dedication the glory of the Christian people, which is now hidden, will appear. Let the enemies be angry now, humiliate them, do not everything they want, but everything they are allowed from above; For not everything we have suffered because of our enemies is to be attributed solely to them, but also to God our Lord; The Mediator demonstrated it in himself by allowing men from above to harm us, certainly not giving them from above the will, but the power to harm. Everyone who is perverse has within him the desire to do evil; but the power to do so is not in his power. By wanting to execute him he is already guilty; The power to carry it out is allowed by the hidden disposition of divine Providence; in some for punishment, in others for test and in others for reward. For punishment, how was it permitted to the áAAórpuAoi, that is, to the vivi, non ad bestias pugnaverunt, quorum memorias celebramus? Quando autem ista illis faciebant homines, nonne iucundabantur super eos? Quomodo ergo potest et populus christianus dicere: Exaltabo te, Domine, quoniam suscepisti me, nec iucundasti inimicos meos super me? 6 [v. l]. Intelligemus hoc, si videamus primo titulum Psalmi. Habet enim: In jinem Psalmus Cantici dedicationis domus ipsi David. In hoc titulo est omnis spes, et universum sacramentum dissolvendae huius quaestionis. Dedicabitur domus aliquando, quae moda fabricatur. Mode enim fabricatur domus, id est Ecclesia, post dedicabitur. In dedicatione apparebit gloria populi christiani, quae moda latet. Saeviant modo inimici, humilient, faciant non quidquid volunt, sed quidquid desuper permittuntur. Non enim quidquid passi ab inimicis fuerimus, inimicis deputandum est, et non Domino Deo nostro.

Quando quidem in ipso suo exemplo mediator demonstravit, quando nobis desuper permittit homines nocere, non voluntatem nocendi desuper dari, sed potestatem. Unusquisque enim malus apud se habet voluntatem nocendi: ut autem possit nocere, non habet in potestate. Ut velit, iam reus est: ut possit, oceulta dispensatione providentiae Dei in allium permittitur ad poenam, in allium permittitur ad probationem, in allium permittitur ad coronara. Ad poenam, quomodo permissi sunt áXXó<puAo\, id est alienigenae, capere populum Israel, quia peccaverunt in Deum (Jud 10,7 et 13,1, etc.). Ad probationem autem permissus est dia-
^narratives about the Psalms

foreigners, take the people of Israel, because they sinned against God. For proof, as the devil was permitted to lay his hands on the holy J o b, with which Job was tested and confused the devil. As a reward, how the persecutors were allowed to torture the martyrs. The martyrs were killed, the persecutors thought they had won; these apparently triumphed in public; those were actually crowned secretly. Therefore, he who is allowed to harm, does so by virtue of a hidden disposition of divine Providence; But wanting to harm is typical of man, but he does not always kill who he wants. 7. The same Lord, judge of the living and the dead, standing before the male judge, offering us an ideal of humility and patience, not defeated, but giving an example of fighting to the soldier, removed the swelling of pride from the judge who threatens with haughty pride and says: Don't you know that I have the power to release you or kill you? high. Also Job, and it should be noted that the devil killed his children and took away all his property, what did he say? The Lord gave it to me, the Lord took it from me; As it pleased him it was fulfilled; May his name be blessed. Let the enemy not be emboldened by having done so; I know, he says, who allowed him to do so. Let it be attributed, therefore, to the devil the will to harm, and to God the power to test. Being wounded in his body, all of him in a sore, the wife who was reserved for him approaches, and like Eve, who was the devil's helper, not the husband's comforter, she tempts him, saying among many other reproaches: Praise God and die. This Adam was bolus in Iob (Iob 1,12): probatus est Iob, confusus est diabolus. Ad coronam vero permissi sunt persecutors in martyres: occisi sunt martyres, quasi vicisse se arbitrati sunt persecutors; illi in manifested false triumpharunt, illi in occulto I will see coronati sunt. Ergo in quem permittitur, occultae díspensationis est providentiae Dei: ut autem velit nocere, ipsius hominis est; non enim continuo quem vult occidit. 7.

Itaque ipse Dominus iudex vivorum et mortuorum, stans ante hominem iudicem, praebens nobis humílitatis et patientiae documentum, non victus, sed militi pugnandi exemplum demonstrans, minanti iudici, tumenti superbia, et diceti, Nescis quia potestatem drooling dimittendi et occidendi te? abstulit typhum inflantis, et tanquam reddens exsufflationem qua detumesceret, Non haberes, inquit, in me potestatem, nisi data tibí esset desuper (lo 19,10.11). Et Iob (nempe diabolus occidit filios ipsius, diabolus tulit omnem substantiam ipsius), et ille quid? Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit; sicut Domino placuit ita jactum est, sit nomen Domini benedictum (Iob 1,21). Non triumphet inimicus, quia ipse fecit: Novi ego, inquit, a quo sit permissus; diabolo tribuatur nocendi voluntas, Domino meo probandi potestas. In ipso vulnere corporis accessit uxor relicta, sicut Eva, adiutrix diaboli, non consolatrix mariti; tentat, et dicit Inter fines increpationes: Dic aliquod verbum in Deum, et morete (Ib. 2,9). Et ille Adam

more cautious lying on the dunghill than the other in paradise, since the one in paradise condescended to the wife's advances, being thrown out of paradise, and this other Adam, on the dunghill, rejected his wife, for which he was admitted to paradise. But what did this Adam say when he found himself in the dunghill, internally conceiving immortality and externally emanating worms? What did he say to his wife? You spoke like a foolish woman. If we have received good things from the hands of the Lord, should we not also receive evil things? Furthermore, Job called the damage caused by the devil the hand of the Lord against himself, since he did not consider who hurt him, but rather who allowed it. Even the devil called the very power that he wanted to be given him the hand of the Lord, because, accusing the righteous man, of whom the Lord testified favorably, he said to God: Does Job worship God for nothing? Didn't you protect him, didn't you fence his house and all his property? You blessed the works of his hands; His possessions increased in the land; You gave him so many goods that he adores you for them; But stretch out your hand and touch everything he has, and you will see if he will not curse you to your face. What does it mean to extend your hand, since the devil himself was the one who wanted to extend it? Since he could not extend it, he called the same power that he received from God the hand of God. 8. Then what shall we say, brothers, when the enemies did so many things against the Christians and rejoiced and rejoiced because of them? But when will be the day when they will not rejoice? When these are confounded, the former will rejoice in stercore cautior, quam Adam in paradiso; nam Adam in paradiso consensit mulieri, ut de paradiso emitteretur; Adam in stercore respuit mulierem, ut ad paradisum admitteretur. Quid ergo ille Adam in stercore, parturiens immortalitatem intrinsecus, vermibus fluescens extrinsecus, quid ait mulieri? Tanquam a former insipientibus mulieribus locuta is. Si bona percepimus de manu Domini, mala non sustinebimus? (Ib. 10). Iterum et ille manum Domini dixit in se, quod eum diabolus percusserat: quia non attendebat quis percuteret, sed quis permitteret.

Namque et ipse diabolus eamdem potestatem, quam sibi volebat dari, manum Domini appellavit: nam obiiciens crime iusto viro, cui Dominus perhibebat testimonium, ait Deo: Numquid gratis lob colit Dominum? nonne tu vallasti eum ac domum eius, universamque substantiam eius per circuitum? Operibus manuum eius benedixisti, et possessio eius crevit in terra: tanta bona illi dedisti, propterea te colit; sed mitte manum tuam, et tange omnia quae sunt eius, nisi in jaciem tuam benedixerit tibí (Iob 1,9-11). Quid est, mitte manum tuam, eum ipse vellet mittere? Sed quia ipse non posset mittere manum suam, ipsam potestatem quam accepit a Deo, manum Dei appellavit. 8. Quid ergo, fratres, quia tanta inimici in Christianos fecerunt; et exsultaverunt, et iucundati sunt super eos? Sed when apparebit quia non sunt iucundati? Quando illi confundentur, illi exsultabunt in adventu Do-
narrations about the Psalms

with the coming of the Lord, our God, who comes bringing rewards in his hand: condemnation for the wicked and the kingdom for the righteous; the company of the devil for the perverse and the company of Christ for the faithful. When will this take place? When the righteous are there with great security. I quote the Scripture; Remember the passage from the Book of Wisdom: Then the righteous will stand in great security against those who afflicted them; These will say among themselves, disillusioned and groaning from the anguish of the spirit: What profit did arrogance profit us, and what reward did pride in riches give us? All these things passed like a shadow. And what will they say about the righteous? See how they have been numbered among the children of God and how their inheritance is among the saints. Then the dedication of the house will take place, which is now being manufactured in the midst of tribulations; Then rightly will that people say: I will praise you, O Lord, because you protected me and did not allow my enemies to rejoice on my account. This cry will have reality in the people of God, who are now tortured, troubled with so many trials, with so many setbacks, with so many persecutions, with so much opposition. These tortures of the spirit are not felt in the Church by those who do not progress, because they think that there is peace; But begin to progress and you will see what tribulations you are in, because, when the grass has grown and has borne its fruit, then the tares will also appear: Whoever multiplies knowledge or science, multiplies the pain. Progress and you will see where it exists. The fruit appears and the tares will be seen. The true word of eternal value, which can never be extinguished, is said by the Apostle: all those who want to live piously, amini Dei nostri, cum venerit ferens in manu retributiones, damnationem impiis, regnum iustis; Societatem cum diabolo iniquis, societatem cum Christo fidelibus. Quando ergo hoc ostenderit, quando stabunt iusti in magna constantia (from Scripturis díco, recordamini lectionem de libro Sapientiae: Tune stabunt iusti in magna constantia ad versus eos qui se angustaverunt: illi autem dicet Ínter se poenitentes, et prae anguish spiritus gementes: Quid nobis profuit superbia, et divitiarum iactantia quid contulit nobis? transierunt enim omnia illa tanquam umbra;

Quomodo computati sutit inter jilios Dei, et inter sanctos sors illorum est? [Wis 5,1, etc.]), tune erit dedication domus, quae moda in tribulationibus fabricatur; tune recte dicet populus ille: Exaltabo te, Domine, quoniam suscepisti me, nec iucundasti inimicos meos super me. Vera ergo erit vox ista in populo Dei, qui populus moda angustatur, moda tribulatur, tantis tentationibus, tantis scandalis, tantis insecutionibus, tanta pressure. Haec storm animi non sentit in Ecclesia qui non proficit, putat enim quia pax est: sed incipiat proficere, et tune videbit in qua pressura sit; quia cum crevisset herba, et fructum fecisset, tune apparuerunt et zizania (Mr. 13,26); et qui apponit scientiam, apponit dolorem (Eccle 1,18). Proficiat, et videbit ubi sit: existat fructus, et apparebunt zizania. Vox verídica est per Apostolum, deleri non potest ab initio usque ad finem: Sed et omnes qui vo-

mind in Christ they will be persecuted. And perverse and deceitful men will go from bad to worse, deceiving others and being deceived. For this reason those words of the psalm are also said: Wait for the Lord, work with strength, and let your heart be comforted and wait for the Lord. It was little to have said once, wait for the Lord, if I did not repeat it. So that you don't wait perhaps two, three, four days, and yet see the tortures and tribulations continue, he added, work manfully, and your heart will also be comforted. And since this will happen from the beginning to the end, the sentence that he gave at the beginning he repeated at the end: and wait for the Lord. These things that now afflict you will pass, and the One you wait for will come, and will wipe your sweat, dry your tears, and from now on you will never cry. Now we groan in tribulations, as Job says, for is not human life on earth a continual temptation? 9. However, brothers, before the day of dedication of the house arrives, let us observe that our Head has already been dedicated. The dedication of the house in our Head has already taken place, as a dedication of the foundation or foundation. The head is up; the foundation, below; Perhaps, in order not to speak evil when saying that Christ is the foundation, we will rather say that he is the summit, since he ascended to heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father. However, I judge that I have not been mistaken, for the Apostle says: No one can lay any other foundation apart from the position, which is Christ Jesus; If anyone builds on this foundation gold, silver, precious stones... Those who live well, those who honor and praise lunt, inquit, pie vívete in Christo, persecutionem patiuntur. Maligni autem homines et seductores projiciunt in peius, ipsi errantes et alios in errorem mittentes (2 Tim 3,12.13). Et unde sunt verba illa psalmi, Sustine Dominum, viriliter age, et conjortetur cor tuum, et sustine Dominum? (Ps 26,14). Parum erat semel, Sustine Dominum, nisi repeteret: ne forte sustineret biduo, triduo, quatriduo, et maneret pressura et tribulatio: ideo addidit, viriliter age; addidit, et conjortetur cor tuum. Et quia ab initio usque in finem sic erit, quod habet sententia in capite, hoc habet in fine, et sustine Dominum. Transeunt ista quae te premuní, et veniet quem sustines, et exterget sudorem: siccabit lacrymam, ultra non flebis.

Modo autem gemamus in tribulationibus, sicut dicit Iob, Nonne tentatio est vita humano super terran? (Iob 7,1). 9. Tamen, fratres, antequam veniat dies dedicationis domus, videamus quia iam dedicatum est caput nostrum: iam facta est dedicatio domus in capite, tanquam dedicatio fundamenti. Caput sursum est, fundamentum deorsum: ne forte propterea male dixerimus fundamentum esse Christum; culmen est potius, ascendit in caelum, sedet ad dexteram Patris. Sed puto nos non errasse. Apóstolus enim dixit: Fundamentum enim aliud nemo potest seguiré, praeter id quod positum est, quod est Iesus Christus: si quis autem superaedijicaverit supra jundamentum hoc, aurum, argentum, lapides pretiosos. Qui bene vivunt, qui Deum honorant et laudant, qui patientes
^narratives about the Psalms

To God, those who are patient in tribulations, those who desire the country, these build gold, silver, precious stones. Those who still love worldly things, and are entangled in earthly affairs, and given over to certain affections and ties of the flesh, to their house, to their wives, to their possessions, and yet are such Christians that their heart is not separated from Christ nor do they put anything before Christ, as, in building, nothing is placed before the foundation, these certainly build wood, hay, straw; but the Apostle continues and says: The fire will prove what each one's work is; the fire of tribulation and temptation. This fire tested many martyrs in this world, but in the end it will test the human race. There were martyrs who possessed these earthly things. How many rich people and senators suffered! They built, no doubt, some of them wood, hay, straw with their affections of carnal and worldly cares; But since they had Christ as the foundation on which they built, the hay burned and they themselves remained on the foundation. Thus says the Apostle: If anyone's work remains, he will receive a reward and lose nothing, because what he loved, this he will find. So what did the fire of tribulation do to them? He tried them. If anyone's work remains, he will receive a reward; If anyone's work is burned, he will suffer loss; He, however, will be saved, but as through fire. It is one thing not to be harmed by fire and another to be saved by fire. And why this? Because of the foundation. Do not move the foundation far from the heart. Do not put the foundation on the hay, that is, do not put the hay before the foundation, so that the hay occupies the first sunt in tribulationibus, qui desiderant patriam, ipsi aedificant aurum, argentum, lapides pretiosos: qui autem amant adhuc saecularia, et negotiis terrenis implicad sunt, et dediti sunt vinculis quibusdam et affectibus carnis, domibus suis, coniugibus, possessionibus, et tamen christiani sunt, ita ut cor eorum non recedat a Christo, et nihil praeponant Christo, quomodo in aedificando nihil praeponitur fundament; aedificant quidem ipsi ligna, fenum, stipulam: sed quid secutus est? Uniuscuiusque opus quale sit ignis probabit: ignis tribulationis et temptationis.

Iste ignis multos martyres hic probavit, omne autem genus humanum probat in fine. Inventi sunt martyres qui haberent ista saecularia. Quam multi divites et senatores passi sunt! Aedificabant tamen quídam eorum ligna, fenum, stipulam in affectibus carnalium et saecularium curarum: sed tamen quia Christum fundamentum habebant super quod aedificabant, arsit fenum, et ipsi remanserunt in fundamental. Sic dicit Apostolus: Si cuius opus manserit, mercedem accipiet: et nihil perdet; quia quod amavit, hoc inveniet. Quid ergo illis fecit ignis tribulationis? Probavit eos. Si cuius opus permanserit, mercedem accipiet: si cuius opus arserit, damnum patietur; ipse autem salvus erit, sic tamen quasi per ignem (1 Cor 3:11-15). Sed aliud est igne non laedi, aliud per ignem salvari. Et where? Propter fundamentum. Non recedat ergo de corde fundamentum. Noli super fenum will put fundamentum, hoc est, noli anteponere fenum fundamental, ut fenum habeat primum lo-

place in your heart, and the second, Christ; And if there is no longer anything less than hay there, let Christ occupy the first place there, and the hay the second. 10. Christ is foundation. As I said, our Head was already dedicated or consecrated; It is the foundation. But the foundation is usually below; the head, up. Your holiness understands what I say; perhaps I can clarify it in the name of Christ. The weights are of two kinds. Weight is a certain impulse or impetus for any object that tries to find its place. This is the weight. You hold a stone in your hand, you feel that the weight depresses your hand, because it seeks its own place. Do you want to know what to look for? Separate your hand, and it will fall to the ground and remain there; He reached where he wanted to go, he found his own place. That weight was a spontaneous movement, lifeless, meaningless. There are other things that are heading upward. If you pour water on oil, due to its own weight it goes downwards. It looks for its place, it seeks to be ordered, because the water on the oil would be out of order. Until it gets its order, until it takes its own place, the movement does not disappear. On the contrary, it introduces oil under the water; For example, a glass of oil falls into the water and reaches the bottom of the sea, and there it breaks; then the oil does not tolerate staying underneath. Just as water spilled on oil seeks by its own weight its own place under the oil, so oil spilled under water seeks by its own weight the upper part, that is, its own place. If so, brothers, where do the water and fire go? cum in corde tuo, et secundum Christus: sed si iam non potest nisi esse ibi fenum, vel primum locum ibi habeat Christus, et fenum secundum. 10. Ergo fundamentum est Christus. Quomodo dixi, dedicatum est caput nostrum, ipsum caput est fundamentum. Sed fundamentum deorsum solet esse, caput autem sursum. Intelligat Sanctitas vestra quid dicam, fortassis explicabo in nomine Christi. Pondera gemina sunt. Pondus enim est impetus quidam cuiusque rei, velut conantis ad locum suum: hoc est pondus. Fers lapidem manu, pateris pondus; premit manum tuam, quia locum suum quaerit. Et vis videre quid quaerat? Subtrahe manum, come ad terram, quiescit in terra: peivenit quo tendebat, invenit locum suum.

Pondus ergo illud motus erat quasi spontaneus, sine anima, sine sensu. Sunt alia quae sursum versus petunt locum. Namque si aquam mittas super oleum, pondere suo in ima tendit. Locum enim suum quaerit, ordinari quaerit: quia praeter ordinem est aqua super oleum. Doñee ergo veniat ad ordinem suum, inquietus motus est, doñee teneat locum suum. Contra, oleum funde sub aqua, verbi gratia, quemadmodum si vas olei cadat in aquam, in abyssum, in mare et frangatur, non se patitur oleum subter. Quomodo aqua super oleum missa, pondere ad ima locum suum quaerit: sic oleum subter aquam fusum, pondere ad summa locum suum quaerit. Si ergo ita est, fratres, quo tendit ignis et aqua? Ignis sursum fertur, locum suum quaerit; et aqua locum suum quaerit pondere suo. Lapis ima
Ennarrations on the Psalms

The fire, heading upward, seeks its own place; The water seeks its own by going downwards, due to its own weight. The stone goes to the bottom, the same as the wood, the columns and the earth with which these houses are built. Therefore they belong to that class of things that by their own weight are directed downwards. Therefore, it is evident that they have their foundation below, because by virtue of their own weight they are directed downwards, and if there is not something to support them, everything falls, because everything inclines to the earth. The foundation of things that tend downward is laid down; On the contrary, the Church of God, placed below, tends towards heaven. There is laid our foundation, our Lord Jesus Christ, seated at the right hand of the Father. If your holiness understands that our foundation has already been dedicated, let us briefly hear the psalm and go through it quickly. 11 fv.2]. I will praise him, O Lord, because you protected me and did not allow my enemies to rejoice on my account. What enemies? The Jews. In the dedication of the foundation we understand the dedication of the future house. What is said now regarding the foundation will be said later regarding the entire house. What enemies? The Jews, or rather the devil and his angels, who, confused, walked away after the resurrection of the Lord. The prince of death lamented that death had been defeated. And you did not allow my enemies to rejoice on my account, because I could not be held in hell. 12 [v.3]. Oh Lord, my God! I cried to you and you healed me. The Lord, before the passion, prayed on the mountain and healed him. Who did he heal who was never sick: the Word who is God, the Word petit, et lignum, et columnae, et terra, unde aedificantur istae domus: de illo ergo sunt genere rerum, quae pondere suo deorsum feruntur. Manifestum est ergo ideo deorsum accipere fundamentum, quia pondere suo deorsum versus feruntur; et nisi sit quod sustineat, totum cadit, quia totum ad terram vergit. Rebus ergo ad ima tendentibus in imo ponitur fundamentum: Ecclesia vero Dei in imo posita tendit in caelum. Fundamentum ergo nostrum ibi positum est, Dominus noster Iesus Christus sedens ad dexteram Patris. Si ergo intellexit Sanctitas vestra, quia iam dedicatum est fundamentum nostrum, audiamus breviter Psalmus, et decurramus. 11 [v.2]. Exaltabo te, Domine, quoniam suscepisti me, nec iucundasti inimicos meos super me. What initials? ludaeos?

In dedicatione fundamentí ipsam dedicationem intelligamus domusfuturae. Quod enim dicitur moda ex persona fundamenti, tune dicetur ex persona universae domus. What ergo initials? ludaeos, an potius diabolum et angelos eius, qui confusi discesserunt, postquam Dominus resurrexit? Práepositus mortis doluit victam mortem. Et non iucundasti inimicos meos super me: quia teneri apud inferos non potui. 12 [v.3]. Domine Deus meus, clamavi ad te, et sanasti me: oravit in monte Dominus ante passionem (Mt 26,39); sanavit eum. I want to heal-

what is divinity? No. But since I carried the flesh of death, since I endured your wound, I was going to heal you of your wound. Healed the flesh. When? When resurrected. Listen to the Apostle and contemplate true healing: Death is immersed in victory. Where is your sting, O death? Where is your victory, oh death? Then that exaltation will then be the exaltation of our voice; now is the exaltation of Christ. 13 [v.4]. Oh Lord, you brought my soul out of hell. This needs no exposition. You brought me out from among those who go down to the lake. Who are those who descend to the lake? All sinners submerged in the abyss, for the lake is the abyss of the century. And what is this depth of the century? The abundance of lust and evil. Then those who immerse themselves in sensualities and worldly desires go down to the lake. These persecuted Christ. But what does it say? You rescued me from those who go down to the lake. 14 [v.5}. Sing to the Lord, you his saints. Since your Head has been resurrected, what you see in it, the remaining members expect. Expect, members, what you believed from the Head. There is an old and true proverb that says: "Where the head is, there are the remaining limbs." Christ ascended to heaven, where we will follow him; He did not stay in the abysses; He was resurrected and will no longer die; When we are resurrected, we will not die either. Counting on these promises, sing to the Lord, you his saints, and confess the memory of his holiness. What does vit, qui nunquam aegrotavit, Verbum Deum, Verbum divinitatem mean? Non, sed mortem carnis portabat, vulnus tuum portabat, sanaturus te de vulnere tuo. Sanata is really expensive. When? Cum resurrectexit. Audi Apostolum, vide veram sanitatem: Absorpta est, ait, mors in victoriam. Ubi est, mors, aculeus tuus? ubi est, mors, contentio tua? (1 Cor 15:54). Ergo exaltatio illa nostrae tune erit vocis, Christi moda est exaltatio. 13 [v.4]. Domine, reduxisti ab inferís animam meam. Non opus est ut exponatur. Salvum jecisti me a descendentibus in lacum. Who sunt who descended in lacum? Omnes peccatores mergentes in profundum: lacus est enim profunditas saeculi. Quae est ista profunditas saeculi? Abundantia luxuriae et nequitiae: qui ergo libidinibus sese immergunt et terrenis desideriis, descendunt in lacum. Tales Christum persecuti sunt. Sed quid dicit? Salvum jecisti me a descendentibus in lacum.

14 [v.5], Psallite Domino, sancti eius: quia resurrexit caput vestrum, hoc sperate membra caetera, quod videtis in capite; hoc sperate membra, quod credidistis in capite. Mortalitas. Saccus de capris conficitur et de haedis, et caprae et haedi Inter peccatores ponuntur (Mt 25,32). Dominus de numero nostro saccum solum accepit, non assumpsit meritum sacci. Then it is here and there; there in itself, here in us. What does it say then? So that I sing my glory to you and not be sad. My humility moans before you; my glory will sing to you. 1 [v. l]. Psalm of David for the end, dedicated to the Mediator with a strong hand in persecutions. The word ecstasy that was added to the title means alienation of the mind, which takes place due to dread or some revelation. But in this psalm it mainly appears that the fear emanates from the people of God due to the disturbance due to the persecution of the people and due to the lack or weakness of faith throughout the world. First the Mediator himself speaks, then the people redeemed by his blood give thanks; Finally he speaks for a long time disturbed, which is typical of ecstasy or rapture. Preached shortly after the commemoration of the martyrdom of the apostles From the beginning of the psalm. 1 [v. l]. Let us search, as far as we can, the secrets of this psalm, which we have recently sung, and, therefore, let us offer to your ears and minds a discourse emanating from it. Its title is: Psalm of David, for the end, of ecstasy. What does it mean for the end? We know it if we know Christ, since the Apostle says: The end of the law is Christ, in order to justice, for every believer. End, not that ends, but that perfects. The end can be understood in two ways: either when something is destroyed or when something that was in the beginning is perfected. Therefore for the end it is understood for Christ. 2. Psalm of the ecstasy of David. The Greek word ectasis, as far as it is possible to express it in Latin, can be translated with a single word, saying excessus (exit); the departure or alienation of the mind is often properly called ecstasy. In the alienation or departure of the mind, two things occur: the dread or vehement desire for heavenly things, to the point of making earthly things disappear in a certain way from memory. All the saints had this rapture or alienation, to whom the arcana of God were revealed, which exceed the things of II SERMO I

If the current ecstasy is to be understood as fear, this does not mean that the text of this psalm fails to adapt to the meaning of this word, since it seems that it must speak of the passion, in which dread occurs. But whose fear is it? Perhaps of Christ, since he said the title for the end, and by the end we understand Christ? Or maybe the fear is ours? Can we rightly understand that Christ was afraid when approaching the passion, even though it was because of it that he came into the world? And approaching what was coming, was he afraid to die? If he had only been a man, without being God, he would rather rejoice at his resurrection than fear his death. Thus, then, the one who deigned to take the form of a servant and in it to clothe himself with us, the one who did not disdain to assume us, did not disdain to transfigure us into Him or speak our words, so that we could also speak his. This wonderful commutation took place, and thus the divine exchange took place and the exchange of things for the divine merchant was celebrated in this world, for he came to receive the affronts and give the honors, to empty the pain within himself and give us health, to receive death and give it life. As he was going to die in what he had of us, he feared not in himself, but in us, and that is why he said that his soul was sad until death, and, therefore, so were all of us with him. Contemnebant tune quando esurienti Christo non ibant cibum, quando sitienti non ibant potum, quando nudum non vestiebant, peregrinum non suscipiebant, aegrotantem non visitabant, tune contemnebant: cum coeperint illis ista enumerari, confundentur, et haec confusio in aeternum erit.

And by your justice deliver me and save me, because, if you attend to my justice, you condemn me. By your justice deliver me. God's justice becomes ours when it is given to us. It is called the justice of God so that man does not think that he has justice of himself. Thus says the apostle Saint Paul: To him who believes in him who justifies the wicked, his faith is imputed to righteousness. And what does he who justifies the wicked mean but he who makes the wicked righteous? The Jews, thinking that they could achieve justice by their own strength, stumbled on the stone of stumbling and the stone of scandal and did not know the grace of Christ. They received the law, becoming prisoners, but not free from crime. What does the Apostle finally say about them? I testify that they have zeal for God, but not according to science. What does this mean when he said: The Jews have zeal for God, but not according to science? Listen to their explanation: Because, not knowing God's justice and trying to establish their own, they did not submit to God's justice. Therefore, if they do not have zeal for God according to science, because they ignore the justice of God and want to establish their own, as if by themselves they became righteous, for the same reason they ignored the grace of God, since they did not want to be saved for free. This is what frees me, not me. For your justice deliver me and save me. 1. Incline your ear to me. God did this when he sent us Jesus Christ. He sent us the one who, bending down, wrote with his finger on the ground when the adulterous woman was brought to him so that he could punish her. But He bowed towards the earth, that is, God bowed towards man, to whom it was said: Earth you are and to the earth you will go. But God does not incline his ears toward us as if he were to spatial places or as if he were circumscribed by these particular bodily members. The human imagination does not think anything of this. God is the truth, and the truth is not square, nor round, nor elongated. It is present everywhere if the eye of the heart is open to it. However, God inclines his ear towards us, placing mercy on us. What greater mercy than to give his Only Begotten Son not only to live with us, but also to die for us? Incline your ear to me. 8. Make haste to free me. He is heard in this, because he says hurry. This word was written so that you understand that everything that seems prolonged to us when time slips by is momentary. Well, everything that has an end is not long. El tiemest, illud me eruat quod me iustificat, quod ex impio pium facit, quod ex iniquo iustum, quod ex caeco videntem, quod ex cadente surgentem, quod ex fiente gaudentem. Hoc me liberat, non ego. Everyone falls who does not hope in God, who does not say: In you, Lord, I hope, may I not be confounded forever, and by your justice deliver me and save me. these stones become bread; Worship me and I will give you all the kingdoms you see; throw yourself down, because it is written that (God) will send his angels and they will catch you in their palms so that you do not stain your foot against a stone. My brothers, when I don't know what evil (persecutions) was ordered against the Christians, at the same time this body was treated with extreme cruelty; all of him were violently mistreated; hence it had been said in the psalm: Like a heap of sand I am pushed to fall, and the Lord sustained me. But once those things that were thrown against the whole body to make it fall ceased, the temptation began to take place in parts. For thus is the body of Christ tempted; one Church endures persecution, another does not; He is not a victim of the emperor's fury, but he is a victim of the populace. How many devastations made by the plebs! How many sorrows did the bad Christians cause to the Church, those who, caught in that net, multiplied in such a way that they put the ships in danger of sinking, as in that fishing of the Lord before the diabolus dices: Dic lapidibus istis ut panes fiant. Adora me, et dabo tibi regna ista. Mitte te deorsum, quia scriptum est: Quia Angelis suis mandavit de te, et in manibus tollent te, ne quando ojjendas ad lapidem pedem tuum (Mt 4,4.9.6). Omnis haec ¡Ilécebra cupiditatem tentat. At ubi clausam ianuam invenit cupiditatis in eo qui tentabatur pro nobis, convertit se ad tentandam ianuam timoris, et praeparavit illi passionem. Denique hoc dicit Evangelista: Et consummata temptatione, diabolus recessit ab eo ad tempus (Luke 4,13). What is it, ad tempus? Tanquam rediturus et tentaturus ianuam timoris, quia clausam invenit ianuam cupiditatis. Totum ergo Corpus Christi tentatur usque in finem.

Fratres mei, quando iussum est nescio quid contra Christianos mali, simul impingebatur hoc corpus, totum impingebatur: unde dictum erat in psalmo: Tanquam cumulus arenae impulsus sum ut caderem, et Dominus suscepit me (Ps 117, 13). At ubi finita sunt illa quae totum corpus impingebant ut caderet, coepit tentatio esse per parts. Tentatur corpus Christi, an Ecclesia non patitur persecutionem, alia patitur. Non patitur furorem imperatoris, sed patitur furorem mali populi. Quantae vastationes a plebibus? Quanta mala ingestion sunt Ecclesiae a malis christianis, ab eis qui capti in illo retiaculo, tam multiplicati sunt, ut premerent naves (Le 5,7) in piscatione illa Domini ante passionem? passion! Then there is no shortage of tribulations of temptation. Let no one say to himself: This is not a time of temptation. The song of the grace of God and our justification, without preceding any merit of ours, but anticipating to us the mercy of our Lord God, was recommended in a special way by the Apostle, in the same way that the previous reading made it known to us when reading the psalm, the exposition of which I took it upon myself to make for your charity, according to my short wit. First of all, I commend my weakness to your prayers, so that, as the Apostle says, eloquence may be given to me when I open my mouth. Thus I will speak to you, it will not be dangerous for me to teach you and it will be healthy for you to hear me. The human spirit, finding itself hesitating and fluctuating between the confession of weakness and the audacity of presumption, often shaken from one side to the other, is pushed in such a way that leaning to any side becomes a cliff for it. For if he gives himself completely to his own weakness and yields to this thought, he will say that the mercy of God is so ordered to the end for all sinners, in whatever kind of sins they persist, that if we only believe that God delivers and forgives, none of the faithful wicked will perish. Anyone who, frightened by this thought, if he prides himself with a certain boldness of presumption and trusts in his strength and justice, and determines in his mind to fulfill justice and execute all the things that are commanded in the law, in such a way that he sins in nothing, and judges that it is in his power to lead his life in such a way that he never slips, never fails, never wavers, never becomes dark, and this he attributes to himself and to the power of his will; Even if he fulfills perfectly all these things that appear righteous to human eyes, so that nothing is found in his life that can be criticized by men, nevertheless, God condemns the same presumption and the boasting of pride. Likewise, if, considering and weighing his weakness and presuming the mercy of God, he disdains to purify his life from his own sins and plunges into every abyss of foolishness and crimes, he too falls. Now, as if refuting the Apostle, I will say what we find from Abraham himself in an epistle from another apostle who wanted to correct the men who misunderstood Saint Paul. This other apostle, James, in his epistle recommended the works of Abraham himself, whose faith Saint Paul recommended, against those who did not want to do good by presuming only faith. And yet the apostles do not object. For James says that Abraham offered his son to God to be sacrificed; work known to everyone. This was a great work, but of faith. I praise the building of the work, but I see the foundation of faith; I praise the fruit of good work, but I recognize that it is based on faith. If Abraham had carried out this without paying attention to faith, any kind of work he had carried out would have profited him nothing. On the contrary, if Abraham had had faith in such a way that, when God commanded him to sacrifice his son, he had said within himself: I do not do it, but nevertheless I believe that God saves me even though I despise his commandment, faith without works would have been a dead thing and would remain like a fruitless root, barren and dry. 4. Do not pay too much attention to what man does, but to what he looks at when he acts, where the arm of good government directs. Imagine a man who knows how to expertly direct the ship and who forgot where he was going. What good does it do you to skillfully handle the mainsail? He moves the ship with mastery, he presents the bow to the waves, prevents them from hitting the sides, he has so much arrogance that he takes the ship wherever it is and wherever it wants. Ask him where he is going and he answers: I don't know; or do not say I don't know, but rather answer I am going to such and such a port and do not go to it, but rush into the rocks. Isn't this sailor, who seems to him to be more agile and dexterous, not all the more dangerous in directing the ship, so that by accelerating it he leads it to shipwreck? The same thing happens to him who runs quickly out of the way. Would it not have been better and more bearable for him if that sailor had been a little more inept, so that, steering the helm with more effort and difficulty, he would nevertheless maintain the straight and proper course, and, on the other hand, would it not also be preferable for him to walk along the road more slowly and with less skill than to run with agility off it? Therefore, he who is on the path and walks well on it is excellent, and also he who, followed by hope, even when he falters somewhat, does not err at all or does not stop, but progresses, although slowly. 5. Brethren, Abraham was justified by faith. If works did not precede faith, at least they followed it. Will your faith be barren? If you're not sterile, neither is she. Did you believe anything bad? With the fire of your malice you burned the root of your faith. You, who must act, retain faith. But you will say: The apostle Saint Paul does not say this. How come I don't? The apostle Saint Paul says: Faith that works through charity; and in another place: The fullness of the law is charity; and in another place: The whole law is contained in a single sentence, in that which was written: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. See if he does not want you to act who says: You shall not commit adultery, you shall not covet, and if there is any other commandment, it is recapitulated in this sentence: You shall love your neighbor as yourself; Love does no harm to others, since charity is the fullness of the law. Does charity allow you to do harm to those you love? Maybe you certainly don't do wrong, but you don't do right either. Does charity allow you not to help those you love in whatever way you can? Is it not about charity that prays even for enemies? Will he then abandon his friend who wishes good things for his enemies? Therefore, if faith is found without charity, it is found without works. So that you do not bother thinking about the works of faith, add to it hope and love or charity and do not think about what you do. Love cannot be idle. What thing works wrong in certain men if it is not love? Present me with an idle and idle love. The evils, the adulteries, the crimes, the homicides, all the dishonesties, are they not executed by love? Purify your love. The water that runs to the latrine leads it to the garden. The im-

pulse that manifested addressing the world, channel it to the Artificer of the world. Are you perhaps told not to love anything? No. If you do not love anything, you will be lazy, worthy of being hated, miserable; you will be dead. Love, but think what you love. The love of God and the love of neighbor is called charity; The love of the world and the love of this century is called concupiscence. Restrain lust; charity be excited. The same charity of the one who does good offers him the hope of a good conscience. A good conscience carries with it hope. Just as a bad conscience resolves itself entirely into despair, so a good conscience resolves itself entirely into hope. And in this way we will have the three virtues that the Apostle speaks of: faith, hope and charity. Likewise, in another place he talks about these three, but instead of hope he wrote good conscience, which he says are the end of the mandate. What is the purpose of the commandment? The one with which the precepts are perfected, not the one with which they are destroyed. In one way we say that the food was finished, and in another that the tunic that was being woven was finished. It ends. the food and nothing is left; is destroyed; A tunic is finished and it is perfect. This and that are called end. He did not say here the end of the precept, as if the precepts had ceased to exist, but in the sense that they are carried out and perfected, not that they disappear. He said the end taking into account those three things: Since he wrote the end of the commandment is the charity that comes from a clean heart, a good conscience and an unfeigned faith. To the one who works, that is, to the one who boasts of his works and says that by virtue of them the grace of faith has been granted, the wages are not paid as a grace, but as a debt. And what does this mean if it is not that our reward or wages is called grace? And if it is grace, it is freely given. And what does it mean freely given? Which is obviously free. You did nothing good, and remission of sins is granted to you. You look at your works, and they are all bad. If God repaid what was due for those works, he would undoubtedly condemn, because the wages of sin is death. What is due to evil works if not condemnation? What do the good ones deserve? The kingdom of heaven. You were found in the midst of evil works; If it were given to you as you deserved, you should be punished. And what is done with you? God does not repay you with the penalty due, but grants you the grace that is not owed to you. He owed punishment and granted forgiveness. You begin, therefore, to be in faith through indulgence. Faith, taking hope and love, begins to work well; But, nevertheless, do not yet boast or be arrogant. Remember by whom you were placed on the path; Remember that with a healthy and light foot you erred; Remember that, if you were weakened and remained half-alive on the road, you were loaded onto the donkey and taken to the inn. There is a man to whom the Lord has not imputed sin and there is no deceit in his mouth. The psalm and also the understanding begins. Understanding or understanding is that you know that you should not boast about your works or boast about the iniquity of sin. The title of the psalm is this: Of David, of intelligence. This psalm is called intelligence. The first thing you must recognize is that you know yourself as a sinner. From this intelligence it follows that, when you begin to do good by faith through love, you do not attribute it to your strength, but to the grace of God. Thus there will be no deception in your heart, that is, in your inner mouth, nor will you have some words on your lips and others in your thoughts. You will not be the number of! those Pharisees of whom it was said: You are like whitewashed tombs: on the outside you appear righteous to men, and within you are full of deceit and iniquity. Is he not a liar who pretends to be righteous while being wicked? It is not that Nathanael of whom the Lord said: Behold a true Israelite in whom there is no deceit. Why was there no fraud in Nathanael? When you were, says the Lord, under the fig tree, I saw you. He was under the fig tree, he was subject to the condition of the flesh. If he was subject to the condition of the flesh, because he was subject to the sin of propagation, he was found under that fig tree in which in another psalm it is moaned in this way: Behold, I was conceived in sin. But he who came with grace saw him. What does saw him mean? He felt sorry for him. Therefore he recommends man in such a way without fraud that he recommends his grace in man. When you were under the fig tree, I saw you. What great thing in ore eius dolus. Iam Psalmus incipit, et incipit intellectus. Intellectus ergo vel intelligentia ipsa est, ut noveris nec iactare te owe de meritis tuis, nec praesumere de impunitate peccati. Psalmi enim titulus ita est: Huic David intellectus. Intelligentiae vocatur psalmus iste. Prima ergo intelligentia, ut te noveris peccatorem. Consequens intelligentia est, ut eum ex fide per dilectionem bene coeperis operani, ne hoc viribus tuis, sed gratiae Dei deputaveris. Ita non erit dolus in corde tuo, hoc est in ore interiore tuo; nec aliud in labiis habebis, aliud in cogitatione. Non eris de illis Pharisaeis, de quibus dictum est: Similes estis monumentis dealbatis; a foris quidem apparetis hominibtts iusti, intus autem pleni estis dolo et iniquitate (Mt 23,27).

Qui ergo eum sit iniquus iustum se praetendit, nonne dolosus est? Non ille Nathanael est, de quo Dominus dicit: Ecce veré Israelita in quo dolus non est? Unde autem in illo Nathanaele dolus non erat? Cum esses, inquit, sub arbore fici, vidi te (lo 1,47.48). Sub arbore fici erat, sub conditione carnis erat. pampering within ourselves. Why does he say redeem me? Because we groan within ourselves waiting for the adoption of children, the redemption of our body. This is why he says redeem me, because we still wait, groaning within ourselves, for the redemption of our body. Why do you say my joy? The Apostle himself explains it below: By hope we have been saved, and the hope that is seen is not hope, because what one sees, how can one expect it? If we wait for what we do not see, we wait patiently. If you wait, you're happy. If you wait patiently, you still groan. Patience is not needed where you endure no evil. What is called tolerance, what is called patience, what is called resignation, what is called fortitude of mind, does not occur in prosperous things. Where you are dejected, there is anguish. Therefore if we wait patiently, we still say: Redeem me from the tribulation that surrounded me; but since we have been saved by hope, at the same time we say both things: My joy, redeem me.

1 [v. l]. This psalm advises us to rejoice in the Lord. Its title is: Psalm of David. Let those who belong to the most sacred line of David hear his voice, and recite his words, and rejoice in the Lord. Well, this is how it begins: Rejoice, ye righteous, in the Lord. Let the wicked rejoice in the world, but know that when the world ends, their joy ends. Let the righteous rejoice in the Lord, for as the Lord remains, the joy of the righteous continues. It is advisable to rejoice in the Lord in such a way that we praise Him who alone has nothing that displeases us, since no one possesses such great things that displease the unbelievers. The rule is very brief: God pleases the one who pleases God. Dearest ones, don't take this as an insignificant thing. You see how many dispute against God and how many those who displease his works. Therefore, having said: Rejoice in the Lord, ye righteous, as we cannot rejoice in Him except by praising, therefore we praise Him whom we please the more the more He has pleased us. To the upright, he says, praise is fitting. Who are the righteous? Those who straighten their hearts according to the will of God, and, if they are disturbed by human frailty, are consoled by divine equity, because even if they would like, due to the corruptible heart, some particular thing that for the moment suits the matter of their cause or the present need, when they understand and know that God wants something else, they put the will of the best before their own, that of the Almighty before that of the weak, that of God before that of man. How far God is from man, the will of God differs so much from that of man. Christ, who takes man upon himself, who proposes the law to us, who teaches us to live and gives us to live, also makes known a certain particular will of man in which he personified his and ours, because he is our head, and to him, as you know, we belong as members. contra voluntatem hominum, quia Dominus est, et novit quid faciat, nec tam attendit nostram voluntatem quam utilitatem; illi qui malunt suam voluntatem impleri quam Dei, volunt ad suam voluntatem flectere Deum, non suam corrigere ad Deum. 3. If you are not righteous, you praise God when He is good to you and revile Him when He seems bad to you. What seems bad to you, if it is fair, is not bad. It is fair because it is done by him who cannot execute anything unjustly. You will be a foolish child in your father's house if you love your father when he caresses you and hate him when he punishes you. As if I didn't provide you with the inheritance by caressing you and punishing you! Hear how praise befits the upright, hear the voice of the upright who praises in another psalm: I will bless the Lord in all times; May your praise always be in my mouth. At all times it is the same as always, and I will bless, just as his praise is in my mouth. At all times and always, both in prosperous things and in adverse ones. Because if you praise in prosperous times and do not praise in adverse times, how will you praise at all times, as always? We have heard many similar voices from more than a few. When something favorable happens to them, they rejoice, rejoice, sing and praise God. They are not to be reproved; On the contrary, we should rejoice with them, because many do not even rejoice then. But these who have already begun to praise God because of prosperity, must be instructed so that they know the father who punishes, and so they do not dare to murmur at the hand that corrects, lest, remaining always perverse, they deserve to be disinherited, but having now become righteous, and what is right consists in not displeasing what God has done, they can in adversity praise God and say: The Lord gave, the Lord took it from me; As it pleased him, so it was done; blessed be the name of the Lord.
