It has to take place during our life, the diversity of which is represented by these two instruments. The zither is a concave piece of wood, similar to the tympanum or timpani, that hangs from a mast, on whose mast and box the strings rest so that, when plucked, they resonate; I am not saying this because they are played with a bow, but I said that it is a concave piece of wood on which the strings are placed on top and in a certain way lie down so that, when they are plucked by the bow, they vibrate and due to that concavity, which collects the sound of the vibrations, they become more sonorous. The zither has this wooden concavity at the bottom; the psaltery, at the top. This is the difference. Now we are commanded to confess with the zither and sing with the ten-stringed psaltery. If I am not mistaken, the ten-stringed zither was not mentioned in this or any other psalm. Let our children, the readers, read and consider it better and without less care; However, as far as I can remember, in many places we find the ten-stringed psaltery; The Ten-String Zither I don't think I've ever read it. Remember that the zither has at the bottom where it resonates; the psaltery, at the top. From the lower life, that is, from the earthly life, we have prosperity and adversity, so we praise God in both so that His praise is always in our mouths and we bless God at all times. There is a certain earthly prosperity and adversity; In both cases God must be praised so that we can play the zither. When does earthly prosperity take place? When we are healthy, when all pendente testudine abound, cui ligno chordae innituntur, ut tactae resonent: non plectrum dico quo tanguntur, sed lignum illud dixi concavum cui superiacent, cui quodammodo incumbunt, ut ex illo cum tanguntur tremefactae, et ex illa concavitate sonum concipientes, magis canorae reddantur: hoc ergo lignum cithara in inferiore parte habet, psalterium in superiore. Haec est distinctio. Iubemur autem moda confiten in cithara, et psallere in psalterio decem chordarum. Non dixit in cithara decem chordarum, ñeque in hoc psalmo, ñeque, si non fallor, alicubi. Man only finds himself with power when he receives it from above. How would the devil himself have dared to even take a single sheep from the holy man Joba unless God had first told him: Stretch out your hand, that is, given him permission? He wanted to, but He didn't let him; only when He allowed him, he could; Therefore, it was not this one who could do it, but the One who allowed it. Having, as you have, two things, the soul and the body, for the very reason that in these two things what is called soul is better, your body can by the best become better, because the body is subject to the soul. Therefore your body can be made better by your soul, so that, your soul remaining just, later even your body itself will be immortal. By the illumination of the soul your body will deserve incorruption, so that the restoration of the inferior one can be done with the better one. Scripture said to replace your doubt with confidence; speak, love, wait for sure. Let your words be those of the psalm: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance. cuius est Dominus Deus eorum. Hoc ama, hoc posside, hoc cum vis habebis, hoc gratis habebis. 17. Beata gens cuius est Dominus Deus eorum. Noster Deus! Cuius enim non est Deus? Non plane omnium eodem moda. Noster magis, noster qui vivimus de illo tanquam de pane nostro. Ipse sit haereditas nostra, possessio nostra. An forte tereré dicimus making nobis Deum possessionem, cum sit Dominus, cum sit Creator? Non est ista fearitas: affectus est desiderii, et dulcedo spei. Dicat anima, omnino secura dicat: Deus meus es tu: qui dicit animae nostrae: Salus tua ego sum (Ps 34,3). Dicat, secura dicat: non faciet iniuriam cum hoc dixerit; imo faciet si non dixerit. Arbores volebas habere quibus beatus esses? Audi Scripturam dicentem de sapientia: Lignum vita» est omnibus possidentibus eam. Ecce possessionem nostram dixit esse sapientiam.

Sed ne putes ipsam sapientiam, quia possessionem tuam dixit Scriptura, aliquid esse quod sit te inferius, sequitur et adiungit: Et incumbentibus in eam velut in Dominum, tuta (Prov 3,18). Ecce Dominus tuus factus est tibi quasi baculus: securas homo incumbit, quia ille non suecumbit. Dic ergo securus, possessio tua est, possidentibus eam. Scriptura dixit, implevit fiducia dubitationem tuam: dic securus, ama securus, spera securus. Tua etiam illa verba sint in Psalm, Dominus pars haereditatis meae (Ps 15:5).

18. Then we will be blessed possessing God. How then? Will we possess him and will he not possess us? Listen to Isaiah: Lord, possess us. Then he possesses and is possessed; and all He for us. We possess him and he possesses us because we adore him and he takes care of us. We worship him as Lord God, he takes care of us as his land. No one doubts that we adore him. Who shows us that they care for us? He who says: I am the vine, and you are the branches, and my Father is the farmer. Behold, in this psalm both things are told to us, and both are demonstrated. I already said that we possess him: Blessed is the nation that has God as Lord. Whose inheritance is this? Of Him. Whose? His. Whose inheritance is this? Let's say from whom: from God. This is how it is customary to respond when we ask about some extensive and very pleasant farms and meadows; For example, there is a certain senator who is called by the same or different name as the one who has the possession, and when he tells us that it is his, we say: Lucky man. In the same way, if we ask whose God this is, there are certain blessed people whose God he is, because he is their Lord and God. But God is the owner of these people, not like the senator, who owns the property and is not owned by the property. To be His, we must work; but we possess each other. You heard that the people possess him: Blessed are the people who have God as Lord. Hear that He also possesses it: The people whom He chose 18. Ergo inde beati erimus, Deum possidendo. Quid ergo? Nos possidebimus eum, et ille non nos possidebit? Unde ergo Isaiah: Domine, posside us? (Is 26,13 sec. LXX). Possidet ergo, et possidetur, et totum propter nos. Non enün quomodo, ut nos ex illo beati simus, possidetur a nobis, ita et ille, ut beatus sit, possidet nos. Et possidet, et possidetur, non ob aliud nisi ut nos beati simus. Possidemus eum, et posidet nos; quia colimus eum et colit nos. Colimus eum tanquam Dominum Deum, colit nos tanquam terram suam. Quia colimus eum, nemo dubitat; quia colit nos, quis nobis indicat? Dicamus de Deo, dicamus cuius est. From his prepared room: the one he prepared for himself. He saw us from the apostles, he saw us from the preachers of the truth, he saw us from the angels, whom he sent1. Wildebeest Deus eorum. By the power of his grace, by the work of his mercy, he formed hearts, he modeled our hearts, he formed them one by one, giving us a particular heart without breaking the unity. As all the members have been formed in particular and have a peculiar operation, and yet they live in the unity of the body, and as it happens that the hand does what the eye does not do, and the ear serves what the eye and the hand do not do, and yet they all work in unity, despite the fact that the hand, the eye and the ear do different things, not in opposition to each other; In the same way, in the body of Christ, each man by himself enjoys as a particular member his own gifts, because He who chose the people for Himself as an inheritance formed their hearts one by one. Are they all apostles? Are they all projects? Are they all doctors? Does everyone have the gift of healing? Do they all speak languages? Does everyone interpret? To one is given by the Spirit the gift of wisdom, to another speaks of science, to another faith according to the same Spirit, to another grace of healing. Because?

rise up against God as if he were something in and of himself. This one will not be saved because of his great strength. 24 [v. 17. 18 }. He has a big, strong, vigorous, fast horse; Still, if some danger comes to him, can he immediately deliver him from it? Don't fool yourself; Listen to what follows: Falaz is the horse for health. Did you understand what was said when they said the horse is a fallacy for health? Don't promise your horse health^; If he promises it to you, he's lying. God willing, you will be delivered; If he doesn't want to free you, you will fall from a height, falling off the horse. Do not think that it was said that the horse is fallacious for health, as if (translating equus as just) the just were fallacious for health because the just also lie for health; since it was not written aequus (equal, fair), which is derived from aequitate, equality, justice; but equus (horse), quadruped animal. This is incontestably declared by the Greek codex, which says ippos, horse. The bad donkeys, the men who seek for themselves opportunities to lie, are refuted when the Scripture says: The mouth that lies kills the soul; and also: You will destroy all those who speak lies. So what does the horse mean for health? That the horse lies to you when it promises you health. But does the horse speak to anyone and promise health? When you see a well-formed, spirited horse, endowed with a long stride, all these things promise you about it, such as health; but they deceive, if God does not protect, because the horse is deceitful for health. He figuratively takes as a horse any dignity of this century, any one.

adversus Deum, velut quia est ipse aliquid in se et per se. Non fit isie salvus in multitudine virtutis suae. 24 [v.17.18]. Sed equum habet magnum, fortem, validum, velocem; potest si aliquid ingruerit, I quote illum de periculo liberae? Non fallatur, audit quod sequitur: Mendax equus ad salutem. Intellexistis quid dictum sit: Mendax equus ad salutem? Non tibi promiset equus tuus salutem: si tibi promiserit, mentietur. Si enim Deus voluer.it, liberaberis: si Deus noluerit, cadente equo altius cades. Non ergo putetis dictum, Mendax equus ad salutem, quasi mendax iustus ad salutem, quod velut iusti ad salutem mentiantur. Non est enim scriptum aequus, quod ab aequitate dicitur; sed equus, quadrupes animal. Hoc graecus codex indicat. Et redarguuntur mala iumenta, homines qui sibi quaerunt occasions mendaciorum: cum Scriptura dicat, Os quod mentitur, occidh animam (Wis 1,11); et, Verdes omnes qui loquuntur mendacium (Ps 5,7). Quid est ergo, Mendax equus ad salutem? Mentitur tibi equus quando promittit salutem. Numquid equus alicui loquitur, et promittit salutem? Sed cum tu vides equum bene formatum, bonis viribus, magno cursu praeditum, ista omnia velut promittunt tibi de illo salutem: sed fallunt, si Deus non tuetur, quia Mendax equus ad salutem. Equum accipe etiam imagine quamlibet amplitudinem saeculi huius, quemlibet honorem in quem superbus ascendis: quo altius ingrederis, eo te non tantum celsiorem, sed

I want honor, to which you ascend proudly; The higher you ride, the more falsely you judge yourself not only higher, but safer. You do not know that it will plunge you into even greater starry danger, the higher you were taken. False is the horse for health, and in the opulence of its strength it will not save you. And how will you save yourself? Not for courage, nor for strength, nor for honor, nor for glory, nor for the horse. And then where will I go? Where will I find how to save myself? Do not search for a long time; don't go far. Here are the eyes of the Lord on those who fear him. You see that these are the same ones with which he looked at those he contemplated from his room. See the eyes of the Lord on those who fear him and on those who hope in his mercy. Not by their merits, not by their courage, not by their strength or by their horse, but by the mercy of the Lord are men saved. 25 [ v, 19 J. To free their souls from death. Promises eternal life. But will he abandon this pilgrimage? Pay attention to what follows: And feed them in hunger. Now is the time of hunger; then, that of satiety. He who did not abandon us to the hunger of this corruption, how will he satisfy us with immortal deeds! But during the time of hunger one must suffer, one must redouble one's effort, one must persevere to the end. All roads must now be traveled, because the path is flat and we must think about what we transport. Perhaps there are still frantic spectators in the amphitheater and sitting in the sun; However, if we remain standing there, we find ourselves in the shadow and the things we contemplate are more useful and beautiful. Let us contemplate beautiful things and be contemplated by etiam tutiorem false whores. Quomodo enim te deiiciat nescis, both elisum gravius, quanto sublimius ferebaris. Mendax equus ad salutem: in abtindantia autem virtutis suae non erit salvus. Et unde erit salvus? Non de virtute, non de viribus, non de honore, non de gloria, non de equo. Et where? What was I going? Ubi inveniam unde salvus sim? Noli diu quaerere, noli longe. Ecce oculi Domini super timentes eum. Videtis quia ipsi sunt quos prospexit de habitáculo suo. Ucee oculi Domini super timentes eum, sperantes super misericordiam eius: non de meritis suis, non de virtute, non de fortitudine, non de equo, thirst for mercy eius. 25 [v.19]. Ut eruat a morte animas eorum.

Vitam aetematrt promittit. What is this pilgrimage? numquid desert? Vide quid sequitur: Et alat eos in jame. Tempus famis est moda, tempus saturitatis post erit. Who us in fame huius corruptionis non deserit, immortales textos quomodo satiabit? Sed quamdiu tempus est famis, tolerandum est, durandum est, perseverandum est usque in finem. lam currenda sunt omnia, quia tt via est plana, et cogitandum est quid portemus. beautiful. Let us contemplate with our minds the things recorded in the sentences of the Scriptures and let us rejoice at such a spectacle. Who is our viewer? Our soul will wait patiently in the Lord. But what will happen if patience disappears from us? What do I say? It will certainly remain in us, because God is our help and protector. Helps in the fight, defends in the sun, does not abandon you; You suffer and remain. He who perseveres to the end will be saved. 27 [v. 21]. What will be given to you if you had waited patiently, if you had suffered, if you had gone to the end? For what reward do you suffer? Why do you endure such hard work for such a long time? For our hearts will rejoice in Him and we hope in His holy name. Wait here to enjoy yourself there; be hungry and thirsty here to eat there. 28 [v. 22]. He exhorted us to endure all this, he filled us with the joy of hope, he proposed to us what we should love, in what and what we should boast about; After these exhortations he made cuntur in sensibus divinarum Scripturarum, et gaudeamus tali spectaculo. Sed propter peregrinationis tolerantiam quamdiu fames est, et exspectamus in via refici, ne defiriamus; quid nobis imponitur, vel quid profiteri debenmus? Anima our patiens erit Domino. Secura exspectabit misericorditer promittentem, misericorditer et veraciter exponentem: et doñee exhibitat, quid agamus? Anima our patiens erit Domino. Sed quid, si in ipsa patientia non durabimus? Brothers, we exhort you to practice this charity, not only among yourselves, but also with those outside, whether they are still pagans who do not yet believe in Christ, or whether they are far from us and who with us recognize the Head, but who are separated from the body. Brothers, let us have compassion on them as our brothers. Whether they like it or not, they are our brothers. They would cease to be our brothers if they stopped saying: Our Father. Of certain men the prophet said: To those who say to you: You are not our brothers, tell them: You are our brothers. Look carefully at who could have said this. Perhaps from the pagans? No, because we do not call these men brothers sefit oratio brevis et salubris: Fiat misericordia tita, Domine, super nos. Et quo merit? Sicut speravimus in te. Non, ñeque enim dicimus eos fratres nostros secundum Scrip-

according to the Scriptures, nor according to the custom of speaking of the Church. Perhaps of the Jews who did not believe in Christ? Read the Apostle and you will see that, when the Apostle speaks without any epithet, he only means Christians by brothers: The brother or sister is not subject to this. Here, when talking about marriage, he calls the Christian brother or sister. Likewise it says: You who judge your brother or who despise him; and in another place: You, he says, commit iniquity and defraud, and this your brothers. These who say: You are not our brothers, call us pagans. That's why they want to rebaptize us, saying that we don't have what they give. And he stretched out at the entrances to the doors. That is to say, he humiliated himself. This is the stretching out from the beginning of our faith. The entrance of the door is the beginning of faith; from here the Church begins and reaches the vision; Therefore, by believing the things you do not see, you deserve to enjoy when you begin to see face to face. This is what the title of the psalm says. You heard him in a compendious explanation. Let us now hear the same words of the one who affected and tympanised at the gates of the city. 3 [v.2). I will bless the Lord at all times; His praise (be) always in my mouth. Christ says it, let the Christian also say it, because he is also part of the body of Christ. Cristum suum in sacerdotio, et dimisit gentem Iudaeorum, et venit ad Gentes. Quid est ergo, Affectabat? Affectu plenus erat. Quid enim tam plenurn affectu, quam mercy Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui videns infirmitatem nostram, ut nos a sempiterna morte liberaet, temporalem mortem cum tanta iniuria contumeliaque suscepit? Et tympanizabat: quia tympanum non fit nisí cum corium jn ligno extenditur; et tympanizabat David significans quod crucifigendus esset Christus. Tympanizabat autem ad ostia civitatis: quae sunt ostia civitatis, nisi corda nostra quae clauseramus contra Christum, qui de tympano crucis aperuit corda mortalium? Et ferebatur in manibus suis: quomodo jerebatur in manibus suis?

Quia cum commendaret ipsum corpus suum et sanguinem suum, accepit in manus suas quod norunt fideles; et ipse se portabat quodam moda, cum diceret: Hoc est corpus meum (Mt 26,26). Et procidebat ad ostia portae: id est, humiliavit se. Hoc est enim procidere usque ad initium fidei nostrae. Ostium enim portae initium fidei, unde incipit Ecclesia, et pervenit usque ad speciem: ut cum credit ea quae non videt, mereatur perfrui, cum facie ad faciem videre coeperit. Sic se habet titulus Psalnli; breviter audimus: audiamus iam ipsa verba affectantis et tympanizantis ad portam civitatis. 3 [v.2]. Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore, semper latís eius in ore meo. Dicit Christus, dicat et christianus; quia et christianus in corpore Christi est; et propterea Christus homo, ut posset esse christianus i
Praise of God, protector of the righteous

He became man so that the Christian can be an angel who says: I will bless the Lord. When will you bless the Lord? When it does you some good? When the goods of the century abound? When wheat, oil, wine, gold, silver, servants, livestock are exceedingly abundant? When mortal health remains intact and robust? When the things you do all develop and nothing perishes through premature death? When happiness overflows in all parts of the house and all good things surround us, then will you bless the Lord? No. At all times. Then then, and when these things, according to the circumstances and the scourge of the Lord our God, are disturbed, they perish, fewer are born and those born die. This happens, and from here comes scarcity, need, work, pain and trial. But you, who sang: I will bless the Lord at all times; His praise (be) always in my mouth, bless him when he gives you these things and when he takes them from you. Because whoever gives them, takes them away; but He does not distance himself from those who bless him. 4. Who is he who blesses the Lord at all times? The humble at heart. Our Lord makes this humility known to us in his body and blood, because when he gives us his body and his blood, he gives us his humility in the same thing that was written in this story, that is, in that like David's frenzy that we have let pass inadvertently: And saliva ran down his beard. When the Apostle was read, you heard this saliva, but it ran down the beard. Some will say: What saliva did we hear? Have we not now read the words of the Apostle: The Jews ask for an angelus sign, qui ait, Benedicam Dominum. When benedicam Dominum? Quando tibí benefacit?, quando abundant saecularia?, quando multum abundat frumenti, olei, vini, auri, argenti, mancipiorum, pecorum, salusque ista mortalis invulnerata et incorrupta persistit, ea quae nascuntur crescunt omnia, nihil immatura morte subtrahitur, congratulations tota abundat in domo, circumfluunt omnia, tune bless Dominum? Non: thirst in omni tempore. Ergo et tune, et quando ista secundum tempus et secundum flagella Domini Dei nostri turbantur, auferuntur, mines nascuntur, iam nata dilabuntur. Fiunt enim haec, et inde sequitur penuria, egestas, labor, dolor et tentatio. Be your qui cantasti, Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore, semper laus eius in ore meo, et quando ista dat, benedic; et when he was tollit, benedic. Quia ille dat, ille tollit: sed seipsum a benedicente se non tollit. 4.

Quis est autem qui benedicit Dominum in omni tempore, nisi humilis corde? Ipsam enim humilitatem docuit Dominus noster in corpore et sanguine suo: quia cum commendat corpus et sanguinem suum, humilitatem suam commendat, in eo quod in ipsa historia scriptum est, in illo quasi furore David, quod praetermisimus, Et salivae decurrebant super barbam eius. Cum legeretur Apostolus, audistis ipsas salivas, sed decurrentes super barbam. Dicit aliquis, Quas salivas audivimus? Nonne moda lectus est Apostolus, cum diceret: ludaei signa petunt, et Graeci
Ennarrations on the Psalms

and the Greeks demand wisdom? Recently it was read: We, on the contrary, preach Christ crucified (then he played the casket), which is a scandal to the Jews, and madness to the Gentiles; But for the same so-called Jews and Greeks, Christ is the strength of God and the Wisdom of God, because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men. Saliva symbolizes foolishness and weakness. But if the foolishness of God is wiser than men and the weakness of God is stronger than men, do not stumble in the saliva, but pay attention, for it runs on the beard. As saliva symbolizes foolishness, so the beard symbolizes strength. Then he covered his strength with the body of weakness, and thus what was externally weakened was manifested as in saliva, but internally the divine strength was covered like a beard. Then humility is recommended to us. Be humble if you want to bless the Lord at all times and may His praise always be in your mouth. Job not only blessed the Lord when he had abundance in all things, with which we read that he had been rich and happy: happy for the livestock, for the servants, for the house, for the children, for all things. Pay attention for a moment: all things were taken from him and he fulfilled when he said: The Lord gave it to me, the Lord took it from me; as it pleased him, so it was done; Blessed be the name of the Lord, what is written in this psalm. Here you have the model of the one who blesses the Lord at all times. 5 {v.3j. Why does man bless the Lord at all times? Because he is humble. What does it mean to be humble? Not be jacsapienliam quaerunt? Modo lectum est: Nos autem praedicamus, inquit, Cbristum crucifixum (tune enim tympanizabat) Iudaeis quidem scandalum, Gentibus autem stultitiam; ipsis vero vocatis Iudaeis et Graecis, Cbristum Dei Virtutem et Dei Sapientiam: quia quod stultum est Dei, sapientius est hominibus; et quod injirmum est Dei, fortius est quam homines (1 Cor 1:22-26). Salivae enim significant stultitiam, salivae signiflcant infirmitatem. Be si quod stultum est Dei, sapientius est hominibus; et quod infirmum est Dei, fortius est quam nomines: non tanquam salivae offendant, sed attende, quia super barbam decurrunt. Quomodo enim salivis infirmitas, sic barba virtus ostenditur. Texit ergo virtutem suam corpore infirmitatis suae: et quod forinsecus infirmabatur, tanquam in saliva apparebat; intus autem divina virtus tanquam barba tegebatur.

Ergo humilitas nobis commendatur. This humilis, si vis benedicere Dominum in omni tempore, et semper laus eius sit in ore tuo. Quia Iob non tantum benedixit Dominum, quando abundabant illi omnia, quibus eum legimus divitem Fuisse et felicem, et pecore, et servís, et domo, felicem filiis, et omnibus rebus. Ablata sunt omnia uno tempore, et implevit quod in hoc psalmo scriptum est, they say: Dominus dedit, Domiñus abstulit; sicut Domino placuit, ita jactum est: sit nomen Domini benedictum (Iob 1,21). Ecce habes exemplum benedicentis Dominum in omni tempore. 5 [v.3]. Quare autem benedicit Dominum homo in omni tempore? Quia humilis est. Quid est esse humilis? Nolle in se laudan. Who in se
Praise of God, protector of the righteous

tantcious He who wants to boast is arrogant. He who is not proud is humble. Don't you want to be arrogant? So that you may be humble, say what was written: My soul will glory in the Lord; Let the humble hear and rejoice. Those who do not want to glory in the Lord are not meek, but fierce, sullen, conceited, arrogant. The Lord wants to have gentle donkeys. Be the Lord's donkey, that is, be meek. He rides you, He rules you, do not be afraid to stumble and fall on the precipice. Weakness is your thing, but see who protects you. You are a colt, but you carry Christ. He also approached the city riding on a colt, and that one was tame. Was that donkey praised? Was it said to the donkey: Hosanna to the son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord? The donkey carried; but the transported one was praised by those who preceded and followed him. Did the donkey perhaps say: My soul will glory in the Lord; Let the meek hear and rejoice? That donkey never said this, oh brothers! But let the people who symbolize that donkey say so if they want to transport their Owner. Perhaps the people are angry because they are compared to the donkey on which the Lord sat, and for this reason some arrogant and vain people will tell me: See, you are making asses of us. Let everyone who says this be an ass of the Lord, so as not to be a horse and a mule, in whom there is no understanding. You know the psalm in which it is said: Do not be like the horse and the mule, in which there is no understanding. The horse and the mule sometimes raise their necks, and in their ferocity throw the knight from them. With the bit, the bit and the whip they are tamed until they learn to carry their master. You, vult laudari, superbus est. Qui superbus non est, humilis est. Non vis ergo esse superbus? Ut possis esse humilis, dic quod dictum est: In Domino laudabitur anima mea: audiant mansueti, et laetentur. Ergo qui non in Domino volunt laudari, non sunt mansueti; sed traces, asperi, elati, superbi. Iumenta mansueta vult habere Dominus: esto iumentum Domini, id est, esto mansuetus. Sedet ille super te, ipse regit te: noli timere ne offendas, et eas in praeceps. Infirmitas quidem tua est, sed atinde quis tibi praesideat. Pullus asini is, sed Cbristum portas. Nam et ipse in pullo asini come ad civitatem, et Fuit illud iumentum mansuetum. Numquid laudabatur iumentum illud? Numquid íumento saysbatur: Hosanna, fili David, benedictus who come in nomine Domini? (Mt 21,9).

Asellus portabat: sed ille qui portabatur, a praecedentibus et consequentibus laudabatur. Et dicebat forte iumentum: In Domino laudabitur anima mea; auditor mansueti, et laetentur. Nunquam illud dixit ille asinus, fratres; sed dicat illud populus qui imítatur iumentum illud, si vult portare Dominum suum. Irascitur forte populus, quia comparatur asello in quo sedit Dominus; et dicet mihi aliqui superbi et elati: Ecce asinos nos fecit. Sit asinus Domini quisquís hoc dicit: ne sit equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus. Nostis enim psalmum ubi dicitur: No/ite esse sicut equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus (Ps 31,9). Equus enim et mulus erigunt cervicem aliquando, et sua ferocitate excutiunt a se sessorem.
Ennarrations on the Psalms

Before the bridle crushes your mouth, be meek and take your Lord; Do not wish to be praised, but let him who rides on you be praised, and therefore you will say: My soul will glory in the Lord; Let the meek hear and rejoice. When those who are not gentle hear it, they do not rejoice, but rather become angry, and these are precisely the ones who say that we have made them asses. Those who are meek deign to hear and be what they hear. 6 [v. 4]. Continue: Magnify the Lord with me. Who is this that exhorts us to magnify the Lord with him? Brothers, everyone who belongs to the body of Christ must dedicate themselves to magnifying the Lord with them. He who acts in this way loves the Lord. And how do you treat me? Not envying his coamador. He who loves carnally, of necessity loves with pestiferous zeal; Thus, if perhaps he would have thought very highly of being able to see a naked woman, whom he desired with pestilent love, would he perhaps want someone else to see her too? Of necessity she will be consumed with jealousy and hatred if someone else sees her too. Chastity is preserved if the one to whom it is permitted sees it and the other does not see it, or if the other does not see it as well. This does not happen with the wisdom of God; we will see her face to face; We will all see it and no one will be jealous there. She shows herself to everyone, and she is pure and chaste with everyone. They will change into her, and she will not change into them. She is the Truth, she is God. Have you ever heard, brothers, that our God could change? He is the Truth that surpasses all things, he is the Word of God, he is the Wisdom of God, by whom all things were made; He has his lovers. But what does her lover say? EngrandeDomantur frenis, camo, verberibus, doñee discant subesse, et portare dominum suum. Tu autem antequam fredo tundantur ora tua, esto mansuetas, et porta Dominum tuum: noli in te velle laudari, sed laudetur ille qui super te sedet, et dices: In Domino laudabitur anima mea, audiant mansueti, et laetentur. Nam quando audiunt non mansueti, non laetantur, sed irascuntur: et ipsí sunt qui dicunt quod asinos eos fecerimus. Qui autem mansueti sunt, dignentur audire et esse quod audiunt. 6 [v.4]. Sequitur, Magnify Yourself Dominum mecum. Quis est iste qui exhortatur ut magnificemus cum illo Dominum? Quisquís est, fratres, in corpore Christi, ad hoc must give operam, ut magnificetur cum illo Dominus.

Amat enim Dominum quisquís est iste. Et quomodo illum amat? Ut non invideat coamatori suo. Quisquís enim amat carnaliter, necesse est ut cum zelo pestífico amet: si forte pro magno nudam videre potuerit, quam pestífico amore desideravit, numquid vult ut videat illam et alius? Necesse est ut zelo et livore saucietur, si et alius eam viderit. Et sic servatur castitas, si aut ille videat cui licet, et alius non videat, aut nec ipse. Non sic est Sapientia Dei: videbimus illam facie ad faciem, et omnes videbimus, et nemo ibi zelabit. Omnibus is exhibited, et integra est, et casta est omnibus. lili mutatur in eam, et ipsa in eos non mutatur. Ipsa est veritas, ipsa est Deus. Numquid aliquando audistis, fratres, quod potuerit commutari Deus noster? Supereminens omnibus ve-
Praise of God, protector of the righteous

yield with me to the Lord. I don't just want to magnify the Lord; I don't just want to love him; I do not want to give myself to Him alone, because I do not fear that, if I am embraced by Him, I will not be able to lend my hands to another. Such is the breadth of God's Wisdom that all souls can be embraced and enjoyed. And what shall I say, brothers? Let those be ashamed who love God so much that they envy others. Lost men love the charioteer, and everyone who loves the charioteer or the hunter of the circus games wants all the people to love him with him, and thus he exhorts and says: Love the pantomime with me, love with me this and that clumsiness. He cries out among the crowd for clumsiness to be loved with him, and the Christian does not cry out in the Church for the Truth of God to be loved with him! Arouse love in you, brothers, and shout to each one of yours and say: Magnify the Lord with me. May this fervor be found in you. Why are these things recited and explained to you? If you love God, snatch to the love of Goddess all those who are united with you and all those who are in your house. If the body of Christ is loved by you, that is, the unity of the Church, snatch them away to enjoy and say to them: Magnify the Lord with me. 7 [v. 4]. And let us all praise his name together. What does it mean, let's praise his name all together? The same as all of them one or at the same time. For many codices say: Magnify the Lord with me and let us all exalt his name together. Whether it is said in idipsum (in the same, together) or in unum (in one, all a ritas est, Verbum Dei est, Spaientia Dei est, per quem facta sunt omnia: habet amatares suos. Sed quid dicit amatar ipsius? Magnificate Dominum mecum. Nolo solus magnificare Dominum, nolo solus amare, nolo solus amplecti. Non enim si ego amplexus fuero, non habet alius ubi inanus ponat. Latitudo tanta est in ipsa Sapientia, ut omnes animae amplectantur et perfruantur. Et quid dicam, fratres? Erubescant qui sic amant Deum, ut invideant alus? ut totus populus cum illo amet; Clámate unicuique vestrorum, et say: Magnify Yourself Dominum mecum.

Sit in vobis iste fervor. Quare vobis recitantur ista, et exponuntur? Si amatis Deum, rapite omnes ad amorem Dei qui vobis iunguntur, et omnes qui sunt in domo vestra: si amatur a vobis corpus Christi, id est unitas Ecclesiae, rapite eos ad fruendum, et dicite: Magnify yourself Dominum mecum. 7 [v.4]. Et exaltemus nomen eius in idipsum. Quid est, exaltemus nomen eius in idipsum? Hoc est, in unum. Nam multi codices sic habent: Magnify yourself Dominum mecum, et exaltemus nomen eius in unum. Sive in idipsum dicatur, sive in unum; hoc Idem dicitur. Ergo rapite quos potestis, hortando, carrying, begging, disputing, rationem redden-
^narratives about the Psalms
Praise of God, protector of the righteous

one, at a time), means the same thing. Then snatch away whomever you can, exhorting, carrying, supplicating, disputing, making known with meekness and kindness. Take them away from love so that, if they magnify the Lord, they magnify him all together. It seems to Donato's party that it magnifies the Lord; How did the globe of the earth offend you? Let us tell them, brothers: Magnify the Lord with me and let us all exalt his name together. Why do you want to magnify the Lord separately? God is one, why do you try to form two peoples for God? Why do you want to divide the body of Christ? He certainly was hanging on the cross when he was tympanising, and hanging he expired; Those who suspended him came, found him dead and did not break his legs; However, the thieves, who were still alive while on the cross, had them broken so that, through the pain that accelerated death, they would be freed from the torment, as is customary to execute those who are crucified. Then the persecutor came and found the Lord who had breathed out his spirit in peace, for he said: I have power to give life. Who did he give his life for? For all his people, for his entire body. The persecutor came and did not break the legs of Christ; Donato comes and destroys the Church of Christ. The body of Christ on the cross remains intact in the hands of the persecutors, and in the hands of Christians the body of the Church is not found in its entirety. Let us cry, brothers, with the greatest possible groan: Magnify the Lord with me and let us all exalt his name together. The Church calls you; These words are the voice of the Church, which calls those who broke away. Why did they break off? For the arrogance. The Lord taught, cum mansuetudine, cum lenitate: rapite ad amorem; ut si magnificant Dominum, in unum magnificent. Et pars Donati videtur sibi magnificare Dominum: quid eos offendit orbis terrarum? Dicamus illis, fratres: Magnify yourself Dominum mecum, et exaltemus nomen eius in unum. Quare in praecisione vultis magnificare Dominum? Ule unus est, quare duos populos vultis faceré Deo? Quare vultis dissipare corpus Christi?

Certe enim ipse pendebat in intersection, quando tympanizabat: et cum pendeet in intersection, emisit spiritum; et venerunt illi qui eumsuspenran*, et invenerunt eum emisisse spiritum, et non illi fregerunt aura: latronibus autem adhuc in intersection vivosibus fregerunt (lo 19,32.33), ut per ipsum dolorem compendio mortis ab illo cruciatu liberareniur, quomodo solebat crucifixis fieri. Ergo venit persecutor, invenit Dominum quiete deposuisse spiritum: quia ipse dixit, Potestaiem drool ponendi animam meam (Ib. 10,18). Pro quibus posit animam suam? Pro universal plebe sua, pro toto corpore suo. Venit ergo persecutor, et non fregit crura Christi: venit Donatus et disrupit Ecclesiam Christi. Integrum Corpus Christi in intersection Inter manus persecutorum est, et Inter manus Christianorum non est integrum corpus Ecclesíae. Clamemus ergo, fratres, cum gemitu quantum possumus, dicentes: Magnificale Dominum mecum, et exaltemus nomen eius in unum. Ecclesia enim illis clamat: vox est Ecclesiae, clamans

humility to the one who gives his body and blood. This is the humility that we told your holiness that this text of the psalm deals with and celebrates when the body and blood of Christ is recommended, when it speaks of the weakness of Christ, which he deigned to take for us. 8 [v.5]. I sought the Lord and he heard me. Where did the Lord hear? Inside you. Where does it hit? Inside. There you pray, there you are heard, there you are sanctified. You prayed; you were heard, you were sanctified, and who is next to you does not realize. Everything is done in secret, as the Lord says in the Gospel: Go into your room, close the door and pray in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you. When you enter your room, you enter your heart. Blessed are those who rejoice when they enter their hearts and find nothing evil there. Your holiness sees how those who have bad wives do not want to enter their homes; how they go to the forum, and enjoy this; But when the time comes to enter their houses, they become sad, because they have to enter the place of sorrow, of grumbling, of bitterness, of desolation, since it is not an orderly house that in which there is no peace between the man and the woman, and it is better for him to wander the street. If those are unfortunate who, upon returning home, fear being in a bad mood because of some quarrels of their own, how much more miserable will be those who do not want to enter into their conscience so as not to be confused there by some quarrel about sins. Then, so that you can return with pleasure to your heart, cleanse it. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God. Throw from there the illis qui se praeciderunt. Unde enim disrupti sunt? Per superbiam. Docet autem Christus humilitatem, cum commendat corpus et sanguinem suum: quod diximus Sanctitati Vestrae in hoc Psalmi textu agi et celebraten, ubi commendatur corpus et sanguis Christi, ubi commendatur humilitas Christi, quam pro nobis suscipere dignitus est. 8 [v.5]. Inquisivi Dominum, et exaudivit me. Ubi exaudivit Dominus? Intus. Ubi dat? Intus. Ibi pray, ibi exaudiris, ibi beatificaris. Orasti, exauditus is, beatificatus is; et non scit qui iuxta te stat: gestum est totum in occulto, sicut Dominus in Gospel dicit: Intra in cubiculum tuum, claude ostium tuum, et ora in occulto, et Pater tuus qui videt in occulto, reddet tibi (Mt 6,6). Cum ergo intras cubiculum tuum, intras cor tuum. Beati qui gaudent quando intrant ad cor suum, et nihil malí ibi inveniunt.

Attendat Sanctitas Vestra: quomodo nolunt intrare domos suas qui habent malas uxores, quomodo exeunt ad forum, et gaudent; coepit hora esse, qua intrent in domum suam, contristantur: intraturí sunt enim ad taedia, ad murmura, ad amaritudines, ad eversiones; quia non est domus composita, ubi inter virum et uxorem pax nulla est; et melius illi est foris circumire. Si ergo miseri sunt, qui cum redeunt ad parietes suos, timent ne aliquibus suorum perturbationibus evertantur; quanto sunt miseriores, qui ad conscientiam suam rediré nolunt, ne ibi litibus peccatorum evertantur! Ergo ut possis libens rediré ad cor tuum,
Ennarrations on the Psalms

filth of desires, the plague of avarice, the rottenness of superstition, sacrilege and evil thoughts, hatred, I do not say against the friend, but also against the enemy; Throw away all these things, enter, enter into your heart, and there you will be glad. When you begin to enjoy, the very cleanliness of your heart will delight you and make you pray. (It will happen to you) as if you had come to a place where there is silence, where perhaps there is rest, and the place is clean; Let's pray, you say, here, because you love the amenity of the place and you believe that God will hear you there. If you delight in the cleanliness of a visible place, why are you not offended by the filth of your heart? Enter him, cleanse all things, raise your eyes to God, and he will immediately hear you. Cry out and say: I sought the Lord and he heard me and delivered me from all my tribulations. Because? Because even if you are enlightened, even when you begin to have a good conscience, tribulations still remain, because something weak remains, until death is submerged in victory and this mortal is clothed with immortality. It is necessary, therefore, that you be scourged in this world; It is necessary that you endure some temptations and suggestions. God will cleanse all things, He will deliver you from all tribulation; look for him 9. I sought the Lord and he heard me. Therefore those who do not seek the Lord are not heard. See your charity that did not say: I received old age from the Lord, and he heard me; I got this or that from the Lord, and he heard me. It is one thing to obtain something from the Lord and another to seek the Lord. I sought, he says, the Lord, and he heard me. But you, when you pray and say: munda illud: beati enim mundi corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt (Ib. 5,8). Aufer inde cupiditatum sordes, aufer labem avaritiae, aufer labem superstitionum, aufer sacrilegia et malas cogitafiones; Odia, non dico adversus amicum, sed etiam adversus inimicum: aufer ista omnia; intra ín cor tuum, et gaudebis ibi. Cum ibi coeperis gaudere, ipsa munditia cordis tui delectabit te, et faciet orare: quomodo si venias ad aliquem locum, silentium est ibi, forte quies est ibi, mundus est locus; oremus hic, say: et delectat te compositio loci, et credis quod ibi te exaudiat Deus. Si ergo loci visibilis te delectat munditia, quare te non offendit immunditia cordis tui? Intra, munda omnia, leva oculos tuos ad Deum, et statim te exaudiet.

Clama, et dic: lnquisivi Dominum, et exaudivit me; et ex omnibus tribulationibus meis eruit me. Quare? Quia cum fueris illuminatus, cum coeperis hic habere bonam conscientiam, restant tribulationes, quia restat aliquid infirmum, doñee mors absorbatur in victoriam, et moríale hoc induat immorlalitatem (1 Cor 15,54): necesse est ut in hoc saeculo flagelleris; Necesse est ut aliquas temptationes suggestionsesque patiaris. Mundabit Deus omnia, eruet te ab omni tribulatione, ipsum quaere. 9- lnquisivi Dominum, et exaudivit me. Qui ergo non exaudiuntur, non Dominum quaerunt. 15. Don't understand like that. Well how am I to understand? Understand all spiritual goods. But where are they? They are not seen with the eyes, but with the heart. I don't see those goods. Those who love see them. I don't see justice. It is not gold or silver. If it were gold, you would see it; As it is faith, you do not see it. But if you don't see faith, why do you love the faithful servant? Ask yourself which servant you love. Perhaps you have a beautiful, tall, slender servant, but a thief, bad, defrauding; Maybe you have another short, ugly, bad color, but faithful, sparing, sober; Listen, I beg you, which of these two do you love? If you ask the eyes of the flesh, you lean towards the beautiful unjust; If in the eyes of the heart, the deformed faithful triumphs. Then you see that what you want another to demonstrate to you, that is, faith, you must demonstrate to him. Why do you show contentment with the one who shows faith to you and praise him for the goods that can only be seen with the eyes of the heart? Being full of spiritual riches, will you be poor? He was rich because he had a bed of ivory, and you will be poor having the bed of your heart filled with so many pearls of virtues: justice, truthfulness, charity, faith, patience and resignation! Consider your wealth, if you have it, and compare it with that of the rich. But he found some superb mules at the fair and bought them. Forte habes servum formosum, staturosum, bene compositum; sed furem, nequam, fraudulentum: habes autem alium forte parvum statura, deformem facie, colore tetro; sed fidelem, parcum, sobrium: attende, rogo te, quem istorum duorum diligis? Who is the man who longs for life and wishes to have good days? Don't look for good days here. He looks for a good house, but he doesn't look for it where it is. This is the same as if you searched even in that country where he does not live and were told: You are looking for a good man, you are looking for a great man; look for him, but not here; You look for him here in vain, you will never find him. You look for good days; Let's look for them with you, but not here. Our parents had them. You deceive yourselves; everyone suffered. Read the Scriptures. God wanted them to be written to console us. In the days of Elijah there was famine; our parents suffered it. The heads of dead donkeys were sold for gold; Amatara arrived and ate them: two women agreed to kill their children and eat them; One killed her son and both ate him; the other did not want to kill hers; but then the one who first killed hers demanded it from her; Such a dispute reached the king's ears, since they appeared before the king disputing about the death of their children. May God take away from us the things we read regarding such foods. There are always bad times in the world, but there are always good times in God. Abraham had good days, but internally in his heart. He had bad days when, due to hunger, he changed regions rentes tuos, similiter tibi de diebus suis murmurarent. Fuerunt beati patres nostri, nos miseri sumus, malo dies habemus: dominatus est ille, putabamus quia illo mortuo posset aliquod refrigerium dari; deteriorates venerunt. O Deus, show off nobis dies bonds! Quis est homo, qui vult vitam, et diligit videre dies bonds? Non hic quaerat dies bonds. Bonam rem quaerit, sed non in regione eius illam quaerit. Quomodo si aliquem iustum quaereres in ea patria, ubi non habitaret, diceretur tibi: Bonum virum quaeris, magnum virum quaeris, quaere illum, sed noli hic, superfluo hic eum quaeris, nunquam eum inventurus es.

Dies bonds quaeris, simul eos quaeramus, nolite hic. Sed habuerunt illos patres nostri. Fallimini: omnes hic laboraverunt. Legite Scripturas: ideo voluit Deus ut scriberentur, ut nos consolaremur. Temporibus Eliae fuet fames, passi sunt eam patres nostri. Capita iumentorum. mortuorum auro vendebantur, occiderunt suos, et comederunt eos: et duae mulleres statuerunt inter se ut occiderent filios suos, et manducarent; occidit a filium suum, et manducaverunt eum ambae; alia nolebat occidere filium suum, et demandingbat illa quae prior occiderat filium suum; et talis rixa venit ante regem, adduxerunt se ante regem, contendantes de interfectione filiorum (4 Reg 4,26-30). De talibus cibis avertat Deus ea quae legimus. Semper dies mali in saeculo, sed semper dies boni in Deo. Habuit these bonds Abraham, sed intus in corde: habuit these bad ones, when a fame mutavit regionem,
Ennarrations on the Psalms

looking for food. In this way everyone tried to acquire food. Saint Paul, who says: In hunger, in thirst, in cold and in nakedness, he had good days. But let the servants not be troubled; The Lord himself had bad days in this world, since he suffered outrages, insults, the cross and many other evils. 18 [v.14]. Therefore the Christian does not murmur; See what footprints you follow. If you long for good days, listen to him who teaches and says: Come, children; hear me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord. What do you want? Life and good days. Hear and restrain your tongue from evil. Do this. I do not want, says the wicked man, I do not want to prohibit evil to my tongue; I want life and good days. If your worker says to you: “I destroy this vineyard and ask you for wages; "You took me to the vineyard to peel and prune it, I will cut all the useful branches, I will tear out the same vines from the vineyard so that you have nowhere to pick grapes, and once this is done, you will pay me for my work," wouldn't you say he is crazy? Wouldn't you throw him out of your house before you took the pruning shears in his hands? Such are the men who intend to do evil, perjure, blaspheme against God, gossip, steal, get drunk, litigate, commit adultery, wear amulets, approach spell-casters and want to have a good day. To him it is said: You cannot, by doing evil, obtain a good reward. If you are unjust, must God be unjust too? Then what will I do? What do you want? I want life and good days. Restrain your tongue from evil and let your lips not speak lies. That is, do not commit fraud or deception. et quaerebat cibum (Gen 12:10, et 26:1). Sic omnes quaesierunt. Paulus habuit dies bonds, who said: ln jame et sift, in frigore et nuditate? (2 Cor 11:27). Sed non irascantur serví: ipse Dominus non habuit dies bonds in hoc saeculo; contumelias, iniurias, cruzem, et tanta mala patiebatur. 18 [v.14]. Non ergo christianus murmuret, videat cuius vestigia sequatur. Sed si dies bondes amat, audiat docentem et dicentem: Venite, filU, audite me, timorem Domini dominicebo vos. Quid vis? Vitam et dies bonds. Audi, et fac: Confine linguam luam a malo. Fac illud. Nolo, dicit homo miser: et linguam meam nolo continere a malo, et vitam voló, et dies bonds. Si operanius tuus tibi diceret: Et vasto istam vineam, et exigo a te mercedem: adduxisti me ad vineam ut falcitem illam et putem, concido omnia ligna utilia, praecidam ipsa robora vitium, ut non hic habeas quod colligas, et cum fecero ista, redditurus es mihi laborera meum.

Nonne insanum illum diceres? nonne illum de domo tua repelieres, antequam mitteret manum ad falcem? Such sunt homines, qui et faceré volunt mala, et iurare mendacium, et blasphemare contra Deum, et murmurare, et fraudin faceré, et inebriari, et litigare, et adulteran, et ligaturas adhibere, et iré ad sorceresses, et dies bonds videre. Dicitur illi: Non potes male faciens quaerere bonam mercedem. If your iniustus is, iniustus erit et Deus? Ergo quid faciam? Quid vis? Vitam flew, dies bonds flew. Confine linguam tuam a malo, et labia tua ne loquantut dolum: id est, nulli fraudm, nulli mendacium.
Praise of God, protector of the righteous

19 [v.15], What does it mean to depart from evil? It is little not to harm, not to kill anyone, not to steal, not to commit adultery, not to steal, not to bear false witness. Turn away from evil; When you have turned away, you will say: I am sure, I have done everything perfectly, I will have life and see good days. But you must not only depart from evil, but also do good. It is a small thing if you do not dispossess anyone; dress naked. If you did not plunder, you turned away from evil; but you do not do good until you receive the pilgrim into your house. Therefore you must turn away from evil in such a way that you do good. Seek peace and follow it. He did not tell you: you will have peace here, but "seek it and follow it." Where will I follow her? Where did he get ahead of me? The Lord is our peace; He resurrected and ascended to heaven. Seek peace and follow it, because also, when you are resurrected, this mortal will change and you will be surrounded by peace where no one will bother you. You possess perfect peace when you do not feel hungry. Here bread provides you peace; supplant bread and you will see what war is waged in your stomach. The righteous themselves, how they groan here, oh brothers! And this happens so that you know that we seek peace here, but we will achieve it in the end. We have it here in part so that we deserve to have it there completely. What does it mean in part? May we live in harmony here; Let us love our neighbors as ourselves. Love your neighbor as yourself, have peace with him. Certainly there cannot but exist some strife, as there existed between the brethren and the saints, between Barnabas and Paul; but not those that break harmony and destroy charity. You also oppose some ve19 [v.15]. Be what it is, Decline to bad? Parum est nulli noceas, nullum occidas, non fureris, non adulteres, non fraudum facías, non falsum testimonium dicas. Decline to bad: cum declinaveris, dicis: Securas sum, perfeci omnia, habebo vitam, videbo dies bonds. Non solum declines to bad; sed, et fac bonum. Parum est ut non exspolies: vesti nudum. Si non exspoliaveris, declinasti a malo: sed non facies bonum, nisi cum peregrinum susceperis in domum tuam. Ergo sic declines to malo, ut facías bonum. Quaere pacem, et sequete eam. Non tibi dixit, habebis hic pacem: quaere illam, et sequere eam. Quo illam sequor? Quo praecessit. Dominus enim est pax nostra, resurrexit et ascendit in caelum. Quaere pacem, et sequere illam: quia et tu cum surrexeris, hoc mortale mutabitur, et amplecteris pacem, ubi tibi nemo molestus erit.

Ibi enim est perfection pax, ubi non esuries. Nam hic tibi pacem facit pañis: subduc panem, et vide quale bellum erit intra viscera tua. Ipsi iusti quomodo gemunt hic, fratres? ut sciatis quia quaerimus hic pacem, consequemur autem in fine. Sed ex parte hic habeamus, ut ex toto illic habere mereamur. What is it, ex parte? Concordes simus hic, diligamus proximum quomodo nos. Sic dilige fratrem quomodo teipsum, habe cum illo pacem. Sed non possunt nisi existence rixae aliquae, quomodo inter fratres et inter sanctos exstiterunt, inter Barnabam et Paulum (Act 15,39): sed non quae occiderent concordiam, non quae interimerent charitatem. Nam
Ennarrations on the Psalms

It's you, and yet you don't hate it. Anyone who repents of something contends with himself. He sinned, he relapsed, he was angry with himself for having done this, for having committed it; then he quarrels within himself, but this dispute is directed towards peace. See how a certain righteous man contends with himself and expresses himself: Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Wait on the Lord, for I will still praise him. When he said to his soul: Why do you trouble me?, we cannot doubt that it troubled him. Perhaps he wanted to suffer for Christ, and his soul grieved him. Also he who knew and said: Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you trouble me?, did not yet have peace within himself, but was united to Christ with his mind so that his soul would follow him and not trouble him. Then seek peace, brothers. The Lord said: This I have spoken to you so that you may have peace in me. I do not promise you peace on earth. In this life there is no true peace or tranquility. The joy of immortality and the company of angels are promised. But he who has not sought it while he was in this world will not obtain it when it arrives. 20 [v. 16]. The eyes of the Lord on the righteous. Don't be afraid, work; The eyes of the Lord are upon you. And his ears (attentive) to his prayers. What more do you want? If the servant who complains in the big house were not heard by the father of the family, he would lament and say: How many things I endure and no one listens to me! Will you say of God: How much I suffer and no one hears me? If he heard me, perhaps, you say, he would remove the tribulation from me; I cry out, and I am troubled. Remain constantly in his ways, and when you are troubled et tibí ipsi resistís alíquando, et tamen non te hated. Omnis enim quem poenitet aliquid, rixatur secum. Peccavit, redit, irascitur sibimetipsi hoc fecisse, illud commississe. Rixam ergo secum habet, sed ista rixa ad concordiam tendit. Vide quomodo secum rixetur, et dicat quídam iustus: Quare tristis es, anima mea, et quare conturbas me? Spera in Dominum, quoniam adhuc conjitebor Mi (Ps 42,5). Cum dicit animae suae, Quare conturbas me; utique turbabat illum. Volebat forte ipse pati pro Christo, et anima ipsius contristabatur. Et ille qui sciebat et dicebat, Quare tristis es, anima mea, et quare conturbas me; pacem adhuc secum non habebat: sed ex mente haerebat Christo, ut sequeretur illum anima eius, et non illum conturbaret. Ergo quaerite pacem, fratres.

Dominus dixit: Haec loquor vobis, ut in me habeatis pacem. Pacem in terra vobis non promitto (lo 16,33). In this vita pax vera non est, nec tranquilinas. Gaudium immortalitatis, societas Angelorum promittitur. Be quisquís non illam cum hic est quaesierit, non illam habebit cum venerit. 20 [v.16]. Oculi Domini super iustos. Noli ergo timere, labora: oculi Domini super te sunt. Et aures eius ad preces eorum. Quid vis amplius? Si murmurantem servum in domo magna non audiret paterfamilias, quéretur, et diceret: Quanta hic patimur, et nemo nos audit! Numquid dicis illud de Deo: Quanta patior, et nemo me audit? Si audiret me, forte dicis, tolleret mihi tribulationem: clamo, et tributar. So-
Praise of God, protector of the righteous

will hear you. Veque is a doctor and you still have something rotten. You shout, and he continues cutting, and he does not raise his hand until he has cut everything that is necessary. On the contrary, he is a cruel doctor who listens to man and forgives the wound and the gangrene. See how mothers scrub their children in the bathroom, taking care of their health. Don't children cry in their hands? Are they, then, cruel because they do not respect or pay attention to their tears? On the contrary, they are most merciful; However, the children cry and are not forgiven. So also our God is full of love; but it seems that he does not hear us, in order to heal us and forgive us forever. 21 [v. 17]. The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears (are attentive) to their prayers. Perhaps the wicked will say: Therefore I do evil for sure, since the eyes of the Lord are not upon me; God looks only at the righteous, he does not look at me; Whatever I do, I do it for sure. Seeing the thoughts of men, the Holy Spirit immediately adds, saying: The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears (are attentive) to their prayers; but the face of the Lord on those who do evil to erase their memory from the earth. 22 [v. 18]. The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them and brought them out of all their tribulations. The three children were fair. From the furnace they cried out to the Lord, and with their praise the flames cooled. The flame could not approach and burn the innocent and righteous children who were praising God, and God saved them from the flames. Some tum tu teñe vias eius, et quando tribularis audit te. Be mediais est, adhuc putre habes nescio quid. Cryings: sed adhuc secat; et non tollit manum, nisi secuerit quantum videtur. Etenim medicus crudelis est qui exaudit hominem, et parcit vulneri et putredini. Matres quomodo fricant in balneis ad salutem filios? Nonne parvuliclamant inter manus earum? IUae ergo crudeles sunt, ut non parcant, non exaudiant lacrymas? Nonne plenae sunt pietate? Et tamen clamant pueri, et non eis parcitur. Sic et Deus noster plenus est charitate: sed ideo videtur non exaudiré, ut sanet et parcat in sempiternum. 21 [v.17]. Oculi Domini super iustos, et aures eius ad preces eorum. Forte dicunt malí: Ergo securus fació mala, quia non super me sunt oculi Domini: iam Deus ad iustos attendit, me non videt, et quidquid fecero, securus fació.

Statim subiecit videns cogitationes hominum Spiritus sanctus, et ait: Oculi Domini super iustos, et aures eius ad preces eorum: vultus autem Domini super facientes mala, ut perdat de tetra memoriam eorum. 22 [v.18]. Clamaverunt iusti, et Dominus exaudivit eos, et ex omnibus tribulationibus eorum eruit eos. Iusti were three pueri: on the way he clamaverunt ad Dominum, et in laudibus eorum ignes friguerunt. Accederé et laedere flamma non potuit laudantes Deum innocentes et iustos pueros, et eruit eos de flamma (Dan 3,49). Dicit aliquis, Ecce veré iusti
Ennarrations on the Psalms

will say: See here the truly righteous, who were heard, as it is written: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them and delivered them from all their tribulations. But I cried and he did not deliver me. Therefore, either I am not fair, or I do not do what he tells me, or perhaps he does not see me. Do not be afraid, do what he commands, and if he does not save you in your body, he will save you in your soul. Did He who freed the three children from the flames free the Maccabees from the flames? Didn't these also sing hymns among the flames and expire among them? Isn't the God of the three children also the same God of the Maccabees? He delivered those, not these. What do I say? He delivered both: he delivered the three children in such a way that he confused the carnal ones; He did not spare the Maccabees in this way, so that those who persecuted them would fall into greater torture when they judged that they were killing the martyrs of God. He delivered Peter when, while he was in prison, the angel came to him and said, “Get up and come out,” and immediately the bonds were loosed and he followed the angel and delivered him. Had Peter lost grace when he did not deliver him from the cross? Did he not also free him then? Certainly yes. Or did he live a long time to become perverse? Perhaps he heard him more perfectly afterwards, when he truly delivered him from all afflictions, than before. For when he first delivered him, how many things did he not suffer afterwards! And yet, lastly, he sent him where he cannot suffer any evil. 23 [v.19-20]. The Lord is near to those who break their hearts, and will save those who are humble in spirit. Excelso is qui exauditi sunt, sicut scriptum est, Clamaverunt iusti, et Dominus exaudivit eos, et ex ómnibus tribulationibus eorum eruit eos: ego autem clamaví, et non me eruit: aut ego non sum iustus, aut non fació quae mihi iubet, aut forte me ille non videt. Noli timere, tantum fac quod iubet; et si te non eruit corporaliter, eruet spiritualiter. Ule enim qui tulit de flamma tres pueros, numquid tulit de flamma Machabaeos? None illi in ignibus hymnizabant, illi in ignibus exspirabant? (2 Mach 6.3). Deus trium puerorum, nonne ipse est et Machabaeorum? Illos eruit, et illos non eruit; imo utrosque eruit: sed tres pueros sic eruit, ut et carnales confunderentur; Machabaeos autem ideo non sic eruit, ut illi qui persequebantur in poenas maiores irent, cum putabant se oppressisse martyres Dei.

Eruit Petrum, quando venit ad illum angelus, cum esset in vinculis, et ait illi, Surge, et exi: et súbito soluta sunt liga, et secutus est angelum, et eruit illum (Act 12,7). Numquid Petras perdiderat iustitiam, quando non illum eruit de crossing? Non eruit tune? Et eruit tune. An ideo diu vixit, ut iniustus ieront? Forte plus eum exaudivit postea quam prius, quando illum veré de omnibus pressuris eruit. Nam quando primum illum eruit, quanta ille pertulit postea! Illuc enim misit postea, ubi nihil mali pati potuisset. 23 [v.19.20]. luxla est Dominus his qui obtriverunt cor, et humiles ípirilu safes faciet. Altus est Deus, humilis sit christianus. Yes vult ut

33 S.2 Praise of God, protector of the just God; Let the Christian be humble. If you want the exalted God to come close to you, be humble. Great mystery, brothers. God is above all things; you get conceited, and you don't touch him; you humble yourself, and He comes down to you. Many are the tribulations of the righteous. Does the Lord say: Let the Christians be righteous, hear my word, that they may not suffer any tribulation? He does not promise this, but says: Many are the tribulations of the righteous. Rather, the unjust endure fewer tribulations than the just; but after few or none they will come to the everlasting tribulation, from where they will never emerge. On the contrary, the righteous, after many anguish, will reach eternal peace, where they will never endure any evil. Many are the tribulations of the righteous, and the Lord will deliver them from all of them. 24 [v.21}. The Lord preserves all their bones, not one of them will be broken. Brothers, let's not take this carnally. The bones are the foundations of the faithful. As in our body the bones constitute the framework, so in the heart of the Christian faith constitutes the foundation. The constancy that exists in faith is the internal bones. These are the ones that cannot be broken. The Lord preserves all their bones, not one of them will be broken. If he had said this referring to our Lord Jesus Christ, he would say: The Lord preserves all the bones of his Son, not one of these will be broken; Just as in another place, when the sacrifice of the lamb was ordered, it was said of him in foreshadowing: No bone of him will be broken, and it was fulfilled in the Lord, since when he was hanging from the cross, those in charge of breaking the legs having expired before reaching it, upon seeing the altus Deus vicinetur illi, ille humilis sit. Magna mysteria, brothers. Deus super omnia est: erigis te, et non illum tangís: humilias te, et ipse ad te descendit. Multae tribulationes iustorum. Numquid dicit: Ideo sint Christiani iusti, ideo audiant verbum meum, ut nihil íribulationis patiantur? Non hoc promittit; sed dicit: Multae tribulationes iustorum. Magis si iniusti sunt, pauciores habent tribulationes; If iusti sunt, fines habent. Sed post paucas tribulationes aut nullas, illi venient ad tríbulationem sempitemam, unde nunquam eruantur: iusti autem post fines tribulationes venient ad pacem sempitemam, ubi nunquam aliquid mali patientur. Multae tribulationes iustorum: et de omnibus his eruet eos Dominus. 24 [v.21].

Custodit Dominus omnia ossa eorum, unum ex his non conteretur. Et hoc, fratres, non accipiamus carnaliter. Ossa sunt firmamenta fidelium. Quomodo enim in carne nostra ossa faciunt firmamentum, sic in corde christiano fides facit firmamentum. Patientia ergo quae est in fide, ossa sunt interius. Ipsa sunt quae frangi non possunt. Custodit Dominus omnia ossa eorum, unum ex his non conteretur. Si de Domino Deo nostro Iesu Christo dixisset hoc, Custodit Dominus omnia ossa Filii sui, unum ex his non conteretur: sicut etiam alio loco praefiguratur de illo, quando agnus dictus est mactandus, et dictum est de illo, Os eius noli frángete (Ex 12,46): impletum est in Domino; quia cum penderet in cruz, exspiravit antequam comerent illi ad cruzem, et invenerunt iam
Ennarrations on the Psalms

lifeless body they did not want to break them, thus fulfilling what was written. But what was now said: The Lord keeps their bones, not one of these will be broken, was promised to all Christians. Therefore, brothers, if we saw a saint suffer tribulations, and perhaps be cut by the doctor or killed by some persecutor who broke his bones, let us not say: This one was not righteous, because the Lord promised this to his righteous ones, since it is said of them: The Lord preserves all their bones; not one of these will be broken. Do you want to see that he spoke only of the bones that we call the foundation of faith, that is, of patience and tolerance in all tribulations? Pay attention and you will see in the Lord's own passion what I say. The Lord was crucified between two thieves: one insulted him, the other believed; one was condemned, the other justified; one had his punishment here and in the future century; To the other the Lord said: Truly I say to you, today you will be with me in paradise; and yet those who approached did not break the bones of the Lord, but those of the thieves. In the same way the bones of the thief who blasphemed were broken as those of the thief who believed. Then how was what was said fulfilled: The Lord preserves all the bones of the righteous; not one of them will be bankrupt? How is it that he to whom he said: Today you will be with me in paradise, could he not save all his bones? The Lord answers you: I kept them in a special way, because the blows by which their legs were broken could not break the foundation of their faith.

Corpus exanime, et noluerunt crura eius frangere, ut impleretur quod scriptum est (lo 19,33). Sed promisit illud et caeteris Christianis: Dominus custodit omnia ossa eorum, unum ex bis non conteretur. Ergo fratres, si viderimus aliquem sanctum tribulationes pati, et forte vel a medico sic secari, vel ab aliquo persecutor sic caedi, ut eius ossa frangantur; non dicamus, Non erat iustus iste, nam Dominus hoc promisit iustis suis, de quibus ait: Custodit Dominus omnia ossa eorum, unum ex bis non conteretur. Vis videre quia allia ossa dixit, quae diximus firmamenta fidei, id est patientiam et tolerantiam in omnibus tribulationibus? Ipsa enim sunt ossa quae non franguntur. Audite, et in ipsa passione Domini inspicite quod dico. Dominus erat in medio crucifixus; iuxta illum duo latrones erant: unus insultavit, alter credidit; unus damnatus est, alter iustificatus est; unus habuit poenam suam et hic et in futurum, alteri autem dixit Dominus: Amen dico tibi, hodie mecum eris in paradiso (Luke 23:43): et tamen illi qui venerant, Domini ossa non fregerunt, latronum autem fregerunt (lo 19:32): sic fracta sunt latronis ossa qui blasphemavit, quomodo latronis qui credit. Ubi est ergo quod dictum est, Dominus custodit omnia ossa eorum, unum ex bis non conteretur? Ecce cui dixit, hodie mecum eris in paradise, non potuit omnia ossa eius custodire? Respondet tibi Dominus: Imo custodivi; nam firmamentum fidei ipsius frangí non potuit illis ictibus quibus crura sunt fracta.
Praise of God, protector of the righteous

25 [v. 22. 23]. The death of sinners is terrible. Pay attention, brothers, and consider those things that we said. Indeed, the Lord is exalted, and great is his mercy; He gave us his body to eat, in which he endured so much labor. Already drink his blood. Observe how he contemplates those who think evil and say: That one died badly because he was devoured by beasts; He was not fair, and that is why he perished badly; If he had been just, he would not have perished like this. Therefore, is he just who dies in his house and in his bed? This is what admires me, you say, because I knew his sins and his crimes, and yet he died well, he died in his house, in his home, without the shame of a pilgrim at an advanced age. Listen: The death of sinners is terrible. What seemed like a good death to you is terrible if you consider it in reality. You see him who lies on the bed; but do you see that the spirit was taken to hell? Hear, brothers, and observe from the Gospel that the death of sinners is terrible. Did not two live in this world: a rich one, who dressed in purple and fine linen and who ate richly every day, and another poor man, who lay ulcerated prostrate at his doors and the dogs came to lick his ulcers, and who wanted to be satisfied with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table? It came to pass that the poor man, who was righteous, died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom. Anyone who saw his body lying on the threshold of the rich man's door, having no one to bury him, how many things would he perhaps not say? Even if my enemy dies and whoever persecutes me, even if my eyes see him. The body is detested for its rottenness; wounds shed 25 [v.22.23}. Mors peccatorum pessima. Attendite, fratres, propter illa quae dicebamus. I will see magnus Dominus, et misericordia eius, I will see qui nobis dedit manducare Corpus suum in quo tanta perpessus est, et sanguinem bibere. Quomodo respicit mala cogitantes, et dicentes: Ule male mortuus est, a bestiis consumptus est: non erat ille iustus, ideo male periit; nam non periret? Ergo ille iustus est, qui in domo sua et in lecto' suo moritur? Hoc est ergo, inquis, quod miror, quia novi peccata et scelera ipsius, et bene mortuus est, in domo sua, intra limina sua, nulla peregrinationis iniuria, nulla vel in matura aetate. Audi: Mors peccatorum pessima.

And those who hated, he says, the righteous, will perish. Who is righteous if not the one who justifies the wicked? Who is righteous if not our Lord Jesus Christ, who is also the propitiation for our sins? Then those who hate him die a terrible death, because they die in their own sins, since they are not reconciled with God through him. The Lord redeems the souls of his servants. It must be understood that death is good or bad considering the soul, not the outrages or honors of the body that men contemplate. And not all who hope in Him will perish. This is the norm of human goodness: to advance in perfection as much as possible in mortal life, and since one cannot go without sin, do not fail in this, to wait for the forgiveness of sins in Him in whom is found. It is, therefore, a psalm for him with a strong and desirable hand who conquered our death and promised us life. It is strong-handed, because it conquered our death, and desirable, because it promised eternal life. What is stronger than this hand that touches the coffin and resurrects the dead? What is more powerful than this hand that conquers the world without being armed with iron, but nailed to the wood? What could be more desirable than Him, whom, not seeing Him, the martyrs wanted to die to deserve to reach Him? 2 [v.11.12]. So let our Head say: Wicked witnesses stood up and asked me what I did not know. Let us say to our Head: Lord, what were you unaware of? Did you ignore something? Did you not know the hearts of those who questioned you? Did you not have his perfidy before your eyes? Hadn't you knowingly given yourself into his hands? Hadn't you come to suffer for them? What were you ignoring? He did not know the sin, he ignored it, not so as not to judge it, but to commit it. Such locutions are frequent

chasms and daily, for example when you say of someone: I do not know that he remains; that is, it does not remain. I don't know what it does well; That is, it does not. I don't know that he does wrong; that is, it does not. What is foreign to the work is foreign to consciousness, and what is far from consciousness seems to be far from intelligence or knowledge. Thus it is said that God ignores, in the same way that art ignores vice or deformity, and yet, known things are judged by art. Then our Head, by the truth of his own Gospel, to us, who question him when we say: Lord, what were you unaware? What could you have been questioned about that you did not know?, he answers us: He was unaware of iniquities; about iniquities I was questioned. If you do not believe that I was ignorant of iniquities, read the Gospel and you will see that I do not know the wicked, to whom at the end of the world I will say: I do not know you, depart from me, you who have done iniquity. We know, brothers, that we belong to the body of Christ, and that we are its members, and that we are warned in all our tribulation; first, not to think about how we should respond to our enemies, but about how we should appease God, and above all not to be defeated in temptation; then, to direct those who persecute us to the health of justice. There is no greater work, no better occupation in tribulation than to get away from that bustle, which is outside, and go inside the chamber of the mind and invoke God where no one sees the one who groans and the one who helps; how to close the door of that enclosure to all annoyance coming from outside, how to humble oneself with the confession of sins and praise and magnify God, who corrects and consoles; which in any case must be attempted. We have said this referring to the body, that is, to nostem, ipsi retribuebant sterilitatem; ego vitam, ipsi mortem; ego honorem, ipsi contumelias: ego medicinem, ipsi vulnera; et in hic omnibus quae retribuebant, utique sterilitas erat. others. Concerning our Lord Jesus Christ, what similar thing do we know? Diligently reviewing and investigating the Gospel, we do not find that the Lord had put on sackcloth in any suffering or tribulation that He suffered. We read that he fasted after his baptism; that he dressed there in sackcloth, we have never heard or read. Furthermore, he fasted when the Jews were not yet persecuting him, but when the devil tempted him. I am not saying that the Lord fasted at the time when they asked him what he did not know and they returned evils for good, harassing him, persecuting him, arresting him, whipping him, wounding him and killing him; but, nevertheless, brothers, if in all these circumstances we lift the veil a little with pious curiosity and search with the keen eye of the heart the secrets of the Scripture, we will find that the Lord also fasted then. Perhaps he calls the mortality of his flesh a sackcloth. Why do you call her that? Because of the likeness of sinful flesh. The Apostle says: God sent his Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, to condemn sin in the flesh for sin; That is, he dressed his Son in sackcloth to condemn the goats with sackcloth. Not because he had sin, I do not mean the Word of God, but not the same holy soul and mind of the man to whom the Word and Wisdom of God had united in unity of person; Furthermore, not even the body itself had any sin, but only the likeness of sinful flesh existed in the Lord, and since death comes from sin, that body was certainly mortal. If he had not been mortal, he would not have died, and if he had not died, he would not have been resurrected, and if he had not been resurrected, we are not moda tenendum est. The Lord clothed himself with this sackcloth, and was not known because he was hidden under the sackcloth. When they bothered me, he says, I dressed in sackcloth; That is to say, they were angry, I hid. If he had not wanted to hide, he would not have been able to die, since in a single moment he gave expression to a bit of his power, if you can say a bit, when they wanted to arrest him, and to a question from him: Who are you looking for?, everyone retreated and fell.
