4. I clothed myself in sackcloth and cast down my soul with fasting. We have understood the sackcloth, how do we understand fasting? Christ wanted to eat when he looked for figs on the fig tree; but would he have eaten if he had found figs in it? Did Christ want to drink when he said to the Samaritan woman: Give me a drink, and when he said on the cross: I am thirsty? What did Christ hunger for, what did Christ thirst for, but for our good works? He fasted on those who crucified him and persecuted him, because he found no good work in them: they returned sterility to his soul. How great was the fast of him who barely found a single thief whom he liked or ate on the cross! The apostles had fled and were hiding among the crowd. And that Peter who promised to persevere until the death of the Lord, had already denied Him three times, was already crying, and was still hiding among the crowd, he was still afraid of being known. Finally, seeing him dead, everyone distrusted his health, and he found them distrustful after the resurrection, and speaking with them he found them sad and crying, no longer expecting anything; For this is how some of them were who spoke with Him when He said to them: What things do you talk among yourselves?, since they, speaking about Him, say: You are just a stranger in Jerusalem, and you did not know the things that our princes and priests did with Jesus of the Nazarene, who was a powerful man in deeds and words, and how they crucified and killed him? We, in truth, hoped that He would be the one who would redeem Israel. The Lord would have remained in a great fast if he had not encouraged those who were to eat. He revived them, consoled them, confirmed them

He cuts so that it heals, and yet, when he cuts the sick person, he feels pain, screams, resists, and if by chance he lost consciousness due to fever, he hurts the doctor; However, he does not give up looking after the health of the sick person, he does not worry about that curser and abuser. Those who are in a state of lethargy are revived, those who are frantic are tied up; however, they are both loved. Let no one say: I suffer persecution. 14 [v.24-26}. Judge me, Lord, according to my justice. That is, according to my cause. Not just one man says it, it is said by the entire group of perverse men who oppose themselves by not wanting to understand so as not to live well; not because they can't, but because they don't want to. It is one thing not to understand when someone tries and cannot because of the weakness of the flesh, as the Scripture says in a certain place: The corruptible body depresses the soul, and the earthly dwelling weighs down the mind that thinks many things, and another is not to understand when the human heart acts perniciously against itself; so that what he could understand if he had good will, he does not understand, not because it is difficult, but because there is an opposite will. This he does when he loves his sins and hates the precepts of God. The word of God is your adversary, if you are a friend of your perversity. On the contrary, if you oppose your iniquity, the word of God is your friend, and adversary of your iniquity. Then if you hated your iniquity, you join yourself to the word of God, and thus there will be two of you who fight against it to annihilate it: you and the word of God. You, by your own strength, can do nothing, but he who gave you his word helps you, and in this way iniquity is defeated. When he notices that it is a sin and desists from committing the sin, because he committed it out of ignorance; then he certainly pretended to know iniquity in order to hate it when he encountered it. Quia sunt homines qui volunt intelligere, et non possunt; sunt autem homines qui nolunt intelligere, ideo non intelligunt. Noluit intelligere ut bene ageret. 5 [v.5]. Iniquitatem meditatus is in cubili suo. Quid dixit, in lair! suo?

Dixit iniustus, ut delinquat in semetipso: quod dixit superius, in semetipso; hoc hic dixit, in cubili suo. Cubile nostrum est cor nostrum: ibi tumultum patimur malae conscienriae: et ibi requiescimus, quando bona conscientia est. Qui amat cubile cordis sui, aliquid boni ibi agat. Ibi est cubile, ubi nos Dominus Iesus Christus iubet orare: lntra in cubiculum tuum, et claude ostium tuum. Quid est, claude ostium tuum? Noli talia exspectare de Deo, quae forinsecus sunt; sed ea quae intrinsecus sunt; Ut Pater tuus, qui videt in abscondito, reddet tibi (Mt 6,6).
Goodness of God and evil of the wicked

found outside, but those that are within: And your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you. Who is the one who doesn't close the door? He who, in order to receive the things that are good in the eyes of the world, asks God for such things as a great benefit and bases all his supplications on that. Then the door is open; The mob sees when you pray. What does closing your door consist of? In asking God for what only God knows how to give you. What is it that you close the door and ask for? What the eye did not see, nor the ear hear, nor did the heart of man glimpse. And perhaps it was not even glimpsed in your enclosure, that is, in your heart. But God knows what he will give you. When will this take place? When the Lord appears, when the judge appears. What is more obvious than what must be said to those placed on the right? Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the beginning of the world. Those on the left will hear these words and groan with sterile penitence, because, living freely, they did not want to act profitably. Why will they moan? Because there is no room for correction anymore. They will also hear the same: Go to the eternal game that was prepared for the devil and his angels. This is the bad ad. But the righteous will rejoice at the good news, for thus it is written: The righteous will live in eternal memory and will not fear the bad news. What bad announcement is there not to fear? The one that must be heard by those to whom it is said: Go to the eternal game. Therefore God, who can do in excess of what we ask or understand, desires our hidden groaning, Quis est qui non claudit ostium? Qui talia petit a Deo pro magno et ibi constituit omnes preces suas, ut accipiat ea quae sunt huius saeculi bona. Patet ostium tuum, peat videt cum oras. Quid est claudere ostium tuum? Ut hoc petas a Deo, quod solus Deus novit quomodo tibi det. Quid est hoc propter quod claudis ostium, et petis? Quod oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascendit (Is 64:4; 1 Cor 2:9). Et forte non ascendit in ipsum cubile tuum, id est in cor tuum. Sed Deus novit quid tibi daturus est. When autem erit? Quando revelabitur Dominus, quando apparebit iudex. Quid enim manifestius quam quod dicturus est ad dexteram positis? Come, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnttm quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi (Mt 25,34).

Audient haec illi qui ad sinistram erunt, et gement infructuosa poenitentia (Sap 5,3); Quia cum ita viverent, eam fructuose noluerunt agere. “How do I moan?” Quia non est illis locus correctionis. Audient autem et ipsi: he in ignem aeternum qui paratus est iiabolo et angelis eius (Mt 25,41). This is auditus malus. Nam iusti ad auditum bonum gaudebunt; sic enim scriptum est: ln memoria aeterna erit tustús, ab auditoru malo non timebit (Ps 111,7). What bad audit? Quem audituri sunt illi, he in ignem aeternum. Deus ergo qui potest supra quam petimus aut intelligimus faceré (Eph 3,20), oceultum gemitum nostrum quaerit, ut in conspectu eius placeamus, et non nos quasi de iustitia nostra ante homines iactemus. Who enim of
Ennarrations on the Psalms

so that we may please him in his presence and not boast of our righteousness before men. He who intends to please men with his justice, not so that the men who see him praise God, but with the intention of being praised, does not close the door to escape the noise, since he leaves the door open to noise, and then God does not hear as he wants to hear. Let us work to clean the space of our heart, so that it can be comfortable for us. Your charity knows how much many suffer publicly in the courts, in dissensions, in disputes, in the entanglements of business; Your charity also knows how everyone who is fatigued by the affairs of the forum goes to his house to rest there, and, therefore, quickly puts an end to the affairs that occupy him in the forum and retires to the rest of his house. Everyone has their home where they can rest. But if you find discomfort there, where can you rest? So what will I say? That it is a good thing that, with everything, he finds rest at home. Maybe he endures enemies outside, and inside, a bad woman; goes out into the street. When he wants to rest from those outside discomforts, he enters the house; but when he does not rest here or abroad, where will he find rest? Enter, at least, into the space of your heart, in order to penetrate the depths of your conscience. And if there by chance you found the excellent wife who does not give you troubles, that is, the wisdom of God, join her, rest internally in your room; from there the stench of a bad conscience will not cast you off. On the contrary, he who, in order to deceive, departed from the place of which the Scripture says

iustitia sua placeré vult hominibus, non eo fine ut homines qui eum vident Deum laudent, sed ea intentione ut ipse laudetur, non claudit ostium contra strepitum: quia patet ostium illo strepitu, et non audit Deus quomodo audire vult. Cubile ergo cor nostrum laboremus mundare, ubi possit nobis bene esse. Novit Charitas Vestra quam fines multi patiuntur in publico, in foro, in iurgiis, in contentionibus, in molestiis negotiorum: quomodo quisque fatiguetus negotiis foris, currit ad domum suam ut ibi requiescat, et dat operam cyto finiré negotia quae foris sunt, et tollere se ad réquiem in domum suam. Ideo enim unusquisque domum suam habet, quia ibi requiescit. Si vero et ibi discomfort patiatur, ubi potest requiescere? Quid ergo? Bonum est ut vel in domo sua requiem habeat. Si autem patitur foris inimicos, intus forte malam uxorem; proceedit in publicum: cum vult requiescere ab his quae foris sunt, intrat in domum: quando vero nec ibi requiescit, nec foris requiescit, ubi erit requies? Saltem in cubicle cordis, ut tollas te ad interiora conscientiae tuae. Si ibi invenisti forte coniugem, quae tibi non facial amaritudinem, sapientiam Dei; cum ipsa coniungere, quiesce intus in cubicle tuo, non inde te eiiciat fumus malae conscientiae. At ille ut meditaretur dolos, illuc se tollebat, de quo loquitur ista Scriptura, ubi homines non vident; et
Goodness of God and evil of the wicked

which men do not see, and he pondered such things there that he did not rest in his heart, he meditated on iniquity in his chamber. 6. He stopped at every bad road. What does stopped mean? He sinned insistently. Hence it is also said of a certain good and pious man: And he did not stand in the way of sinners. Just as this one did not stop, so did that one stop. And he hated no evil. Here we have the end and the fruit, if not it can pass without malice or, at least, hate it. When you hate it, it can barely enter to drag you into some evil. Certainly sin exists in the mortal body; but what does the Apostle say? Let not sin reign in your mortal body, so that it obeys its appetites. When does it begin to not exist? When what is written is fulfilled in us: When this corruptible has put on incorruption, and this mortal has put on immortality. Before this happens, there is the delight of iniquity in the body; but greater is the delight of the pleasure of the word of wisdom, that is, of the precept of God. Turn, then, to sin and its desire. You must hate sin and iniquity to unite with God, who hates him with you. If with your mind you are united to the law of God, you already serve the law of God with it, even though now with the flesh you serve the law of sin. Now there are certain carnal delights in you; then there will be none when you no longer fight. It is one thing not to fight and be in true and perpetual peace, and another to fight and win, and another to fight and be defeated, and another not to fight, but to be carried away. There are men who do not fight at all, as happens with this one who is spoken of when saying: talia ibi meditabatur, ut nec in ipso corde requiesceret. Iniquiíatem meditatus est in cubili suo. 6. Astitit omni viae non bonae. What is it, astitit? Perseveranter peccavit. Undc et de quodam pió et bono dicitur: Et in via peccatorum non stetit (Ps 1,1). Quomodo ille non stetit, sic iste astitit. Malitiam autem non odio habuit. Ibi est finis, ibi fructus: si non potest non habere malitiam, vel oderit illam. Cum enim odisti illam, vix tibi surepit ut aliquid mali facías. Est enim peccatum in mortali corpore: sed quid dicit Apostolus? Non regnet peccatum in vestro mortali corpore, ad obediendum desideriis eius (Rom 6:12). When does ncipit non esse?

Quando complebitur in nobis quod ait: Cum corruptibile hoc induerit incorruptionem, et moríale hoc induerit immortalitatem (1 Cor 15:53). Antequam hoc fiar, est delectatio iniquitatis in corpore; sed maior est delectado voluptatis verbi sapientiae, praecepti Dei. Vince peccatum et voluntatem eius. Peccatum et ¡niquitatem oderis, ut iungas te Deo qui tecum illud oderit. Iam coniunctus mente legi Dei, mente servís legi Dei. Et si carne propterea servis legi peccati (Rom 7:25), quia sunt in te delectationes quaedam carnales, tune nullae erunt quando iam non pugnabis. Aliud est non pugnare, et esse in pace vera atque perpetua, aliud pugnare et vincere; aliud pugnare et vinci; aliud nec pugnare, sed trahi. Sunt enim homines prorsus qui non pugnant, qualis est iste de quo loquitur: cum enim dicit, Malitiam
Ennarrations on the Psalms

And he did not hate malice. How do you fight against it, if you don't hate it? He is carried away by malice and does not fight. There are others who begin to fight; But, as they boast of their strength, to show God that He is the one who conquers, if man submits to Him, and that by fighting they are defeated, when they begin to possess justice they become arrogant and crash. They fight, but are defeated. Who is the one who fights and is not defeated? He who says: I see another law in my members that is opposed to the law of my mind. He sees another law that opposes it, but this one does not presume his strength; That's why he wins. How does it continue? Unhappy man I, who will free me from this body of death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord. He boasts of the one who orders him to fight, and defeats the enemy helped by the commander. But this one we speak of now did not hate malice. 7 [v. 6]. Lord, your mercy (is) in heaven, and your truth (reaches) to the clouds. I don't know what mercy he speaks of when he says he is in heaven. For the mercy of God is on the earth, as it is written: The earth is full of the mercy of God. What mercy is spoken of when it says: Lord, your mercy (is) in heaven? The gifts of God are partly earthly and temporal, partly heavenly and eternal. Whoever worships God in order to receive these earthly and temporal goods, which are granted to everyone, is still like an animal; He enjoys the mercy of God, but not that singular mercy that is only given to the just, holy and good. What are the goods with which they are all filled? I don't hate habit; Qumodo fight against eam quam non odit? Iste a malitia trahitur, nec pugnat. Sunt autem qui pugnare incipiunt; sed quia de viribus suis praesumunt, ut ostendat illis Deus quia ipse vincit, si se homo subiungit Deo, et pugnantes vincuntur, et cum quasi coeperint tenere iustitiam, fiunt superbi, et eliduntur. Isti pugnant, sed vincuntur. Quis est autem qui pugnat, et non vincitur? Qui dicit: Video aliam le geni in membris meis repugnantem legi mentís meae. Vide pugnantem: sed non de viribus suis praesumit iste, ideo victor erit. Quid enim sequitur? Infelix ego homo, quis liberate me from corpore mortis huius? Gratia Dei per lesum Christum Dominum nostrum (Rom 7:23-25). Praesumit de eo qui iussit ut pugnet, et vincit hostem adiutus a iubente.

This autem malitiam non odio habuit. 7 [v.6]. Domine, in cáelo misericordia tua, et veritas tua usque ad clouds. Nescio quam misericordiam ipsius dicit, quae in cáelo est. Est enim mercy Domini et in terra. Habes scriptum: Misericordia Domini plena est terra (Ps 32,5). De qua ergo misericordia loquitur, cum dicit: Domine, in cáelo misericordia tua? Doll Dei partim temporalia sunt atque terrena, partim aeterna et caelestia: qui propter hoc colit Deum, ut terrena ista atque temporalia accipiat, quae omnibus praesto sunt, quasi adhuc ut pecus est; utitur quidem misericordia Dei, sed non illa quae excepta est, quae non dabitur nisi solis iustis, sanctis, bonis. Quae sunt doll quae bus abundant? Qui solem suum oriri facit super bonds
Goodness of God and evil of the wicked

Those offered by the one who makes his sun rise on the good and the bad and rains on the just and the sinners. Who does not possess this mercy of God: for example, firstly, existence, being distinguished from other animals, being a rational animal, being able to know God, and secondly, enjoying this light, this air, the fruits, the diversity of times, earthly satisfactions, the health of the body, the affection of friends and the well-being of the home? All these things are goods and gifts from God. Do not think, brothers, that anyone can give them apart from God. Therefore, anyone who does not expect them from another, but only from God, differs greatly from these and from those who obtain them from demons, or from spellcasters, or from astrologers. These are unfortunate in two different ways: because they not only desire earthly goods, but also because they do not ask for them from him who gives all goods. Those who long for these goods and intend to be happy with them and only ask for these from God, are undoubtedly better, since they ask for them from God, but they are still in danger. Why, some will say, are they in danger? Because sometimes, when considering human things and seeing that all these earthly things, which they desire, the impious and wicked have and abound in them, they think that they have lost the reward of worshiping God, since they have what the wicked also have, while they worship the God that they do not worship, or it also happens other times that those who worship do not have them, and those who blaspheme have them. Then they are still in danger. 8. Here he clearly made known the mercy that God asks for. By saying: Lord, your mercy (is) in heaven, and your et evils, et pluit super iustos et unjust (Mt 5,45). Quis non habet istam misericordiam Dei, primo ut sit, ut discernatur a pecoribus, ut rationale sit animal, qui possit Deum intelligere, deinde frui ista luz, isto aere, pluvia, fructibus, diversitate temporum, solatiis terrenis, salute corporis, affectu amicorum, salute domus suae? Omnia is bona sunt, et Dei muñera sunt. Ne putetis, fratres, quod aliquis illa poterit daré, nisi unus Deus. Quicumque ergo non exspectant ista, nisi a Domino, multum interest inter hos et eos qui illa quaerunt aut a daemonibus, aut a sortilegis, aut a mathematicis.

Isti enim duobus modis miseri sunt, quia et terrena sola bona desiderant, et non ab eo petunt qui dat omnia bona. Qui vero is this bona desiderant, et in his bonis tristes esse volunt, et ista sola petunt a Deo, hoc quidem meliores sunt, quia a Deo petunt; sed adhuc periclitantur. Dicit aliquis: Quare periclitantur? Aliquando enim considering human rights, et vident ista omnia bona terrena, quae desiderant, habere atque abundare impíos et iniquos, et putant quia perdiderunt mercedem colendi Deum, quia id quod mali habent, et ipsi habent, cum ipsi colant Deum, quem non colunt illi; aut aliquando illi qui colunt non habent, et illi habent qui blasphemant: ergo in periculo sunt adhuc. 8. Hic autem veré intellexit quam misericordiam deprecetur a Deo. Domine, in cáelo your mercy, et veritas tua usque ad clouds: id est,
^.narratives about the Psalms

truth (reaches) to the clouds, you manifest that a certain mercy that you give to your saints is heavenly, not earthly; It is eternal, not temporary. How then could you announce it to men? Because your truth (reaches) to the clouds. Who could have known the heavenly mercy of God if Goddess had not announced it to men? How did you announce it? Sending your truth to the clouds. What clouds are these? The preachers of the word of God. Hence, in a certain place, God was angry with a certain vineyard. As soon as I believe, your charity will understand that I am referring to the prophet Isaiah, who says of a certain vineyard: I expected it to produce grapes, and it produced thorns. And lest anyone think that he was speaking of these visible vineyards, he concludes thus: The vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the man Judas is a beloved vineyard, just planted. Then he harshly rebukes the same vineyard that he expected to produce grapes and produced thorns. And what does it say? I will command my clouds not to rain on it; and truly so it happened. The apostles were sent to it to preach, since we read in the Apostolic Acts that Saint Paul wanted to preach to the Jews and did not find grapes there, but thorns, since they began to return evils for good and to persecute him, and, therefore, as in fulfillment of what was written: I will command my clouds not to rain on it, he says: To you we were sent; But because you rejected the word of God, behold, we have turned to the Gentiles. Then it was fulfilled: I will command my clouds not to rain on her. The truth reached the clouds, and that is why God's mercy could be announced to us, mercy quaedam quam donas sanctis tuis, caelestis est, non terrena; aeterna est, temporalis non est. Et quomodo illam potuisti annuntiare hominibus? Quia veritas tua usque ad clouds. Nam quis posset nosse caelestem misericordiam Dei, nisi annutiaret Deus hominibus? Quomodo illam annuntiavit? Mittendo veritatem suam usque ad clouds. What sunt clouds? Praedicatores verbi Dei. Unde quodam loco Deus iratus est carem vineae. Intelligit enim, quantum puto, Charitas Vestra, audivit Isaiam prophetam, ubi dicit de quadam vinea: Exspectavi ut jaceret uvam, fecit autem ¡pinas.

Et ne quis putaret de vinea ista visibili dicere, sic conclusit: Vinea autem Domini Sabaoth, domus Israel est; et homo luda, novellum dilectum. Ergo ipsam vineam increpabat, quam exspectavít ut faceret uvam, fecít autem spinas. Et quid ait? Mandabo nubibus meis ne pluant super eam. Iratus Deus hoc dixit: Mandabo nubibus meis, ne pluant super eam (Is 5,4.6.7); et veré factum est. Missi sunt enim praedicatores Apostoli. Sic habemus in Actibus Apostolorum, quia apostolus Paulus volebat praedicare Iudaeis, et invenit ibi non uvam, sed spinas: coeperunt enim pro bonis mala reddere, et persequi. Et ait, tanquam implens quod dictum est, Mandabo nubibus meis ne pluant super eam: Ad vos missi eramus, sed quia respuistis Verbum Dei, ecce convertimur ad Gentes (Act 13,46). Ergo impletum est, Mandabo nubibus meis ne pluant super eam. Usque ad clouds veritas venit: ideo nobis potuit nuntiari mercy Dei quae in
Roundness of God and evil of the wicked

that resides in heaven and not on earth. Truly, brothers, the clouds are the preachers of the word of truth. When God threatens through preachers, He thunders through the clouds. When God works miracles through preachers, he lightnings through the clouds, terrifies through the clouds, and waters through the rain. Therefore these preachers by whom the Gospel of God is announced are clouds of God. Let us wait for mercy, but that which is in heaven. 9 [v. 7]. Your righteousness is like the mountains of God, and your judgments are like the deep abyss. Who are the mountains of God? Those that are called clouds, these same ones are also mountains of God; Therefore the great preachers are the mountains of God. Just as, when the sun rises, it first floods the mountains with light and from there the light descends to the earthly valleys, so when our Lord Jesus Christ came he first illuminated the apostolic peaks; That is, in the first place it illuminated the mountains and from there its light descended into the earthly valley. This is why the psalmist says in a certain place: I lift up my eyes to the mountains, from where help comes to me. But do not think that the mountains themselves will give you help; they receive what you give; Therefore, they do not give of their own. What's more, if you stayed in the mountains, your hope would not be firm. Your hope and your firmness must be based on him who illuminates the mountains. Surely help comes to you from the mountains; Through the great preachers of the truth the holy Scriptures are given to you, but do not fix your hope in them. Or and what is said below: I lifted up my eyes to the mountains, from where help comes to me. cáelo est, et non in terra. Et revera, fratres, clouds sunt praedicatores verbi veritatis. When minatur per praedicatores Deus, tonat per clouds. When miracula facit per praedicatores Deus, coruscat per clouds, terret per clouds, et irrigat per pluviam. Praedicatores ergo isti, per quos praedicatur Evangelium Dei, clouds Dei sunt. Speremus ergo misericordiam, sed illam quae in cáelo est. 9 [v-7j. Justitia tua sicut montes Dei: iudicia tua sicut abyssus Fine. Who sunt montes Dei? Qui dicti sunt clouds, ipsi sunt et montes Dei: magni praedicatores, montes Dei.

Et quomodo, quando oritur sol, prius luz montes vestit, et inde lux ad humilima terrarum descendit: sic quando venit Dominus noster Iesus Christus, prius radiavit in altitudinem Apostolorum, prius illustravit montes, et sic descendit lux eius ad convallem terrarum. Et ideo quodam loco dicit in psalmo: Levavi oculos meos in montes, unde veniet auxilium mihi. Sed noli putare, quia ipsi montes tibi dabunt auxilium: accipiunt enim quod dent, non de suo dant. Et si remanseris in montibus, non erit firma spes tua: sed in illo qui illuminat montes spes tua et praesumptio tua debent esse. Auxilium autem veniet tibi de montibus, quia Scripturae per montes tibi ministratae sunt, per magnos praedicatores veritatis: sed noli in illis figere spem tuam. Audi quid dicat consequenter: Levavi oculos meos in montes, unde veniet auxilium mihi. Quid ergo? Montes tibi dant auxilium? Non: audi sequence: Auxi-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

Well what? Do the mountains provide you with help? No; Hear the following: My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. Help comes from the mountains, but it does not flow from the mountains. So whose? From the Lord, who made heaven and earth. There were other mountains, and when each individual drove the ship through them, he was shipwrecked. For the princes of heresies emerged on the plain, which were mountains. Mount was Arius, Mount Donatus, and a little while ago it was made like Mount Maximianus. Many, tending to these mountains and longing for dry land, wanting to escape the waves, were thrown against the rocks and shipwrecked on land. Was not he seduced by such mountains who said: I trust in the Lord, why do you say to my soul: Fly towards the mountains like a bird? I don't want to put my hope in Arius, I don't want to place it in Donatus; My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. Learn what you should boast of God and what you should attribute to men, because cursed is everyone who puts his hope in man. In all humility and modesty, the apostle Saint Paul, looking with true zeal at the Church and in attention to the husband, not himself, contemplating with horror those who in a certain circumstance tried to say: I am of Paul, I of Apollo, taking rather his person, which he despised and disdained to glorify Christ, said: Was Paul crucified for you, or were you baptized in the name of Paul? Away from oneself, but to send towards Christ. He does not want the wife to love in place of the husband or even the husband's friend. The husband's friends are the apostles. This husband was jealous of that lium meum a Domino, qui jecit caelum et terram (Ps 120,1.2). De montibus come auxilium, sed non a montibus. Et a quo? A Domino qui jecit caelum et terram. Erant montes alii, per quos unusquisque cum duceret navim, naufragium faceret. Emerserunt enim principes haeresum, et montes erant. Arius mons erat, Donatus mons erat, Maximianus mode quasi mons factus est. Multi in these montes attendentes, et terram desiderantes, cum de fluctibus volunt liberai, ad saxa compulsi sunt, et naufragium in terra fecerunt. A talibus montibus non seducebatur ille qui ait: In Domino conjido, quomodo dicitis animae meae, Transmigra in montes sicut basser? (Ps 10,2). Nolo sit spes mea in Ario, nolo in Donato: Auxilium meum a Domino, qui jecit caelum et terram.

Discite quantum praesumatis de Deo, et quantum tribuatis hominibus; quia maledictus omnis qui spem suam ponit in nomine (Ier 17,5). Modestissime et humiliter sanctus apostolus Paulus zelans veré Ecclesiam, sed sponso, non sibi, et horrens illos quando voluerunt dicere, Ego sum Pauli, ego Apollo (1 Cor 3,4); suam personam potius assumpsit, quam calcaret et contemneret, ut Christum glorificadoret: Numquid Paulus pro vobis crucijixus est, aut in nomine Pauli baptizati estis? (Ib. 1,13). Repellit a se, sed ut mittat ad Christum. Non vult a sponsa amari pro sponso nec amicum sponsi. Amici enim sponsi Apostoli. Huic sponso et ille humilis Ioannes, qui putabatur Christus, zelabat. Unde ait: Non sum ego Christus, sed qui post me venit,
Goodness of God and evil of the wicked

humble John who was considered Christ. Therefore he says: I am not the Christ, but he who comes after me is greater than I, and I am not worthy to loosen the thong of his shoes. Indeed, by humbling himself so much, he showed that he was not the husband, but rather the husband's friend, and that is why he says: He who has a wife is a husband; But the bridegroom's friend who is present and hears him, rejoices in the bridegroom's voice. Although the friend of the bridegroom is a mountain, yet the mountain has no light of its own emanating from it, but it hears and rejoices in the voice of the bridegroom. We, he says, have received of his fullness. Whose fullness? From him who was true light that illuminates every man who comes into this world. For this the Apostle was jealous of the Church, saying: So let man consider us as ministers of Christ and dispensers of the mysteries of God. For I lifted my eyes to the mountains from where my help comes, it is the same as man considers us as ministers of Christ and dispensers of the mysteries of God. But so that hope may not be fixed again on the mountains, but on God, listen: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase, and also: Neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but God, who gives the growth. About the first part of Psalm 1. It is known that the last day will come terribly for those who do not want to be secure by living well and prefer to live continually evil. God wanted to profitably hide this tuerunt stare: prior ille qui in veritate non stetit, deinde per eum illi quos dimisit Deus de paradiso. Unde ille humilis qui non se dicit dignum solvere corrigiam calceamenti, non est expulsus, sed stat et audit eum, et gaudio gaudet propter vocem sponsi (lo 1,27; 3,29), et non propter suam, ne veniat ei pes superbiae, et expellatur, nec possit stare. 19. Et si cum labore aliquibus vestrum taedio fuerimus, finivimus Psalmum, transivit taedium, et gratulabimur, quia Psalmus totus expositus est. In medio iam timens ne onerarem vos, dimissurus eram: sed cogitavi quia intentio nostra praecideretur, et non sic rediretur ad dimidium, quomodo si excurreremus totum; et malui vobis gravis esse, quam re imperfecta servare relics. day so that the heart is always prepared to wait for what it knows will come, although it does not know when it will arrive. Our Lord Jesus Christ, sent to us as a Teacher and being the Son of man, said that he was unaware of this day, because it was not within his teaching to teach us this. The Father knows nothing that the Son does not know, since the Father's own knowledge is his Wisdom, and his Wisdom is his Son, his Word. But since it was not convenient for us to know what He who had come to teach us certainly knew, not precisely what it was not useful for us to know, therefore, as a Teacher, he not only taught some things, but also kept silent about others. As a Teacher he knew what was appropriate to teach and what was harmful to declare. Thus, it is said, by a certain way of speaking, that the Son is ignorant of what he does not teach; That is to say, it is said that he ignores what we ignore without making it known to us. This is how we commonly speak using certain idioms, as I just said. In this way, we say that the day is happy because it makes us happy, and it is also sad because it makes us sad, and that the cold is lazy because it slows us down. Also in a contrary way the Lord says: Now I know. AAbraham was told: Now I know that you fear God. The Lord knew this even before that trial. We have already remembered in this psalm the will of God, that is, what he wants to teach us, what to warn, what things we should guard against and what we should tolerate and wait for. In this world and in this life there are two types of men mixed together, that of the just and that of sinners. Each of these two genres has its own tendencies at its heart. The race of the just strives to strive for sublime things through humility. The race of the wicked inclines to the abject by arrogance. The first one was overwhelmed to go up; the second gets muddy to fall. Hence it happens that one gender tolerates and the other is tolerated. The design of the righteous is to win the wicked to eternal life, and that of the wicked is to return evil for good and to deprive, if possible, even of temporal life from those who seek eternal life for themselves. The wicked reluctantly endures the righteous, and the righteous the wicked; remora are for each other. No one doubts that these two are a burden to themselves, but for different reasons. The just is a weight for the unjust, because he does not want him to be unjust, but he wants to make him just, and he longs for it with supplications and tries to do it with actions; The unjust, on the contrary, hates the just so much that he would not want him to exist, so that the good would not exist. The more good it is, the more burdensome it is to iniquity. Furthermore, he works to, if possible, make him unjust; If he cannot achieve it, he strives to get it out of the way and thus be free of his grief and annoyance. But if, nevertheless, it makes him unjust, it will nevertheless be burdensome to him. For not only is the just a burden for the unjust, but equally two unjust people barely tolerate each other, and when it seems that they love each other, it must be attributed to complicity in action, not to amisvestri. Commendaveramus autem iam voluntatem Dei in isto psalmo, quid nos velit docere, quid admonere, contra quid cautos esse, et quid tolerare, et quid sperare. Duo enim genera hominum, iustorum et iniquorum, in hac terra et in hac vita commixta sunt. Habent singular ista generates proprias intentiones cordis sui. Genus iustorum conatur in sublimia per humilitatem: genus iniquorum praeponderat ad inferiora per elationem. Hoc enim se depressit ut surgat, illud se extollit ut cadat.

Ex eo fit ut unum genus toleret, altera toleretur: propositumque sit iustis ipsos etiam iniquos in vitam aeternam lucrari, propositum autem iniquis reddere mala pro nobis, et eos qui sibi vitam aeternam volunt, si fieri potest, etiam vita temporali privare. Aegre enim fert, et iniustus iustum, et iustus iniustum: oneri sibi sunt. Nemo dubitat quod isti duo alterutrum sibi oneri sunt, sed diversis intentionibus. Ad hoc enim iustus iniusto oneri est, quia iniustum eum esse non vult, sed eum iustum fieri, et optat votis, et conatur factis: iniustus autem sic odit iustum, ut nolit eum esse, non ut bonum velit esse. Quanto enim bonus est, so much magis oneri est iniquitati illius. Et laborat quidem, si fieri potest, ut enim iniustum faciat; si autem non potest, de medio tollat, et a suo taedio discomfortque removeat. Sed et si eum fecerit iniustum, nihilominus oneri illi erit. Non enim iustus tantum iniusto oneri est, sed et duo iniusti vix se patiuntur: et quando se videntur dili-

word, to the cross, since it was already abolished as a penalty of the human race. Formerly the wicked were crucified; now no one is. It was honored and extinguished. It became extinct as a penalty and remains as a sign of glory. He went from places of torture to the foreheads of emperors. Whoever exalted his sorrows so much, what will he not reserve for his believers? With these things, with these words, with these speeches, with such an example the Lord encourages the righteous. Let sinners be taught as much as they want and as much as they are allowed: The Lord encourages the righteous. Whatever happens to the righteous, attribute it to the divine will, not to the power of the enemy. This one can be taught; hurt, if the Lord does not want, he cannot. And if He allows it to hurt, He knows how to protect His own: The Lord loves those who correct, and punishes everyone whom He accepts as a son. Then what does the wicked applaud, that my Father made a scourge of him? He took him to be a servant, and instructed me to be an heir. We must not consider what He allows for the unjust, but what He reserves for the just. 5. But we must desire that those who afflict us may be converted and amended. This is how he who made Saul a scourge for himself taught the faithful, since he later converted him. When the Lord said to the holy Ananias, by whom Saul was baptized, that he should receive him, because he was to be a vessel of election, Ananias responded, fearing and being terrified because of the fame of the persecutor: Lord, I heard from this man how many evils he has done to your saints in Jerusalem, and now, having received authorization, he sets out illa flagella, ad illam ignominiosam vestem, ad illam spineam coronam, ad illam dessertmo cruzem non pervenies, quia iam et de poena generis humani sublata est. Cum enim sub antiquis scelerati crucifigerentur, moda nullus crucifigitur. Honorata est, et finita. Finita est in poena, manet in gloria. A locis suppliciorum fecit transitum ad frontes imperatorum. Qui tantum honorem dedit poenis suis, quid servat fidelibus suis? His ergo rebus, his verbis, his allocutionibus, hoc tali exemplo conjirmat iustos Dominus. Saeviant quantum voluerint, et quantum permissi fuerint peccatores: conjirmat iustos Dominus. Quidquid acciderit iusto, will divinae deputet, non potestati inimici.

Saevire ille potest: ferire, si ille noluerit, non potest. Et si ille voluerit ut mercado, novit suum quemadmodum excipiat: Quem enim diligit Dominus, corripil: jlagellat autem omnem jilium quem recipit (Hebr 12,6). Quid sibi ergo plaudit iniquus, quia flagellum sibi de illo fecit Pater meus? Illum assumit ad ministerium, me erudit ad patrimonium. Nec attendere debenmus quantum permittat iniustis, sed quantum servet iustis. 5. Sed debenmus opte etiam illis per quos flagellamur, ut convertantur, et flagellentur. Sic enim suos fideles erudiebat, qui de Saulo flagellum sibi fecerat, sed postea convertit et Saulum. Et cum Ananiae sancto, a quo baptizatus est Saulus, diceret Dominus, illum suscipiendum esse Saulum, quia vas esset electionis; responded Ananias, timens et exhorrescens audita fame Sauli persecutoris; Domine, audi, inquit, ego de viro isto

to search everywhere for those who invoke your name in order to capture them, hand them over and lead them to the pontiffs. The Lord, on the contrary, tells him: Be calm; I will show you the things that are good for you to suffer for my name. I will surrender to him, he says; I will take revenge on him, and he who is cruel in my name will suffer for my name. I teach or taught others through him; I will also teach him through others. This happened. And we know how many persecutions Saul endured; many more that it unleashed. As a greedy collector he received with usury what he had given. 6. But see if what the psalm now says was fulfilled in him: The Lord encourages the righteous. Saint Paul having suffered many sufferings, says: We were not only encouraged, but we even gloried in tribulations, knowing that tribulation works patience; patience, trial; the test, the hope; Hope does not blush, because the charity of God has been spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. Alright, now it's completely fair and encouraged. Then, just as he, now encouraged, did not harm those who persecuted him, nor did he harm those he persecuted. The Lord encourages, he says, the righteous. Hear other words also from the encouraged righteous: Who will separate us from the charity of Christ? Tribulation, or anguish, or famine, or nakedness, or persecution? How one was united to Christ who was not separated by such sufferings! Some prophets had come from Jerusalem and, filled with the Holy Spirit, they prophesied to Saint Paul himself that he would suffer many tortures in Jerusalem, so that one of them, called quantas persecuciones sanctis tuis jecerit in lerosolyma, et nunc acceptis litteris vadit, ut ubicumque invenerit invontes nomen tuutn, trahat et liget, et ad pontifices adducat. Et contra Dominus: Sine, inquit, ego Mi ostendam quae illum oporteat pati pro nomine meo (Acts 9,13-16). Reddam illi, inquit, vindicabo me de illo; et patietur pro nomine meo, qui saevit in nomen meum. Erudio vel erudivi per eum alios, erudiam et ipsum per alios. Factum est hoc, et novimus quanta sustinuerit Saulus, multo plura quam fecerat, quasi avarus exactor cum usuris recepit quod dederat. 6. Sed vide utrum in illo impletum sit quod moda Psalmus dicit, Conjirmat autem iustos Dominus.

Non solum, inquit idem Paulus, cum tumba mala pateretur, sed et gloriamur in tribulationibus, scientes quia tribulatio patientiam operatur, patientia probationem, probatio spem, spes autem non conjundit, quia charitas Dei dijjusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis (Rom 5,3-5). Bene; plan iam iustus, iam confirmatus. Quomodo ergo isti iam confirmato nihil nocebant qui illum insectabantur, sic nec ipse illis quos persequebatur. Conjirmat autem, inquit, iustos Dominus. Audi alias voices confirmati iusti, Quis separabit a charitate Cbristi? Tributary, an anguish, an james, an nuditas, an persecutio (Ib. 8,35). Quomodo haerebat, qui rebus talibus non separabatur? Conjirmat autem iustos Dominus. Descenderant quidam prophetae de lerosolyma, et impleti Spiritu sancto prophetaverunt eidem Paulo quod

Agabus, taking Paul's sash, began to bind himself, as is customary, to demonstrate by the prophet, with the signs of things, what was to happen to Saint Paul, and saying this at the same time: As you see me bound, so it is fitting that the man whose sash belongs should be bound in Jerusalem. The brothers, upon hearing this, began to dissuade the admonished Saul and Paul from surrendering to so many dangers, begging him to revoke his intention of going to Jerusalem. But he, who was already among the number of those of whom it was said: The Lord encourages the righteous, answers them: Why do you break my heart? I don't value my life for myself. He had already said to those whom he gave birth to for the Gospel: I will consume myself for your souls. And now he says: I, indeed, am not only prepared to be bound, but even to die for the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. 7 [v. 18]. The Lord encourages the righteous. How do you encourage or sustain them? The Lord knows the way of the innocent. When these endure misfortunes, the ignorant, who fail to know the ways of the innocent, believe that the good walk down bad paths. He who knows them, knows by what straight path he leads his meek ones. For this reason he says in another psalm: He will guide the humble in judgment, he will teach the meek his paths. Why do you think that the wicked passers-by detested the poor wounded man who lay before the rich man's door? Why, perhaps, did they spit on him while holding their nose? However, the Lord saw that paradise was preparing him. How this man longed for the life of him who wore purple muna passurus esset in lerusalem: ita ut quídam eorum, Agabus nomine, soluta zona alligaret se, quemadmodum solet fieri, ut his indiciis rerumfutura demonstraret propheta, they say: Sicut alligatum me videtis, sic oportet alligari hominem hunc in lerosolymis. Fratres autem responso admonitum Saulum, iam Paulum, ne se tantis periculis committeret, coeperunt deterrere, et monendo et rogando revocare ne iret in Ierosolymam. Ule autem qui iam in eorum numero erat de quibus dictum est, Conjirmat autem iustos Dominus; Quid, inquit, confringitis cor meum? Non fació animam meam pretiosam mihi. Quia iam dixerat eis quos parturierat in Gospel: Et ipse impendar pro animabus vestris (2 Cor 12,15). Ego enim, inquit, non solum alligari, sed etiam mori paratus sum pro nomine Domini lesu Christi (Acts 21:11-13). 7 [v.18].

Conjirmat ergo iustos Dominus. How do we confirm this? Novit Dominus vias immaculatorum. Quando patiuntur mala, vias malas ambulare creduntur ab ignorantibus, ab his qui non noverunt videre vias immaculatorum. Ule qui eas novit, scit per quam rectum ducat mansuetos suos. Unde dixit in alio psalmo: Diriget mites in iudicio, twelvebit mansuetos vias suas (Ps 24,9). Quomodo putatis detestatos nomines passersby ulcerosum pauperem iacentem ante divitis ianuam? (Le 16,20). Quomodo forte hunc occlusis naribus conspuebant? Noverat autem Dominus illi servare paradisum. Quomodo autem sibi optbat vitam illius qui induebatur

and flax and ate splendidly every day! But the Lord saw their days and knew their future torments, and torments without end. Then the Lord knows the ways of the innocent. 8. And his inheritance will last forever. We know this by faith. Does the Lord also know this by faith? The Lord knows it with so much evidence that we will not be able to explain it even when we become equal to the angels. For the things that are manifested to us will not be as clear to us as they are to Him who cannot change. However, what was said about us? Dearest ones, now we are children of God and it has not yet been shown what we will be. We know that when He is shown to us, we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is. Then an extremely delightful spectacle is in store for us; and if in some way we can imagine him in an enigma and in a mirror, however, in no way can we express the beauty of the sweetness that God reserves for those who fear him and prepares for those who wait in him. For this reason our hearts are prepared for all the tribulations and temptations of this life. Do not be surprised to be ordered to work; You are ready for something big. Hence those words of the just man who has been encouraged: The sufferings of this time are not in proportion to the glory to come that will be manifested in us. What will be our future glory? Equalize ourselves with the angels and see God. How much the one who healed his eyes helps the blind man to see this light! When he was healed, he did not find anything worthy to reward the one who healed him; No matter how much you give him, you will never give him as much as he gave you. Pormucho que le purpura et bysso, et epulabatur quotidie splendide? Dominus autem qui prospiciebat dies illius, noverat eius future storm, et sine fine storm. Ergo, Novit Dominus vias immaculatorum. 8. Et haereditas eorum in aeternum erit. Hoc in fide habemus: Dominus numquid in fide? Dominus novit illa in tanta manifestatione, in quanta non possumus dicere, cum vel aequati Angelis erimus. Non enim nobis tam manifesta erunt, quae erunt manifesta, quam sunt manifesta illi qui nec commutari potest. Tamen et de nobis quid dictum est? Dilectissimi, nunc filii Dei sumus, et nondum apparuit quod erimus: scimus quia cum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est (1 lo 3,2).

Servatur ergo nobis nescio quod dulce spectaculum omnino: et si cogitari ex aliqua parte in aenigmate et per speculum potest, dici tamen nullo moda potest pulchritudo illius dulcedinis, quam servat Deus timentibus se, perficit autem sperantibus in se (Ps 30,20). Illuc parantur corda nostra in omnibus vitae huius tribulationibus et temptationibus. Noli mirai, quia in laboribus pararis: ad magnum aliquid pararis. Unde vox illa iusti confirmati: Non sunt condignae passiones huius temporis ad juturam gloriam, quae revelabitur in nobis (Rom 8,18). Quae erit future gloria nostra, nisi aequari Angelis, et videre Deum? Quantum praestat caeco, qui illi oculos sanaverit, ut videat hanc luzem? Cum sanus factus fuerit ille, nec invenit quid dignum rependat sanatori suo: quantumlibet enim illi det, quid dabit

give, he will give you gold, much gold; but He gave him sight. So that you know that nothing gives, see in the darkness what it gives. What will we give to that doctor who heals our inner eyes so that we may see a certain eternal light, which is He? What will we give him? Let us seek, let us find, if we can, and in the bitterness of our inquisition let us exclaim: What will I return to the Lord for all that he granted me? And what did he find? I will take the cup of health and call on the name of the Lord. Can you, he says, drink the cup that I am to drink? Hence he also says to Saint Peter: Do you love me? Feed my sheep. Through them he will drink the cup of the Lord. The Lord encourages the righteous. The Lord knows the ways of the undefiled and his inheritance will last forever. 9 [v. 19 ] - They will not be confused in bad times. What does it mean they will not be confused in bad times? They will not be confounded in the day of tribulation, in the day of trouble, as is he who is deceived by hope. Who is confused? He who says: I did not find what I expected. You are rightly confused, because you expected something from yourself or from some friendly man, and cursed is he who puts his hope in man. You were confused because hope deceived you; The hope placed in lies deceived you, for every man is a liar. If you had based your hope on God, you would not have been confused, because the one in whom you should place your hope cannot be deceived. For this reason, he of whom I spoke a little before as righteous encouraged and placed in the evil time, that is, on the day of the tale quale Ule praestitit? Ut purimum det, aurum dabit, et multum aurum dabit: ille luzm praestitit. Ut noverit ille quia nihil dat, videat in tenebrís quod dat. Quid ergo dabimus nos medico illi, interior oculos nos sananti, ad videndam quamdam luzem aeternam, quod est ipse? quid illi dabimus? Quaeramus, inveniamus, si possumus; et in angustiis inquisitionis nostrae exclamemus: Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quae retribuit mihi? Et quid invenit? Calicem salutaris accipiam, et nomen Domini invokebo (Ps 115,12.13). Potestis, inquit, bibere calicem quem ego bibiturus sum? (Mt 20,22). Inde Petro: Do ​​you love me? Pasee oves meas (lo 21,17): pro quibus biberet calicem Domini. Confirmat autem iustos Dominus. Novit Dominas vias immaculatorum, et haereditas eorum in aeternum erit. 9 [v.19]. Non conjundentur in tempore malo.

Quid est, Non conjundentur in tempore malo? In die tribulationis, in die anguishrum non confundentur: sicut confunditur quem fallit spes. Quis est qui confunditur? Qui dicit: Ego quod sperabam non inveni. Non immerito: sperabas enim de te, aut sperabas de homine amico: maledictus autem qui spem suam ponit in homine (Jer 17,5). Confunderis, quia fefellit te spes, fefellit spes posita in mendacio: omnis enim homo mendax (Ps 115,11). Si autem ponas spem tuam in Deo tuo, do not confuseris; Quia ille in quo spem posuisti, I failed non potest. Unde et ille quem paulo ante commemoravi, iustus confirmatus, positus in tempore malo, in die tribulationis, quia non confundebatur, quid ait? Gloriamur in tribulationibus, scientes quoniam
divine providence

tribulation, not being confused, what does it say? We glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation cultivates patience; patience, trial; the test, the hope, and the hope does not confuse. How is hope not confused? Because it is placed in God. Therefore, he continues: For the charity of God is spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us. The Holy Spirit has already been given to us, how can the faith placed in him from whom we have such a pledge deceive us? They will not be confounded in evil times, and in days of famine they will be satisfied. They have a certain amount of stuff here. Days of hunger are those of this life; But since the righteous are satisfied in them, others will be found hungry. How would he boast, saying: We glory in tribulations, if he were inwardly hungry? On the outside there were tribulations and anguish, but on the inside there was breadth and joy. 10 [v. 20]. What does the bad man do when he begins to be troubled? Outside it has nothing; all things have been taken from him; There is no consolation in the conscience either, it has nowhere to go, because everything external is adverse; It has nowhere to enter, because what is inside is bad. No wonder what the psalm says next happens to him: The wicked will perish. There is no place for them. How can they not perish? They have no internal or external comfort. They are outside of us, there is no consolation for them. All those who do not have God serve the powers of the world, money, friendship, glory. And all earthly and corporal goods cannot console one's interior, as one consoled tribulatio patientiam operatur, patientia probationem, probatio spem, spes autem non confudit. Unde spes non confundit? Quia in Deo posita est. Ideo sequitur, Quia charitas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum qui datus est nobis. Iam datus est nobis Spiritus sanctus, quomodo nos fallit cuius tale pignus tenemus? Non conjundentur in tempore malo: et in diebus famis saturabuntur. Est enim quaedam hic saturitas eorum. Nam dies famis, vitae huius sunt: ​​alus esurientibus, illi saturantur. Nam ille unde gloriaretur they say, Gloriamur in tribulationibus, si egestatem ¡ntus pateretur? Videbantur foris anguishe, sed intus latitudo erat. 10 [v.20].

Quid autem facit malus homo cum coeperit tribulari? Foris nihil habet, ablata sunt omnia, in conscientia nullum solatium est: non est quo exeat, quia dura sunt; non est quo intret, quia mala sunt. Merit ei fit quod sequitur: Quoniam peccatores peribunt. Quibus enim locus nusquam est, quomodo non peribunt? Consolatio is not in externis, it is not in internis. Extra sunt enim a nobis, de quibus consolatio nulla est. Et universi qui Deum non habent, pecuniae, amicitiae, gloriae, facultatibus mundi serviunt, et quaecumque bona sunt corporalia, non possunt consolari intrinsecus, quomodo consolabatur ille plenus sagina interiore, et de ipsa sagina ructans: Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit, sicut Do-

he who was full of inner nourishment and, exhaling this nourishment, said: The Lord gave it to me, the Lord took it away from me; as it pleased him, so it was done; be his name blessed. Therefore sinners do not console themselves with external things, because with them they suffer tribulations; Conscience does not console them either, since they are not right with themselves, and good cannot be together with evil. Everyone who is bad is bad with himself, and it is necessary for him to torment himself with the same torment. He who torments his own conscience, he himself is his punishment. He runs away from his friend wherever he can; from himself, where will he flee? 11. So, then, a certain man of Donato's party, accused and excommunicated by his people, came to me, seeking here what he had lost there. But, since he could not be received except in the place where he should be, wanting to appear without dishonor before his people, so as not to appear that he was doing it out of necessity, but out of free choice, he did not abandon that party. Since there he could not obtain what he wanted, since he sought vain greatness and false honor, not finding here what he lost there, he perished. He moaned hurt and was not consoled, he had horrible secret regrets in his conscience. I tried to console him with the word of God; but he was not one of the wise ants, which gather during the summer to have something to live on in the winter. When tranquility reigns, then man must collect the word of God for himself and hide it inside his heart, just as the ant hides the work of summer in undermined rooms. During the summer he spends his time doing this; Winter is coming, that is, placuit is premino, ita faclum est; sil nomen Domini benedictum (lob 1,21). Ergo illis peccatoribus non est locus in his quae foris sunt, quia ibi patiuntur tnbulationes: conscientia illos non consolatur; non est bene illis secum, quia bene esse cum malo non potest. Quisquís autem malus est, male secum est: torqueatur necesse est sibi seipso tormento. Ipse est enim poena sua, quem torquet conscientia sua. Fugit ab inimico quo potuerit, a se quo fugiet? 11. Ita quidarn ex parte Donatí venerat ad nos, accusatus et excommunicatus a suis, hic quaerens quod ibi perdiderat.

Sed quia suscipi non potuit, nisi eo loco quo debuit: non enim deseruit illam partem quasi integer apud ipsos, ut appareret eum non necessitate, sed electione fecisse: quia ibi ergo habere non potuit quod quaerebat, quaerebat autem vanam elationem et falsum honorem, et quia hic non invenit quod ibi perdidit, et ipse periit. Gemebat saucius, et non consolabatur: werent enim in conscientia eius aculei horribiles taciti. Tentavimus consolari eum de verbo Dei: sed ille non erat de sapientibus formicis, quae sibi aestate collegerunt unde hieme vivant. Cum enim res sunt tranquillae, tune homo sibi colligere debent verbum Dei, et recondere in intimis cordis sui, quemadmodum formica abscondit in cavernosis penetralibus labores aestatis (Prov 6,6, et 30,25). Per aestatem enim vacat hoc agere: come it autem hiems, id est, supervenit tribulatio; et nisi intus invenerit quod edat,
divine providence

He felt tribulation, and if he did not find food internally, he would necessarily perish from hunger. This one had not treasured the word of God; Winter came, and he did not find here, from where he could only receive comfort, what he was looking for, since he could not receive it from the word of God, which he did not treasure. Inside he had nothing; What I was looking for I couldn't find outside; he was burned with the ardor of indignation; His mind was violently moved, and, this flame being hidden for some time, it later emerged in the form of sighs, so that they were perceived among the brothers, while he was unaware that he was heard. We saw this and we grieved, God knew it, vehemently in the face of so much pain of the soul, in the face of so much suffering, in the face of so much martyrdom and so much torment. What to refer more to? He could not tolerate, occupying a humble position; If he had liked it, it could have been a healthy place for him; thus he proved himself worthy of being rejected. But, brothers, we should not distrust for this reason others who perhaps choose the truth without being forced by necessity. You should not distrust others to the point of losing all confidence, since I do not even distrust this one while he lives. No living being should be mistrusted. Because of this fact, brothers, your charity must know, lest anyone tell you otherwise, that we should not distrust anyone. In fact, a subdeacon of Donato's party, without having caused any altercation there, chose peace and Catholic unity, and, abandoning his own, he came in truth as choosing what is good, not as having been repudiated by the evil ones. He was received in such a way that we should rejoice at his conversion and commend him to your prayers. God is powerful to make you better and better. About no one we should pronounce est ut lame dispereat. Isíe ergo sibi non collegerat verbum Dei, supervenit hiems, non hic invenit quod quaerebat, consolari nisi inde non poterat, de verbo autem Dei nullo moda. Intus apud se nihil habebat, foris quod quaerebat non inveniebat: ardebat indignationum et dolorum facibus, agitabatur mens eius violenter, et tamdiu oceulte, doñee etiam erumperet in quosdam gemitus, ita ut inter fratres sonaret, et se audiri nesciret. Videbamus, et dolebamus vehementer, Deus scit, tantam poenam animae, so many crosses, so many gehennas, so much storm. Quid pluribus? Impatiens loci humilis, cui si saperet, posset esse locus salubris, talis apparuit, ut etiam proiieeretur.

Ñeque hinc desperare deben, fratres, de alus, qui forte elegerint veritatem, non secuti fuerint necessitatem. Usque adeo enim de caeteris desperandum non est, ut nec de isto desperem, quamdiu vivit. De nullo enim vívente desperandum est. Hoc ergo, fratres, ex occasione hac scíre debuit Charitas Vestra, ne quis forte aliud vobis dicat. Nam subdíaconus eorum, qui, cum ei nulla quaestio ibi commoveretur, elegit cathoiicam pacem et unitatem, et illis dimissis venit, venit revera sicut eligens quod bonum est, non sicut repudiatus a malis: sic acceptus est, ut de eius conversione gaudeamus, et eum vestris orationibus commendemus. Potens est enim Deus, qui eum faciat etiam at-

ing ourselves, leaning towards a certain part, now good, now bad. While living in this life, tomorrow is always unknown. They will not be confounded in evil times, and in days of famine they will be satisfied. For the wicked will perish. 12. And the enemies of the Lord, at the moment of boasting and exalting themselves, will be weakened and vanish like smoke. Remember Jo who hinted to you because of the similarity. The smoke, as it emerges from the fire, rises high, and at the same height it expands more and more; but the more the plume expands, the more subtle it becomes. That greatness without base and without consolidation, since it is suspended and swollen, when directed to the air it vanishes; For this reason you will see that greatness itself harmed him. The higher it rose, the more it spread, the more it spread everywhere, occupying a greater area, the more tenuous, weaker and invisible it became. The enemies of the Lord, at the moment of glorying and exalting themselves, weakened, will vanish like smoke. Of these it was said that in the same way that Fannes and Mambres resisted Moses, so these also (resist) the truth, being men corrupted in mind and reprobate in matters of faith. How do these men who resolve themselves in the wind and who exalt themselves as just and great resist the truth, if not for the swelling of their pride? What does Saint Paul say about them? As if speaking of smoke, he writes: But they will not advance anything, because their insanity will be manifested to everyone, as that of Fannes and Mambres was manifested. The enemies of the Lord, at the moment of glorying and exalting themselves, weakened, will vanish like smoke. que etiam meliorem. Caeterum de nullo pronuntiandum est in aliquam partem, sive in bonam, sive in malam. Quamdiu enim hic vivitur, crastinus dies semper ignoratur. Non conjundentur in tempore malo, et in diebus famis saturabuntur; quoniam peccatores peribunt. 12. lnimici autem Domini statim ut gloriabuntur et exaltabuntur, deficient sicut fumus deficient.
