See that, if this holy thought saves you by meditating on this kind of bread, you never saw the righteous forsaken or his descendants begging for bread. 6 [v.26]. All day long he sympathizes (et feneratur) and lends. The Latin word feneratur means to give and receive at interest; It is more clearly understood if we say fenerat. What does it matter to us what grammarians try? You understand me better by committing a barbarity than by becoming skilled in our dissertation. Therefore this righteous man sympathizes all day long (et fenerat) and lends interest. But usurers or moneylenders do not rejoice. We have finally found a certain usurer or moneylender, just as we have already found a certain bread, so that, by completely opening the roof, we may reach Christ. I don't want you to be usurers; and I don't want it because God doesn't want it either. If I don't want it, but God wants it, be it; If God doesn't want it, even if I want it, it's for his own sake whoever is. Where does it appear that God does not want it? Where it was said: He who did not give his money to usury. I think that the usurers themselves knew how detestable, how abominable and how worthy of being execrated this is. On the other hand, I myself, indeed, our God himself, who pientia per Salomonem says: Thesaurus desiderabilis requiescit in ore sapientis; vir autem stultus glutit illum (Prov 21:20). Qui enim glutit, ut non in illo appareat quod voravit, oblitus est quod audivit. Qui autem non est oblitus, cogitat, et cogitando ruminat, ruminando delectatur. Unde dicitur: Cogitatio sancta servabit te (Prov 2,11). Et ecce si servat te in ruminatione pañis huius sancta cogitatio, nunquam vidisti iustum derelictum, nec semen eius quaerens panem. 6 [v.26]. All miseretur, et feneratur. Feneratur quidem latine dicitur, et qui dat mutuum, et qui accipit: planius hoc autem dicitur, si dicamus. phenerat. Quid ad nos quid grammatici velint? Melius in barbarismo nostro vos intelligitis, quam in our disertitudine vos deserti eritis. Ergo iustus iste all miseretur, et fenerat. Sed non gaudeant feneratores.

Invenimus enim quemdam feneratorem, sicut invenimus quemdam panem: ut ubique aperto tecto perveniamus ad Christum. Nolo sitis feneratores, et ideo nolo, quia Deus non vult. Nam si ego nolo, et Deus vult, agite: si autem Deus non vult, etiamsi ego vellem, malo suo ageret qui ageret. Unde apparet Deum hoc nolle? Dictum est alio loco: Qui pecuniam suam non dedit ad usuram (Ps 14,5). Et quam detestabile sit, quam odiosum, quam exsecrandum, puto quia et ipsi feneratores noverunt. Rursus autem ego ipse, imo Deus noster, qui te prohibet esse feneratorem, iubet te esse feneratorem; et dicitur tibi, Fenera Deo. If feneras homini, habes spem; et si feneras Deo, spem non habebis? Si feneraveris homini, id est,
Ennarrations on the Psalms

It forbids being a usurer, it commands you to be a usurer, and thus it is told to you: Lend to God with usury. If you lend to man, you have hope (of receiving), and if you lend to God, will you not? If you had lent to man, that is, if you had given your money at interest to someone from whom you expect to receive something more than what you gave him, not only of money, but something more than what you gave of wheat, wine, oil or anything else; If you expect, I repeat, to receive more than what you gave, you are a usurer, and for this you should be reviled, not praised. What will I do, you say, to be a useful usurer? Pay attention to what the usurer does. Without a doubt he wants to give little and receive much; Do this too: give small things and receive big things. Watch your profits grow like wildfire. Give temporal things and receive eternal things; gives earth and receives heaven. Perhaps you will say: To whom will I give? The same Lord, who prohibited lending at interest, comes forward to tell you to whom you should lend at interest. Listen to the Scripture and you will hear how you should lend to the Lord: Lend, says he, to the Lord who has compassion on the poor. The Lord does not need you, but you have another who needs you; nevertheless, He receives, to Him you give. The poor person has nothing to give back to you, and yet he wants to give back and can't find what; He only has the good will to pray for you. When the poor man prays to God for you, he says as follows: Lord, receive the loan; be my guarantor. Therefore, if you do not have the poor who can repay, you nevertheless have a good guarantor. See that God tells you in his Scripture: Give with confidence, and I will repay you. How do bondsmen usually speak? What do they say? I give back, because I am the one who receives, you give to me. Perhaps noi mutualm pecuniam tuam dederis, a quo aliquid plus quam dedisti exspectes accipere: non pecuniam solam, sed aliquid plus quam dedisti, sive illud triticum sit, sive vinum, sive oleum, sive quodlibet aliud; si plus quam dedisti exspectas accipere fenerator es, et in hoc improbandus, non laudandus. Quid ergo, inquis, fació, ut sim utiliter fenerator? Attende quid facit fenerator. Minus vult daré certe, et plus accipere: hoc fac et tu; da modica, accipe magna. Vide quam late crescat fenus tuum. Da temporalia, accipe aeterna: da terram, accipe caelum. Et cui dabo, forte dicis? Ipse Dominus proceedit quem feneres, qui tibi iubebat ne feneres. Audi Scripturam, quomodo teneres Dominum: Fenerat, inquit, Dominum, qui miseretur pauperis (Prov 19:17).

Non enim eget a te Dominus, sed habes alium qui a te egeat: illi porrigis, ille accipit. Non enim habet pauper quod tibi retribuat: et tamen ipse vult retribuere, et non invenit quid; alone in illo remanet benevolentia orandi pro te. Cum autem pauper orat pro te, tanquam Deo dicit: Domine, mutuum accepi, fidedic me. Proinde et si non tenes pauperem redditorem, sed idoneum tenes fideiussorem. Ecce Deus tibi de Scriptura sua dicit: Da securas, ego reddo. Quomodo solent dicere fideiussores? quid dicunt? Ego reddo, ego accipio, mihi das. Putamusne et hoc dicit Deus: Ego accipio, mihi das? Plan si Deus Christus, quod non dubitatur, ipse dixit: Esurivi, et dedistis mihi mandticare. Et cum illi dicerent, When do you viditnus esurientem? ut ostenderet se pauperum fideius-

Do we believe that God says this: I receive, you give to me? Christ God said, what cannot be doubted: I was hungry, and you gave me food. And when they answered him: When did we see you hungry?, he answers, to show that He was surety for the poor, surety for all their members, since He is head and they are members, and when they receive the members He also receives the head: When you did it to one of my little ones, you did it to me. Hey, greedy lender, look at what you gave, look at what you will receive! If you had given a little money and the one to whom you gave gave you a large fifth for the little money, of incomparably greater value than the money you gave him, what thanks you would give, how you would rejoice! Hear the possession that the one to whom you lent at interest will give you: Come, blessed of my Father, receive... What? What you gave? No. You gave earthly things, and if you had not given them, they would be corrupted on earth. What were you to do with them if you had not given them? What was to perish on earth was preserved in heaven. Therefore what was preserved, this we must receive. The credit was placed; your merit became your treasure. For look at what you will receive: Receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you from the beginning of the world. On the contrary, those who did not want to lend, what will they hear? Go to the eternal game that was prepared for the devil and his angels. What is the name of the kingdom we will receive? Pay attention to what follows: These will go to eternal punishment, and the righteous to eternal life. Covet this1, buy it, lend for this purpose at interest. You have Christ sitting in heaven and praying on earth. We have found out how the righteous lend at interest: All day long he sympathizes and lends at interest. sorem, omnium membrorum suorum sponsorem; quia ille caput, illi membra, et cum accipiunt membra, caput accipit: Cum uni, inquit, ex bis minimis meis fecistis, mihi fecistis. Eia, avare fenerator, vide quid dedisti, vide quid accepturus es! Si dedisses paucam pecuniam, et ille cui dederas pro parva pecunia tua daret tibi magnam villam, incomparabiliter amplius valentem quam dederas tu pecuniam; How many gratias ageres, how much laetitia tolleris! Audi quam possessionem det quem fenerasti: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite. Crux? quod dedistis? absit. Terrena dedistis, quae si non dedissetis, in terra putrescerent. Quid enim inde facturus esses, si non dedisses? Quod periturum erat in terra, servatum est in cáelo.

Ergo quod servatum est, hoc accepturi sumus. Servatum est meritum: factus est thesaurus tuus meritum tuum. Nam vide quid sis accepturus: Percipite regnum, quod vobis paratum est ab initio mundi. Contra, illi qui fenerare noluerunt, quid audience? Lte in ignem aeternum, qui paratus est diabolo et angelis eius. Et quid vocatur regnum quod accipimus? Attendite sequence: Isti ibunt in combustionem aeternam, iusti autem in vitam aetemam (Mt 25,34-36). Ad hoc ambite, hoc emits, ad hoc fenerate. Habetis Christum in cáelo sedentem, in terra petentem. Invenimus quomodo feneret iustus. All miseretur, et fenerat.
Ennarrations on the Psalms

7. And his descendants will be blessed. Don't take this in a carnal sense. We see many children of righteous people dying of hunger; then how will his descendants be blessed? His descendants are his relics; What you sow here, you reap later. Since the Apostle says: In doing good, let us not give up, because by remaining indefatigable, we will reap in due time. Therefore, while we have time, let us do good to all. This is the offspring that will be blessed. You sow on the earth and you reap with as much abundance as the seed is; you sow in Christ, and must you lose? He sees the same offspring more clearly mentioned by the Apostle when he speaks of alms, for he says thus: He who sows little will reap little; and he who sows in blessings will reap blessings. But maybe you work when you sow, and you suffer when you feel sorry for the poor. It will be better when there is no need to give these things to anyone. When all become incorruptible, no one will be hungry to whom you can give bread, no one will be thirsty to whom you can give drink, no one will be naked to whom you can clothe, there will be no pilgrim to host; here, then, we sow among calamities, temptations, pains and groans. But pay attention to what another psalm says: They were walking and praying as they threw their seed; But he continues to attend: How will his descendants be blessed? When they return, he says, they return with joy bringing their sheaves. 8 [v.27}. See what follows and do not be lazy: Turn away from evil and do good. Do not think that it is enough for you not to strip the one who is clothed. Certainly, not by stripping the garment, 7. Et semen eius in benedictione erit. Et hic non occurrat catnalis cogitatio. Videmus multos filios iustorum fame morientes: quomodo ergo semen eius in benedictione erit? Semen eius relice eius, unde hic seminat, et postea metet. Namque Apostolus dicit: Bonum autem facientes non dejiciamus: tempore enim suo metemus infatigabiles. ltaque dum tempus habemus, ait, operemur bonum ad omnes (Gal 6,9). Hoc est semen tuum, quod erit in benedictione. Terrae committis, et tanta amplius colligis: Christo committis, et perdis? Vide ipsum semen expressius nominatum ab Apostólo, cum de eleemosynis diceret. Hoc enim ait: Qui parce seminat, parce et metet; et qui seminal in benedictionibus, de benedictionibus et metet (2 Cor 9:6). Sed laboras forte cum seminas, et dotes cum misereris, quia miseros vides. Melius enim aliquando non habebimus quibus ista demus.

Cum omnes in incorruptionem commutabuntur, nullus esuriet cui porriges panem, nullus sitiet cui des potum, nullus nudus erit quem ropas, nullus peregrinus quem suscipias: hic autem inter aerumnas, temptationes, dolors, gemitus, mittimus semen. Sed réspice ad psalmum alium: Euntes ibat, et jlebant, mittentes semina sua. Attende, quia semen eius in benedictione erit: Venientes autem venient cum exsuhatione, portantes manipulos suos (Ps 125,6). 8 [v.27] Vide ergo quod sequitur, et noli esse piger: Decline a malo, et fac bonum. Noli tibí putare sufficere, si non exspolias vestitum. Not

you turned away from evil; but do not dry yourself, lest you become barren. Do not strip the garment and clothe the naked; This is what it means to turn away from evil and do good. But you will say: What will I receive for this? He has already written for you what He to whom you lend will give you. It will give you eternal life. You give it without hesitation. Hear also what follows: Depart from evil and do good, and dwell forever and ever. Do not think, when you give, that no one sees you, or that God will abandon you when perhaps you gave to the poor and some damage or some regret would follow for the lost thing, and, for the same reason, say to yourself: What benefit did it profit me from having performed good works?; I think that God does not love men who do good. Where does this murmuring come from, where does this uproar come from, if not because these voices are often heard? Now each one notices these voices, either in his own mouth, or in that of his neighbor, or in that of his friend. God cover them and remove the thorns from their field; plant good fruit and fruitful tree. Why are you grieved, O man, for having given to the poor and having lost some things? Don't you see that you lost what you didn't give? Why don't you look at your God? Where is the faith? Why do you sleep this way? Wake it up in your heart. Pay attention to what the Lord told you when he exhorted you in this way to good works: Make yourselves purses that will not grow old, treasure in heaven that will not fail, where the thief does not approach. Remember this when you cry in misfortune. Why do you cry foolishly, man of timid heart or foolish heart? Why did you lose, if it wasn't because you didn't lend to me? Why did you lose? Who stole you? Respondeexspoliando enim vestitum, declinasti a malo: sed noli arescere, et sterilis esse. Sic noli exspolíare vestitum, ut ropas nudum: hoc est enim declinare a malo, et faceré bonum. Et quid inde habebo, dicturus is it? Iam tibi commendavit ille quem teñeras, quid tibi dabit: vitam aeternam dabit tibi; da illi securus. Audi et id quod sequitur: Decline to bad, et fac bonum; et inhabita in saecula saeculorum. Et noli putare cum das, quod nemo te videat; aut quia deserit te Deus, quando forte dederis pauperi, et consecutum fuerit aliquod damnum, aut aliqua tristitia reí amissae, et dicas tibi: Quid profuit bona me fecisse opera? Puto non amat Deus homines qui benefaciunt. Unde this vestra submurmuratio, unde iste strepitus, nor siquia abundant istae voices?

Unusquisque way of knowing your voices, aut in ore suo, aut in ore vicini sui, aut in ore amici sui. Deleat illas Deus, et exstirpet spinas de agro suo: plantet frugem bonam, et arborem fructiferam. Quid enim contristatus is, or homo, quia dedisti pauperi, et alia perdidisti? Nonne vides quia perdidisti quod non dedisti? Quare non respicis ad Deum tuum? Ubi est fides? Quare sic dormit? Excita illam in corde tuo. Attende quid tibi dixerit ipse Dominus, quando te ad huiusmodi opera bona exhortabatur: Facite vobis sácenlos non veterascentes, thesaurum non dejicientem in caelis, quo jur non accedit (Luke 12,33). Hoc ergo commemora, quando plangis in damno. Quid ploras stulte parvi cordis, aut non sani cordis? Quare perdidisti, nisi quia mihi non commodasti? Quare
Ennarrations on the Psalms

ras: The thief. Didn't I warn you in advance not to place it where the thief could approach? If the one who lost complains, it hurts him for not having put him there where he couldn't get lost. 9 £v.28]. For the Lord loves judgment and does not forsake his saints. When saints endure hardships, do not think that God does not judge or that He judges crookedly. He who commands you to judge justly, must he judge unjustly? He loves judgment and does not forsake his saints. In whatever way the life of the saints is hidden in the Lord, it will happen that those who now work on the earth, appearing as trees, which in winter time have neither leaves nor fruit, will present themselves when He appears, like a splendid sun that is born, showing in the fruits that which lived hidden in the root. Therefore He loves judgment and does not forsake His saints. Does the saint endure hunger? God does not abandon him, because he punishes everyone he receives as a son. You despise the son of God when he is punished, but you are filled with fear when he becomes rich. How is he punished? With temporary tribulations. When will he be enriched? When I hear: Come, you blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world. Prepare to be punished, so that you may be among those who deserve to be received. He loves justice so much that he does not abandon the saints, whom he flogs for a time. Because he punishes everyone whom he receives as a son, he did not forgive the Only One, in whom he found no sin. For the Lord loves judgment and does not forsake his saints. Then, since He does not abandon them, perhaps He will give them what you love in this life, that is, to live many years, perdidisti? Quis tibí abstulit? You answer: Fur. Norme hoc te praemonueram, ne ibi pontes quo fur posset acces? Si ergo dolet qui perdidit, hoc doleat, qui non ibi posuit unde perire non potuit. 9 [v.28]. Quoniam Dominas amat iudicium, et non derelinquet sanetos sitos. Quando patiuntur labores sancti, nolite putare quia non iudicat Deus, aut perverse iudicat. Qui te monet ut iuste iudices, ipse perverse iudicaturus est? Amat ille iudicium, et non derelinquet sanaos sites. Sed quo moda sit abscondita apud illum vita sanctorum, ut qui moda laborant in terra, quasi tempore hiemis arbores non habentes fructum et folia, illo apparente tanquam novo solé exorto, illud quod in radice vivebat, in fructibus appareat. Amat ergo ille iudicium, et non derelinquet sanctos sitos. Sed laborat sanctus in fame?

Non illum derelinquet Deus: flagellat omnem filium, quem recipit (Hebr 12:6). Contemnis illum quando flagellatur, expavescis quando ditatur. Unde enim flagellatur? Pressuris temporalibus. When does ditabitur? Quando audiet, Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum, quod vobis paratum est ab initio mundi. Noli ergo piger esse flagellari, ut sis inter eos qui merentur recipi. Usque adeo ille amat iudicium, ut non derelinquat sanctos, quos flagellat ad tempus. Et quoniam flagellat omnem filium, quem recipit, nec Único pepercit, in quo delictum non invenit. Quoniam Dominus amat iudicium, et non derelinquet sanctos suos. Quia ergo non eos derelinquet, forte hoc eis dabit

get old? Don't you see that if you want old age to come to you, you want the one you will complain about when it comes? Let this life not tell you, bad, sick and short: Is it true that the Lord loves judgment and does not forsake his saints? He certainly did not abandon the three young men who praised him in the fiery furnace; The fire did not touch them. But were not the Maccabees his saints, who fainted in the midst of the fire in regard to the flesh, but not in regard to faith? But this, you say, involves an even greater question, because, not having failed in their faith, He forsook them. Hear what follows: They will be preserved forever. You wanted a few years, to whom, if the Lord gave them, in your opinion, He would not abandon His saints. Visibly he did not abandon the three young people; Nor did he secretly forsake the Maccabees; To the first he granted temporary life, to confuse the unbelievers; The latter he crowned secretly, to judge the impiety of the persecutor; He who does not forsake his saints does not forsake either one or the other. The three young men would not have received anything valuable if they had not been preserved for eternity. They will be preserved forever. 10. The unrighteous will be punished, and the descendants of the wicked will perish. As the offspring of the righteous will be blessed, so the offspring of the wicked will perish. The offspring of the wicked is their way of acting. We see the son of the wicked prospering in the world, and sometimes, being made righteous, also prospering in Christ. See, then, how you understand it so that you open the roof quod hic amas, multos annos vivere, senescere? Non attendis quia si senectutem optas vinore, hanc optas de qua cum venerit conqueraris. Non tibi ergo dicat anima, vel mala, vel infirma, vel párvula: Quomodo verum est, Dominus amat iudicium, et non derelinquet sanctos sitos? Revera non dereliquit tres pueros in camino laudantes, non eos tetigit ignis (Dan 3,50): numquid sancti eius Machabaei non erat, qui in ignibus defecerunt carne, non fide? (2 Mach 7.7). Sed hoc, inquis, maiorem quaestíonem habet, quia cum fide illi non defecerint, ille illos dereliquerit. Audi quod sequitur: In aeternum conservabuntur. Tu paucos annos eis optabas, quos eis si daret Dominus, non derelinqueret sanctos suos.

Visibiliter non dereliquit tres pueros, oceulte non dereliquit Machabaeos: illis etiam dedít vitam temporalem ad confundendos infideles; illos autem oceulte coronavit ad iudicandam impietatem persecutoris: nec illos tamen, nec illos dereliquit, qui non derelinquet sanctos suos. Et nihil magnum acceperunt tres pueri, si non in aeternum conservantur. In aeternum conservabuntur. 10. Iniusti autem punientur, et semen impiorum peribit. Quomodo semens illius in benedictione erit, sic semen impiorum peribit. Semen enim impiorum, opera impiorum. Nam invenimus rursum filium impii florere in saeculo, et aliquando fieri iustum, et florere in Christo. Vide ergo quomodo accipias, ut tectum aperias, et ad Christum pervenias: noli carnaliter, nam decipieris. Sed semen impiorum, omnia opera impiorum pe-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

and present yourself to Christ. Do not understand it carnally, because you will be deceived. The descendants of the wicked, that is, all their works will perish, because they will have no fruit; for a time they have some value; Then they will look for what they executed and will not find it, because the words did pride profit us, or the boasting of riches what good did it bring us? All those things passed away like a shadow, they are words of the wicked, who did evil. Then the descendants of the wicked will perish, 11 [v. 29]. The righteous will inherit the land. Do not let greed sneakily take over you or promise you some villa, so that you do not expect there what you are told to despise here. For that certain land of the living is the kingdom of the saints. Hence it is said: You are my hope, you are my portion in the land of those who live. If your life is that, understand what kind of land you will receive. That is the land of the living; This is the land of those who die, and it will receive the dead those it fed alive. What is that land, such is life; If life is eternal, the earth is eternal. What will eternal land be like? And they will dwell in it forever and ever. Then there will be another land where we will dwell forever and ever. For of this it was said: Heaven and earth will pass away. 12 [v. 30-32]. The mouth of the righteous is exercised in wisdom. See here the bread. See how willingly this righteous man eats, how he tastes wisdom in his mouth. And his tongue speaks justice. The law of his God (is) in his heart. So that perhaps you would not think that he has in his mouth what he does not have in his heart and for ribunt, fructum non habebunt: ad tempus enim aliquid valent; post quaerent, et non invenient quod operati sunt. Nam perdentium quod operad sunt, vox erit illa: Quid nobis profuit superbia, aut quid divitiarum iactatio contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra (Wis 5,8). Ergo semen impiorum peribit. 11 [v.29]- lusti haereditate possidebunt terram. Rursus avaritia non subrepat, nec tibi aliquam villam magnam promittat, ne quod hic iuberis contemnere, ibi speres. Terra est quaedam illa vivorum, regnum sanctorum. Unde dicitur, Spes mea es tu, he insisted mea in terra vivorum (Ps 141,6). Nam et si vita tua illa est, intellige qualem terram accepturus sis. Illa est terra vivostium: haec est autem terra morientium, receptura mortuos quod nutrivit vivos.

Qualis ergo illa terra, talis et ipsa vita: si aeterna vita, aeterna terra. Et quomodo aeterna terra? Et inhabitabunt in saeculum saeculi super eam. Alia ergo terra erit ubi inhabitabimus in saeculum saeculi. Nam de ista dictum est: Caelum et terra transibunt (Mt 24,35). 12 [v.30-32]. Os iusti meditabitur sapientiam. Ecce Ule est pañis: videte quam libenter manducet iustus iste, quomodo verset in ore suo sapientiam. Et lingua eius loquetur iudicium. Lex De/ eius in corde ipsius, Ne forte putares eum in ore habere quod in corde non habet: ne forte computares eum cum illis, de quibus dictum est, Populus hic labiis

that you should not count him among those of whom it was said: This people praises me with their lips, but their heart is far from me, (it was written): And their tongue speaks righteousness. The law of his God is found in his heart. And what good is it? And his feet will not be tripped. The word of God that is found in the heart frees us from snares, from evil paths and from ruin. With you is He whose word does not depart from you. What evil will he suffer whom God guards? You place a guard in the vineyard and are safe from thieves; However, that guard can fall asleep and become intimidated and give way to the thief; He who keeps Israel does not slumber or sleep. The law of his God is in his heart and will not be tripped at his feet. Live safely, live among the wicked safely, live among the wicked safely. What harm can the wicked and the unjust do to the righteous? Pay attention to what follows: The sinner spies on the righteous and looks for an opportunity to kill him. Here he says what was prophesied in the Book of Wisdom: It is hard for us to see him, because his life differs from that of others. He intends to kill. Because? Will the Lord, who preserves the righteous, who dwells with him, who does not depart from his mouth or from his heart, abandon him? How will what was previously said be fulfilled: And he will not forsake his saints? 13 [ v - 33 }. Then the sinner stalks the righteous and looks for an opportunity to kill him. But the Lord will not let him fall into his hands. Why did he let the martyrs fall into the hands of the wicked? Why did they commit whatever they wanted to them? For some were put to the sword, others were crucified; They threw some to the beasts; to others me honoral, cor autem eorum longe est a me (Is 29,13): Et lingua eius loquetur iudicium. Lex Dei eius in corde ipsius. Et quid illi prodest? Et non supplantabuntur gressus eius. Liberat a laqueo verbum Dei in corde, liberat a via prava verbum Dei in corde, liberat a labina verbum Dei in corde. Tecum est, cuius verbum a te non recedit. Quid autem mali patitur quem custodit Deus? Sed, Non est pax ossibus meis a facie peccatorum meorum, quomodo diceret qui nullum peccatum habebat? (1 Petr 2:22). Coarctat nos ergo intelligendi necessitas ad cognoscendum tanquam plenum et totum Christum, id est caput et corpus. Cum enim Christus loquitur, aliquando ex persona solius capitis loquitur, quod est ipse Salvator, natus ex María virgine; aliquando ex persona corporis sui, quod est sancta Ecclesia, diffusa toto orbe terrarum. Et nos in corpore ipsius sumus, si tamen fides nostra sincera sit in illo, et spes certa, et charitas accensa: sumus in corpore ipsius, et membra ipsius, et ¡nvenimus nos ibi loqui, Apostólo dicente, Quoniam membra sumus corporis eius (Eph 5,30); et multis locis dicit hoc Apostolus. Nam si dixeriraus verba non esse Christi, non erunt et illa verba Christi: Deus meus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti? Et ibi enim habes, Deus meus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti? longe a salute mea verba delktorum meorum (Ps 21,2): quomodo hic habes, a facie peccatorum meorum; sic et ibi habes, verba delktorum meorum. Et si Christus utique sine peccato et sine delicto, incipimus non putare verba illa Psalmi jllius esse. Et valde durum et contrarium est, ut ille psalmus non pertineat ad Christum, ubi habemus tam apertam passionem eius, tanquam ex Gospel recitetur. Ibi enim habemus, Diviserunt sibi ropa mea, et super vestimentum meum mise-

runt sortem (Ib. 19). Quid quod ipse Dominus in cruz pendens, primum versum psalmi ipsius ore suo protulit, et dixit: Deus meus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti? (Mt 27,46). Quid voluit intelligi, nisj illum psalmum totum ad se pertinere, quia caput ipsius ipse pronuntiavit? Ubi autem sequitur et dicit, Verba delictorum meorum, non est dubium quia vox Christi est. Unde ergo peccata, nisi de corpore quod est Ecclesia? Quia loquitur corpus Christi et caput. Quare tanquam unus loquitur? Quia erunt, inquit, duo in carne una. Sacramentum hoc magnum est, ait Apostolus, ego autem dtco iti Christo et in Ecclesia (Eph 5,31-52). Unde etiam cum ipse loqueretur in Gospel, respond eis qui quaestionem intulerant de uxore dimittenda, ait: Non legistis quod scriplum est, quod Deus ab initio masculum et jeminam fecit eos, et relinquet homo patrem et matiem, et adhaerebit uxori suae, el erunt duo in carne una? lgitur iam non duo, be one is expensive (Mt 19,4-6). Yes ergo ipse dixit, lam non duo, sed una est caro; quid mirum si una caro, una lingua, eadem verba, tanquam unius carnis, capitis et corporis? Sic audiamus tanquam unum: sed tamen caput tanquam caput, et corpus tanquam corpus. Non dividuntur personae, sed distinctiontur dignitas: quia caput salvat, salvatur corpus. Caput exhibits miseriam, corpus defleat miseriam. Caput est ad purganda, corpus ad confitenda peccata: una tamen vox, ubi non scriptum est quando dicat corpus, quando caput; sed nos in audiendo distinguishus;

Why should he not say of my sins who said: I was hungry, and you gave me no food; I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink; I was a pilgrim, and you did not welcome me; I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit me? Certainly the Lord was not in prison. Why would she not say this who, when we saw you hungry, or thirsty, or in prison, and did not help you?, responds, in the person of her body, in this way: When you did not do it to one of my little ones, you did not do it to me? Why should he not say in the presence of my sins who said to Saul: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? Who certainly, being in heaven, was no longer persecuted by anyone. As in these passages of the Gospel the head spoke for the body, so here, in this passage of the psalm, the head expresses the words of the body when you hear the voices of the head. Therefore, when you hear the voices of the body, do not separate the head, and when you hear the voices of the head, do not separate the body, for they are no longer two, but one flesh. 7. Explain the justice of God's wrath, so that it does not appear that you are making excuses and accusing Him. Go ahead and declare where God's wrath comes from: There is no health in my flesh before your angry face; there is no peace in ille autem tanquam unus loquitur. Quare enira non dicat, peccatorum meorum, qui dixit, Esurivi, et non dedistis mihi manducare; sitivi, et non dedistis mihi potum; Hospes fue, et non recepistis me; infirmus fue et in prison, et non visitatis me? Certe Dominus non fuet in prison. Quare non hoc diceret, cui cum dictum esset, Quando te vidimus esurientem et sitientem, aut in prison, et non ministravimus tibí? respondedit, sic ex persona corporis sui se dixisse, Cum uni ex minimis meis non jecistis, nec mihi fecistis? (Ib. 25,42.45). Quare non dicat, a jacie peccatorum meorum, who said Saulo, Saule, Saule, quid persequeris me? (Acts 9,4). Qui utique in cáelo iam neminem persecutorem patiebatur.

Sed quomodo ibi caput loquebatur pro corpore, sic et hic caput dicit corporis voices, cum et capitis voices auditis. Sed ñeque cum corporis voices audieritis, separetis caput; ñeque cum capitis voices audieritis, separetis corpus; quia iam non duo, sed una caro. 7. Non est sanitas in carne mea a vultu irae tuae. Be strong iniuste tibi Deus iratus est, o Adam, o genus humanum, iniuste jratus est Deus! quia dixisti iam agnoscens ipsam poenam tuam, iam in corpore Christi constitutus homo: Non est sanitas in carne mea a vultu irae tuae. Expone iustitiam irae Dei: ne te excusare videaris, illum accusare. Sequere, et dic unde ira Domini. Non est sanitas in carne mea a vultu irae tuae: non

my bones He repeated what he said, because there is no health in my flesh is the same as there is no peace in my bones; However, he did not repeat in the second paragraph before your angry face, but instead expressed the reason for God's wrath, because he says: There is no peace in my bones because of the presence of my sins. 8 [v. 5]. For my iniquities were over my head and like heavy baggage they burdened me. Here he announces first the cause and then the effect, for he said what happened, emanating from the words my iniquities surpassed my head. No one is proud unless he is wicked, and his head is lifted up. He who raises his head against God rises upward. You heard when the lesson of Ecclesiasticus was read: The beginning of man's pride is apostasy from God. He who first did not want to attend to the precept, because of his iniquity, raised his head against God. And when iniquities raised their heads, what did God do with him? Now he will say it: They loaded me like heavy baggage. It is characteristic of lightness to raise one's head; For this reason, he who raises his head appears as if he were carrying nothing. Since what can be erected is light, that is why it receives weight, to be compressed. His work will be on his head, and his iniquity will be on his head. They loaded my iniquities on me like heavy baggage. 9 [v. 6 J. My wounds became corrupted and stank. He who has wounds is not healthy. Add to this that the wounds oozed poison and stank. Why did they stink? Because they were corrupted. Who does not know how this develops in life est pax ossibus meis. I repeated id quod dixit, Non est sanitas in carne tnea: hoc est enim, non est pax ossibus meis. Non autem repetivit, a vultu irae tuae, sed causam dixit irae Dei, Non est pax, inquit, ossibus meis a jacie peccatorum meorum. 8 [ v -5]- Quoniam iniquilates meae sustulerunt caput meum, sicut jaseis gravisgravatae sunt super me. Et hic causam praemisit, et effectum subiecit; quid unde contigerit dixit: Iniquitates meae sustulerunt caput meum. Nemo enim superbus, nisi iniquus, cui sustollitur caput. Sursum tollitur, qui erigi caput adversus Deum. Audistis cum lectio legeretur libri Ecclesiastici, Initium superbiae hominis, apostatare a Deo (Eccli 10, 14). Ule qui prior noluit audire praeceptum, sustulit iniquitas ipsius caput adversus Deum.

Et quia iniquitates sustulerunt caput eius, quid illi fecit Deus? Sicut jaseis gravisgravatae sunt super me. Levitatis est erigere caput, quasi nihil portat qui erigit caput. Quia ergo leve est quod potest erigi, accipit pondus unde possit compresí. Convertitur enim labor eius in caput eius, et iniquitas eius in verticem eius descendit (Ps 7:17). Sicut jaseis gravisgravatae sunt super me. 9 [v.6]. Computruerunt et putuerunt livores mei. Iam qui livores habet, non est sanus. Adde quia ipsi livores computruerunt et putuerunt. Unde putuerunt? Quia computruerunt. Iam quomodo hoc explicetur in

human? If anyone has a healthy sense of smell, he perceives the stench of sins. Contrary to this stench of sins was that odor of which the Apostle speaks: We are a good odor of Christ to God, in every place, in those who are saved. But where does this come from if not from hope? From where but from the memory of Saturday? We cry for one thing in this life and we foresee another in the next. What is cried stinks; what is anticipated exudes a good smell. Then, unless that smell was such that it stimulated us, we would never remember the Sabbath. But since we have, due to the Holy Spirit, this smell, so that we say to the bridegroom: We run after the smell of your ointments, that is why we remove our smell from our stench and breathe a little, addressing Him. If our evils did not cause us stench, we would never confess with these groans: Our wounds have corrupted and stank. For what reason? Because of my foolishness. For the same thing that he said above because of my sins, he now says because of my foolishness. 10 [v.7]. I was afflicted with misfortunes and bent to the extreme. Why was he bent over? Because he had stood up. If you humble yourself, you will be exalted; If you exalt yourself, you will be humbled, because God does not lack weight to bow you down. This weight is the burden of your sins; He will bow him over your head and you will stoop. What does it mean to be stooped? Not being able to straighten up. This is how the Lord found the woman who had been unable to straighten herself for eighteen years. So are those who have their hearts set on the earth. But since that woman found the Lord and therefore healed her, does the human coravite put quis hoc non novit? Habeat aliquis sanum olfactum animae, sentit quomodo puteant peccata. Cui putori peccatorum contrarius erat odor ilte, de quo dicit Apostolus: Cbristi bonus odor sumus Deo, in omni loco, iis qui salvi fiunt (2 Cor 2,15). Sed unde, nisi de spe? Unde, nisi de remembrancee sabbati? Aliud enim plangimus in hac vita, aliud praesumimus in illa vita. Quod plangitur, putet: quod praesumitur, íragrat. Ergo nisi esset ille talis odor qui nos viviret, nunquam sabbatum rememberemur. Sed quia habemus per Spiritum ipsum odorem, ut dicamus sponso nostro, Post odorem unguentorum tuorum curremus (Song 1,3); avertimus a putoribus nostris olfactum, et convertentes nos ad ipsum aliquantum respiramus. Sed nisi ad nos oleant et mala nostra, nunquam istis gemitibus confitemur, Computruerunt et putuerunt livores mei. Where? A facie insipientiae meae.

Unde dixit superius, A facie peccatorum meorum: inde nunc, A jacte insipientiae meae. 10 [v.7]. Miseras afflictus sum, et curvatus sum usque in finem. Where is curvatus? Quia elatus erat. If you were humilis, erigeris; If you were elatus, you would curve: non enim deerit Deo pondus unde te curvet. Illud erit pondus, fascis peccatorum tuorum: hoc replicabitur in caput tuum, et curvaberís. Quid est autem curvari? It cannot be erected. Talem invenit Dominus mulierem per decem et octo annos curvam: non se poterat erigere (Luke 13:11). Such sunt qui in terra cor habent. At vero, quia invenit mulier illa Dominum, et sanavit eam, habeat sursum cor. In quantum

Groan among these things to obtain the memory of the Sabbath, in order to deserve to reach it. The one the Jews celebrated was a sign. What was it a sign of? Of him who remembers him who says: I was afflicted with misfortunes and bowed down to the extreme. What does it mean to the end or to the end? Until death. All day he was sad. All day. That is, without interruption. He says all day long, all life long. But where did knowing him come from? That he began to remember on Saturday. Don't you want him to be troubled while he remembers what he doesn't yet have? All day long he was sad. 11 [v.8]. Because my soul is full of illusions and there is no health in my flesh. Where the whole man is, there is the soul and the body. The soul is full of illusions, the body is not healthy; How can he be happy then? But isn't it appropriate for him to grieve? All day long he was sad. We grieve while our soul is not rid of illusions and our body regains health. Immortality is true health. If I wanted to count how many the soul's illusions are, I wouldn't have time. From what things does the soul not forge these illusions? Brief is what I warn: our soul is full of illusions. Because of them, sometimes we barely manage to pray. But if it is not for images, we cannot think about bodies. Many tamen curvatur, adhuc gemit. Hoc dicit tota die, tota vita. Sed ex quo cognovit? Ex quo sabbatum I will remember coepit. Quamdiu enim recordatur quod nondum habet, non vis ut contristatus incedat? All the contristatus ambulabam. 11 [v.8]. Quoniam anima mea complete est illusionibus, et non est sanitas in carne mea. Ubi ergo est totus homo, anima et caro est.

Full anima est illusionibus, caro sanitatem non habet: quid remanet unde sit laetitia? None oportet ut contristetur? All the contristatus ambulabam. Tristitia nobis sit, doñee et anima nostra exuatur illusionibus, et corpus nostrum induatur sanitate. Illa est enim vera sanitas, quae est immortalitas. Quantae sint autem illusiones animae, si voluero dicere, tempus quando sufficit? Cuius enim anima ista non patitur? Breve est quod admoneo, quomodo anima nostra compleat est illusionibus. A facie ipsarum illusionum, aliquando vix orare permittimur. De corporibus cogitare non novimus nisi imagines; et saepe irruunt quas non quaerimus, et

Sometimes those we do not look for crowd together; then we intend to go from one to another, and from this to the one we are looking for. Other times you want to go back to what you previously thought and throw away what you think; but something else occurs to you; You want to remember what you forgot and it doesn't come to mind, but rather what you don't intend comes to mind. Where was that thing you forgot? Why does it present itself to the mind later, when it is no longer sought? When we searched for it, countless things that were not sought were presented in its place. I have said it briefly, brothers; I have deposited in your minds some ideas so that, thinking about the rest, you can find what it means to deplore the illusions of our soul. He received the punishment of illusion, he lost the truth. Just as illusion is the soul's punishment, so truth is its reward. When we were in the midst of these illusions, the truth approached us, and finding us full of them, it took our flesh, or, rather, it took it from us, that is, from the human race. He showed himself to the eyes of the flesh to heal by faith those to whom he was to make the truth evident, so that, once the eye was healed, they would see the truth. He is the truth, which was promised to us; When his flesh appeared, faith began, of which truth is the reward. Christ did not show himself on earth as he is, but rather he showed his flesh. If he had shown himself, the Jews would have seen and known him; but, if they had known him, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory. Perhaps the disciples saw him when they said to him: Show us the Father, and this is enough for us. But He, to declare that He had not been seen by them, added: Have I been so long with volumus ex hac in hanc iré, et ab illa in íllam transiré; et aliquando vis rediré ad id quod cogitabas, et dimittere unde cogitas, et aliud tibi occurrit: vis rememberi quod oblitus eras; et non tibi venit inmentem, et venit potius aliud quod nolebas. Ubi erat quod oblitus eras? Nam quare postea venit inmentem, cum iam non quaereretur? Cum autem quaereretur, occurrerunt pro illo innumerabilia quae non quaerebantur. Rem dixi brevim, fratres: aspersi nescio quid vobis, quo accepto caetera vos ipsj cogitantes, inveniatis quid sit plangere illusiones animae nostrae. Accepit ergo poenam illusionis, amisit veritatem. Sicut enim poena est animae illusio, sic praemium animae veritas.

Sed in his illusionibus constituti cum essemus, come ad us veritas, et invenit nos coopertos illusionibus, suscepit carnem nostram, vel potius a nobis, id est a genere humano. Apparuit oculis carnis, ut per fidem sanaret eos quibus veritatem fuet monstraturus: ut sanato oculo veritas patesceret. Ipse enim est veritas, quam nobis promisit, cum caro eius videretur, ut fides inchoaretur, cuius praemium veritas esset. Non enim se ipse Christus demonstravit in terra, sed demonstravit carnem suam. Nam si seipsum demonstraret, viderent íllum Iudaei et cognoscerent: sed si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent (1 Cor 2:8). Sed forte discipuli viderunt, when illi said: Ostende nobis Patrem, et sujjicit nobis. Et ille ut ab eis se non visum esse monstraret, subiec.it: Tanto tempore vobiscum sum, et non cognovistis

you and you have not known me? Felipe, who sees me, sees the Father. Then if they saw Christ, how did they still seek the Father? If they had seen Christ, they would have also seen the Father. Therefore, those who wanted the Father to be shown to them did not yet see Christ. Hear how they had not yet seen Christ; This was promised elsewhere as a reward: He who loves me keeps my commandments, and he who loves me is loved by the Father, and I will love him. Therefore, if he promised those who love him the reward of showing them himself, it is evident that we are promised such a vision of the truth, by which, once seen, we will no longer say: My soul is full of illusions. 12 fv.9}. I am weakened and humiliated to the extreme. Whoever remembers the greatness of the Sabbath sees to what extent he has been humiliated. But those who cannot think about the sublimity of rest do not see where they currently are. That is why another psalm said: I said in my rapture: I was thrown out of the presence of your sight. His mind alienated, he saw something sublime, even though, when he saw it, it was not yet completely there; However, upon perceiving certainly, if it may be said, as a radiance of eternal light, that he was not completely there, which he could understand in any way, he realized where he was and in what way he was weakened and constrained by human evils; and, therefore, he says: I said in my rapture: I was thrown out of the presence of your sight. Is what I saw in the rapture such that I warn myself? Phüippe, qui me videt, videt et Patrem. Si ergo Christum videbant, quomodo adhuc Patrem quaerebant? Si enim viderent Christum, viderent et Patrem. Nondum itaque Christum videbant, qui Patrem sibi ostendi cupiebant. Audi quia nondum videbant: In praemio illud promisit alio loco, they say, Qui diligit me, mandata mea custodit: et qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo, et ego diligam eum. Et tanquam diceretur ei, Quid illi dabis, diligens eum? Et ostendam, inquit, meipsum illi (lo 14,8.9-21). Si ergo diligentibus eum hoc in praemio promisit, quia ostendet seipsum illis; manifestum est, quia illa visio veritatis talis nobis promittitur, qua visa iam non dicamus, Impleta est anima mea illusionibus. 12 [v.9]. Infirmatus sum et humiliatus sum usque nimis. Qui rememberatur altitudinem sabbati, ipse videt quantum sit humiliatus. Nam qui non potest cogitare quae sit illa quietis altitudo, non videt ubi nunc sit.

Propterea alius psalmus dixit, Ego dixi in ecstasi mea: Proiectus sum a facie oculorum tuorum (Ps 30,23). Assumpta enim mente vjdit nescio quid sublime, et quod vidit nondum ibi totus erat: et quadam, si dici potest, quasi coruscatione facta luminis aeterni, ubi sensit non se ibi esse, quod potuit utcumque intelligere, vidit ubi esset, et quemadmodum malis humanis infirmatus et coarctatus esset: et ait, Ego dixi in ecstasi mea: Proiectus sum a jacte oculorum tuorum. Tale est nescio quid quod vidi in ecstasi, ut inde sentiam quam longe sum, qui nondum ibi sum. Iam ibi erat qui dixit assumptum se in tertium caelum, et ibi audiebat ineffabilia

how distant I am, I who am not there yet. There was the one who said that he was caught up to the third heaven and that there he heard ineffable words that it is not possible for man to express. But he turned to us to groan first, that he might perfect himself in weakness, and then arm himself with strength. However, encouraged because he saw, in view of the ministry he carried out, something of those things, he added, saying: I heard ineffable words that it is not given to man to speak. Therefore it is no longer necessary for you to ask me or anyone else the things that are not permitted to be spoken, since it was not permitted to express them to the one to whom it was permitted to hear them. Let us cry, however, and groan in confession. Let us know where we are, let us remember the Sabbath and wait patiently for what was promised by the one who gave us an example of patience in himself: I am weakened and humiliated to the extreme. 13. I roared because of the groaning of my heart. You frequently observe that the servants of God break out into groans: the reason is investigated, and the groaning of some servant of God is only noticed, if it reached the ears of a man who is next to him. For there is a hidden groaning that is not heard by man; However, if the intense thought of some desire takes hold of the heart, so that the wound of the inner man comes to express itself with a clearer voice, then the cause is investigated, and the man who hears says within himself: Perhaps he groans for this or perhaps this other thing happened to him. But who can understand but He before whose eyes and ears he groans? Therefore he roared, he says, verba, quae non licet homini loqui. Sed revocatus est ad nos, ut gemeret prius perficiendus in ínfirmitate, et sic postea indueretur virtute: animatus tamen, quia vidit aliquid rerum illarum pro dispensatione officií sui, adiecit dices, Audivi ineffat/ilia verba, quae non licet homini loqui (2 Cor 12,2-10). Iam ergo quid opus est ut a me aut a quoquam quaeratis quae non licet homini loqui: si illi non licuit loqui, cuj licuit audire? Plangamus tamen et gemamus in confessione, agnoscamus ubi simus, recordemur sabbatum, et patienter exspectemus quod ille promisit, qui nobis et in se ipso exemplum patientiae demonstravit. Injirmatus sum et kumiliatus sutn usque nimis. 13. Rugiebam a gemitu coráis mei. Attenditis plerumque interpellare gemitibus servos Dei, et quaeritur causa: et non apparet nisi gemitus alicuius serví Dei; si tamen ad aures hominis circa illum positi pervenerit.

Est enim gemitus occultus qui ab homine non auditur: tamen si tanta occupaverit cor cogitatio desiderii cuiusdam, ut voce clariore exprimatur vulnus interioris hominis, quaeritur causa; et dicit homo apud semetipsum, Forte illud est unde gemit, et forte illud illi factum est. Quis potest intelligere, nisi ille in cuius oculis et auribus gemit? Propterea rugiebam, inquit, a gemitu coráis mei: quia homines si quando audiunt gemitum hominis, plerumque gemitum carnis audiunt; gementem a gemitu cordis non

because of the groaning of my heart, because, even when men hear the groaning of man, they often hear the groaning of the flesh, but they do not hear him who groans with the groaning of his heart. A certain man took away another man's things; the latter roars, but not with the groan of the heart; another roars because he buried his son; another, because he buried his wife; another, because his vineyard was stoned, or because his vat turned sour, or because a gypsy stole his donkey; another roars because he suffered some damage; another, because he fears an enemy man. All these roar with the groaning of the flesh. On the contrary, the servant of God, as he roars for the remembrance of the Sabbath, which is the kingdom of God, which flesh and blood shall not possess, roared, he says, because of the groaning of my heart. 14 [v.10]. He who knew why he roared, adds: And before you is all my desire. Not before men, who cannot see the heart, but before you is all my desire. May your desire be found before Him; and the Father, who sees in secret, will reward you. Your wish is your prayer; If the desire is continuous, the prayer is continuous. Not in vain did the Apostle say: Pray without ceasing. But do we kneel, prostrate and raise our hands continuously, and that is why it is said: Pray without ceasing? If we say we pray like this, I think we cannot do this without interruption. There is another interior and continuous prayer, which is the desire. Whatever you do, if you wish that Sabbath, do not interrupt the prayer. If you don't want to stop praying, don't interrupt the desire; Your continuous desire is your voice, that is, your continuous prayer. You are silent if you stop loving. Who was silent? Those of whom I heard. It was said: Because iniquity increased, the charity of many grew cold. The cold of charity is the silence of the heart, and the fire of love is the cry of the heart. If charity remains continually, you always cry out; If you always cry, you always desire; If you want, you remember the break. But it is convenient that you know in front of whom the roar of the heart should be. Consider now what desire you should have before the presence of God. What if our enemy dies? Men desire this as a just thing, as sometimes we ask for what we do not owe; Let's see what men ask for as a just thing. They ask that someone die so that they can have their property. But these who ask for the death of their enemies, hear the Lord, who says: Pray for your enemies. Then do not ask for the enemies to die, but ask for their correction, and thus the enemies will die; Well, once corrected, they will no longer be enemies. And before you is all my desire. What will happen if the desire is before God and the groaning is not? But how can this happen, since the moan is the voice of desire? This is why the psalm adds: And my groaning is not hidden from you. For you it is not hidden, for many men it is. But sometimes it is noticed that the humble servant of God says: And my groaning is not hidden from you. It is also observed that from time to time the servant of God laughs; Perhaps this is why that desire died in your heart? If the desire is found there, so is the moan; It does not always reach the ears of man, but it never departs from the ears of God.

15 [v. l l ]. My heart was troubled. Why was he disturbed? Because my strength abandoned me. Many times something unexpected suddenly breaks in and confusion takes over the heart; The earth shakes, it thunders, there is a movement or a frightening roar, perhaps a lion is seen on the road, the thieves are surprised; the heart is troubled; Everywhere there is fear, anxiety is instilled. Why does this happen? Because my strength abandoned me. If the fortress survived, what would be feared? Whatever event was announced, whatever roared, whatever resounded, whatever fell, whatever rippled, would not frighten you. But where does that confusion come from? That my strength abandoned me. How did he abandon me? I lack the light in my eyes. The light was hidden from Adam's eyes. God was the light of his eyes; As soon as he offended him he fled into the darkness and hid among the trees of paradise. He feared the presence of God and sought the protection of the trees. Between the trees he was already missing the light in his eyes, in which he used to rejoice. Then if Adam lost this light from his origin and we also lost it since then because we are his race, when these members of Adam turn to the second or last Adam, because the last Adam was made in a life-giving spirit, and cry out from their new body saying: And I lack the light of my eyes, are we to believe that, confessing and being already redeemed and already belonging to the body of Christ, they must lack the light of their eyes? Certainly they are missing. For they are still among those who forget the Sabbath, as among those who see in

derium tuum, continua vox tua est. Tacebis, si amare destiteris. Who tacuerunt? De quibus dictum is: Quoniam abnndavit imquitas, refrigescet charitas multorum (Mt 24:12). Frigus charitatis, silentium cordis est: flagrantia charitatis, clamor cordis est. If you always manet charitas, you always cry; If you always cry, you always desire; If you consider, requiem you will remember. And rugitus cordis tui ante quem sit, oportet ut intelligas. Iam quale desiderium debeat esse ante oculos Dei, consider. Numquid ut moriatur inimicus noster, quod quasi iuste optant nomines? Nam aliquando oramus quod non debenmus. Illud quod quasi iuste orant nomines, videamus. Nam orant ut moriatur aliquís, et ad illos haereditas veniat. Sed et illi qui orant ut moriantur inimici, audiant Dominum dicentem: Orate pro inimicis vestris (Ib. 5,44, et Le 6,27). Non ergo hoc orent, ut moriantur inimici: sed hoc orent, ut corrígantur; et mortui erunt inimici; iam enim correcti, non erunt inimici. Et ante te omne desiderium tneum. What if desiderium ante illum est, et ipse gemitus non est ante illum? Unde fieri potest, quando ipsum desiderium vocem suam habet gemítum? Ideo sequitur, Et gemitus meus non est absconditus a te. A te non est absconditus, a multis autem hominibus absconditus est.. Videtur aliquando humilis servus Dei dicere: Et gemitus meus non est absconditus a te. Videtur aliquando et ridere servus Dei: numquid desiderium illud mortuum est in corde? Si autem inest desiderium, inest et gemitus: non semper pervenit ad aures hominum, sed nunquam recedit ab auribus Dei.

15 [v. l l ]. Cor meum contuxbatum est. Where is conturbatum? Et deseruit me fortitudo mea. Plerumque irruit nescio quid repentinum; fit conturbatio cordis: contremiscit terra, tonitrus datur de cáelo, horribilis fit Ímpetus vel strepitus, leo forte videtur in via; fit conturbatio: latrones insidiantur; fit conturbatio cordis, pavetur, undique sollicitudo incutitur. Unde hoc? Quia deseruit me fortitudo mea. Si enim maneret illa fortitudo, quid timeretur? Quidquid nuntiaretur, quidquid frenderet, quidquid sonaret, quidquid caderet, quidquid horreret, non terreret. Are you disturbed? Deseruit me fortitudo mea. Unde seruit fortitudo? Et lumen oculorum meorum non est mecum. Latuerat ergo Adam lumen oculorum ipsius. Nam lumen oculorum ipsius ipse Deus erat: quem cum offendisset, fugit ad umbram, et abscondit se inter ligna paradisi (Gen 3,8). Pavebat a facie Dei, et quaesivit umbram arborum. Iam inter arbores lumen oculorum non habebat, ad quod gaudere consueverat. Si ergo ille de origine, et nos de propagagine; et redeunt ad illum secundum vel novissimum Adam membra ista, quia novissimus Adam in spiritum vivificantem (1 Cor 15:45); et clamant de corpore eius in ista confessione, Et lumen oculorum meorum non est mecum: iam confitens, iam redemptus, iam in corpore Christi est, et lumen oculorum ipsius non est cum ipso? Plan non est cum ipso: sed est quidem tanquam adhuc recordantium sabbatum, tanquam cetnentium in spe; sed nondum est illud lumen de quo dicitur, Ostendam meipsum illi

hope, but who do not yet possess that light of which it is said: I will show myself to him. There is some light in us because we are children of God, and we retain this by faith, but it is not yet the light that we will see, it has not yet been manifested what we will be. We know that, when He appears, we will be like Him; because we will see him as he is. Now we have the light of faith and hope, because, while we live in body, we make a pilgrimage towards God, and we walk by faith, not by vision. And while we wait for what we do not see, we wait patiently. These voices are from the pilgrims, not from those who are already in the homeland. Therefore, he speaks rightly, and speaks truthfully, and if he is not a liar, he truthfully confesses, that he lacks the light of his eyes. These things the inner man endures with himself, in himself and for himself; without coming from anyone outside of himself. He himself deserved to have everything I listed above be his punishment. 16 [v.12.13]. But is this only what man suffers? Inwardly he suffers for his cause; externally, by those among whom he lives. He suffers his own ills and is forced to also suffer those of others. From here come these two cries: Cleanse me from my hidden sins, O Lord, and free your servant from those of others. He has already confessed his hidden sins, from which he wishes to be cleansed; Speak also of those of others, from whom you long to be free: My friends... What shall I not say of the enemies? My friends and relatives approached me and remained standing. They understand what it means and they stood against me. If they stood against me, they fell against each other. My friends and relatives know (14,21). Est quiddam luminis, quia filii Dei sumus, et utique hoc in fide retinemus: sed nondum est illud lumen quod videbimus. Nondum enim apparuit quod erimus: scimus quia cum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est (1 lo 3,2). Nam modo lumen fidei et lumen spei est. Quamdiu enim sumus in corpore, pilgrimage to Domino: per fidem enim ambulamus, non per speciem (2 Cor 5,6.7). Et quamdiu quod non videmus speramus, per patientiam exspectamus (Rom 8,25). Voces sunt ergo istae peregrinantium, nondum in patria constitutorum. Et recte dieit, et veré dicit, et si non sit dolosus, veraciter confitetur: Et lumen oculorum meorum non est mecum. Haec patitur homo intus, ibi secum, in seipso, et seipsum, de nemine ad neminem praeter se: haec sibi ipse poena sua esse meruit, quidquid superius enumeravit. 16 [v.12.13].

Sed numquid hoc solum est quod patitur homo? Patitur enim ex se intrinsecus, forinsecus autem ex eis inter quos vivit: patitur mala sua, cogitur pati et aliena. Inde sunt illae duae voices: Ab occultis meis munda me, Domine, et ab aiienis parce servo tuo (Ps 18,13.14). Iam de occultis suis confessus est, a quibus se cupit mundari: dicat et de aiienis a quibus sibi vult parci. Amici mei. What do you mean by inimicis? Amici mei et proximi mei adversum me appropinquaverunt, et steterunt. Hoc quod ait, adversum me steterunt, intellige. Si enim adversum me steterunt, adversus se ceciderunt. Amici mei et proximi mei adversum me appropin-

They approached me and stood there. Let's understand that the voice in the head is already speaking; Our Head is already beginning to show itself in passion. But, when the Head begins to speak, do not separate the body from there. If the Head did not want to separate itself from the clamor of the body, will the body dare to separate itself from the sufferings of the Head? You suffer in Christ, since Christ appears in your weakness as a sinner. Now he speaks, as through his mouth, of your sins, and calls them his own; for he says in the presence of my sins, which were not his. Then, just as He wanted to have our sins as His, taking care of His body, in the same way we must want His sufferings to be ours because He is our Head. For it must not be He alone who endures torments from enemies in favor of friends, and we excuse ourselves from them. Rather, let us prepare to celebrate the banquet with Him. Let us not throw away the cup, in order to reach the sublimity of Christ through his humility or weakness. Well, he answered those who wanted to achieve his greatness and did not think about the humility of Christ at that time, saying: Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink? Therefore the sufferings of the Lord are our sufferings. If each one is to serve God rightly, let him keep the faith, manifest what he owes, and live justly among men; and I want to see if he does not suffer what Christ enumerates regarding his passion. 17. My friends and relatives came against me and stood, and those close to me stood at a distance. Which loved ones came closer and which loved ones stayed at a distance? The quaverunt, et steterunt. Iam intelligamus capitis voices, Iam incipiat illucescere caput nostrum in passione. Sed rursum cum coeperit caput dicere, noli inde separare Corpus. Si caput noluit se separare a vocibus corporis, Corpus se audeat separare a passionibus capitis? Patere in Christo; Quia tanquam peccavit in firmitate tua Christus. Modo enim peccata tua tanquam ex ore suo dicebat, et ea dicebat sua. Dicebat enim, A jacie peccatorum meorum, quae noneront ipsius. Quomodo ergo peccata nostra sua esse voluit propter corpus suum, sic et nos passíones eius nostras esse velimus propter caput nostrum. Non enim ille ex amicis passus est inimicos, et nos non. Imo et nos ad hoc paremus in eodem convivari: talem calicem non respuamus, ut celsitudinis eius desiderium per humilitatem eius inveniamus.

Respondit enim celsitudini eius haerere volentibus, qui eius adhuc humilitatem non cogitabant, et ait illis: Po/estis bibere calicem quem ego bibiturus sum? (Mt 20,22). Ergo et illae passiones Domini, passiones nostrae sunt: ​​et unusquisque si bene serviat Deo, bene servet fidem, exhibitat quod deben, et versetur inter homines iuste, voló videre si non patitur, etiam quod hic enumerat in passione sua Christus. 17. Amici mei et proximi mei adversum me appropinquaverunt, et steterunt: et proximi a longe steterunt. Who next appropinquaverunt, et who next a longe steterunt? Next were Iudaei, quia cognati were:

The Jews were close to him, because they were his fellow citizens; These approached when they crucified him. The apostles were also close and, however, they stayed at a distance so as not to suffer with Him. It can also be understood in this way: my friends, that is, those who pretended to be his friends when they said to him: We know that you teach the way of God with truth. Well, his friends wanted to try to tempt him on this occasion, asking him if the tribute should be paid to Caesar and convincing them through his own mouth. But He did not need anyone to testify to Him about the man, because He knew what was inside the man; and he knew it in such a way that, having spoken to him with friendly words, He answered them: Why do you tempt me, you hypocrites? Then my friends and relatives approached me and remained standing, and those close to me remained at a distance. You know my opinion. I called close to those who approached and yet remained at a distance. They came closer with their bodies, but remained a little distance from their hearts. Well, who was closer with the body than those who lifted him up on the cross, and who remained more distant than those who insulted him? I heard of this departure from the prophet Isaiah; Notice this distancing and approaching: This people honors me with their lips; here we have the approach of the body; but his heart is far from me. They are near and far: close with the lips, far with the heart. However, as the apostles, fearing, remained at a distance, we more clearly and aptly apply the second part of the verse to them. So that some approached and others remained at a distance: thus, Peter, who had boldly seized him, et quando crucifixerunt Proximi et Apostoli: et tamen ipsi a longe steterunt, ne cum illo paterentur. Potest etiam hoc sic intelligi: Amici mei, id est, qui se finxerunt amicos meos. Amicos enim se finxerunt, quando dixerunt: Scimus quia in veritate viam Dei twelves (Ib.

22,16): quando illum tentare voluerunt, utrum solvendum esset tributum Caesari, quando illos convicit ore ipsorum, amici videri volebant: sed non illi erat opus ut quisquam ei testimonium perhiberet de homine; ipse enim scíebat quid esset in homine (lo 2,25): adeo ut cum árnica verba dixissent, responderet eis, Quid me, inquit, tentatis hypocritae? (Mt 22,18). Ergo Amici mei et proximi mei adversum me appropinquaverunt, et steterunt: et proximi a longe steterunt. Nostis quid dixi. Next dixi qui appropinquaverunt, et tamen a longe steterunt. Appropinquaverunt enim corpore, sed longe steterunt corde. Qui tam propinqui corpore, quam qui in cruzem levaverunt? Qui tam longe corde, quam qui blasphemaverunt? Audite istam longinquitatem ab Isaia propheta, videte istam propinquitatem et longinquitatem: Populus bic labiis me honorat: ecce propinquat corpore: Cor autem eorum longe est a me (Is 29,13). Iidem propinqui, iidem longinqui: propinqui labiis, longinqui corde. Verumtamen quia longe steterunt timentes Apostoli, absolutius et planius de illis accipimus, ut alios propínquasse, alíos longe stetisse intelligamus: quandoquidem et Petrus qui audacius secutus fuet,

Guided by the passion, he was so distant that, questioned and disturbed, he denied three times the Lord, who promised that he would die with Him. Later, from a distance, in order to get closer, upon hearing after the resurrection: Do you love me?, he answers: I love you. He who, denying, moved away, affirming, came closer, thus destroying the triune denial through the triune confession of love. And my loved ones were left at a distance. 18. And those who sought my life were strong. It is evident who sought his life: those who did not possess his life, because they did not belong to his body. Those who sought her life were distant from her, but they were searching for her to take it from her. His life is also sought in a good sense, since in another passage he argues with some by saying: There is no one who seeks my life. He blames some who do not seek his life, and he also blames others who seek it. Who is he who seeks well the life of Christ? Who imitates his sufferings. Who are those who seek their lives badly? Those who rioted against Him and crucified Him. 19- Continue: Those who sought my evils spoke in vain. What does it mean for those who searched for my evils? They searched for many and did not find them. Maybe he meant: they were looking for my evils or crimes. Well, Saint Matthew writes: They were looking for what to say about him and could not find. They looked for evil in the good, they looked for crimes in the innocent, how could they find them in Him who was without sin? But, as they searched for sins in which ita adhuc longe erat, ut interrogatus et perturbatus, ter denialet Dominum, cum quo se moriturum esse promiserat (Mt 27:70). Who posts ex longinquo ut propinquus ièret, audivit post resurrectionem, Do you love me? et dicebat, Master (lo 21,17). And saying propinquabat, qui negando longe factus erat, doñee trina voce amoris, solveret trinam vocem negationis. And next to me a long time. 18. Et vim faciebant qui quaerebant animam meam. Iam manifestum is qui quaerebant animam ipsius: qui non habebant animam eius, quia noneront in corpore eius. Qui quaerebant animam eius, longe erant ab anima eius: sed quaerebant ut occiderent eam. Quaeritur enim anima eius et bene. Nam alio loco arguit quosdam say: Et non est qui requirat animam meam (Ps 141,5). Arguit quosdam non quaerentes animam eius, et rursus arguit alios quaerentes animam eius. Quis est qui quaerit bene animam ipsius?

Qui eius passiones imitatur. Who sunt who quaerebant male animam eius? Qui ei vim faciebant, et crucifigebant eum. 19. Sequitur, Qui quaerebant mala mea, locuti sunt vanitatem. Quid est, Qui quaerebant mala mea? Fine quaerebant, et non inveniebant. Forte hoc dixerit, Quaerebant crimina mea. Quaesierunt enim quae in illum dicerent, et non inveniebant (Mt 26,59.60). Quaerebant enim mala de bono, quaerebant scelera de innocente: quando invenirent in eo qui nullum peccatum habebat? Sed quia peccata quaerebant in eo qui nullum peccatum S.Ag. 19

lacked them, they had no choice but to pretend what they couldn't find. For this reason, those who sought a thousand evils spoke lies, not truth. And all day long they plotted deceptions. That is, they concocted fallacies incessantly. You already know how many false testimonies were told against Christ before the passion. You also know how many were said against Him after His resurrection. For the soldiers guarding the tomb, of whom Isaiah said: I will place wicked men before his tomb, were undoubtedly wicked, for they did not want to tell the truth, and, bought, they spread the lie. I heard the foolishness they uttered. When questioned, they declared that while they were asleep, his disciples came and robbed him. This is idle talk. If they were asleep, how did they know what happened? 20 [v. 14. 15]. Therefore he says: And I, being deaf, did not hear. He who did not respond to the things he heard, showed himself as one who did not hear them. And, like a deaf man, he did not hear, and like a mute, he does not open his mouth. Then he repeats the same thing, saying: And I became like a man who does not hear and who has no answer in his mouth. As if I didn't have anything to tell them or argue with them. But had he not previously rebuked them, had he not reproached them for many things and said: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!, and so many other similar things? However, when he suffered, he said none of this, not because he had nothing to say to them, but because he hoped that they would carry out all things and fulfill all the prophecies about Him, of whom it had been written: And like a voiceless sheep before the habebat, restabat ut fingerent quod non inveniebant. Ideo, Qui quaerebant mala mea, locuti sunt vanitatem, non veritatem. Et dolum tota die meditabantur: hoc est, fallaciam sine cessatione meditabantur. Nostis quanta false testimony dicta sunt in Dominum, antequam pateretur. Nostis quanta false testimony dicta sunt, etiam cum resurrexisset. Nam illi milites custodes sepulcri, de quibus Isaiah dixit, Ponam malas pro sepultura eius (Is 53,9) (malí enim erant, et veritatem dicere noluerunt, et corrupti mendacium seminaverunt): attendite qualem vanitatem locuti sunt. Interrogad sunt etiam ipsi, et dixerunt: Cum dormeremus, venerunt discipuli eius, et abstulerunt eum (Mt 28:13). Hoc est loqui vanitatem. Si enim dormiebant, unde sciebant quod gestum erat? 20 [v.14.15].

Ergo ait, Ego autem velut surdus non audiebam. Qui ad ea quae audiebat non responderbat, tanquam non audiebat. Ego autem velut surdus non audiebam: et sicut mutus non aperiens os suum. Et repetit eadem: Et jactas sum sicut homo non audiens, et non habens in ore suo argutiones. Quasi non esset quod illis diceret, quasi non esset unde illos argueret. Nonne iam antea mulla increpaverat, mula dixerat, et dixerat, Vae vobis, Scribae et Pharisaei, hypocritae (Mt 23:13), et mula talia? Tamen quando passus est, nihil horum dixit: non quia non habebat quod diceret, sed exspectabat ut complerent illi omnia, et implerentur omnes prophetiae de illo, de quo dictum erat: Et sicut ovis coram tondente se sine poce, non aperuit os suum (Is 53,7). Oportebat ergo ut taceret in passione.

shearer, did not open his mouth. It was appropriate that he who should not be silent in judgment remain silent in passion. The one who will judge later presented himself to be judged, and therefore the one who was judged in extreme humility must judge with great power. 21 [v. 16 }. Because in you, Lord, I waited; You will hear me, Lord, my God. As if it were said to him: Why did you not open your mouth, why did you not say forgive, why, hanging on the cross, did you not rebuke the wicked?, he responds: Because in you, Lord, I hoped; you will hear me, Lord, my God. I warn you what you should do when tribulation attacks you. You try to defend yourself, and perhaps no one comes to your defense. Then you are disturbed as if you had lost your cause, because you have no one to defend or witness you. Keep your innocence internally where no one violates your cause. False testimony prevailed against you, but before men; But will it have any value before God, before whom your case must be substantiated? When God is the judge, there will be no witness but your conscience. Fear only your cause between the just judge and your conscience; If she is good, you will not fear any accuser, you will not challenge any false witness nor seek any true one. You only present a good conscience so that you can say: For in you, Lord, I waited; you will hear me, Lord, my God. 22 [v. 171. For I said, Let my enemies never mock me, for when my feet were moved, they spoke arrogantly against me. Once again he focuses his gaze on the weakness of his body, and, therefore, his head looks through his feet. Well, not non taciturus in iudicio. Iudkandus enim venerat, qui postea iudicaturus vinoet: et ideo cum magna potestate iudicaturus, quia cum magna humilitate iudicatus. 21 [v.16]. Quoniam in te, Domine, speravi; you exaudies. Domine, Deus meus. Tanquam si ei diceretur, Quare non aperuisti os tuum? quare non dixisti, Parcite? quare non in cruz pendens iniquos arguisti? Sequitur et dicit: Quoniam in te, Domine, speravi; you exaudies, Domine, Deus meus. Monuit te quid facías, si forte occurrerit tribulatio. Quaeris enim I will defend you, et forte nemo accipit defensionem tuam. Iam tu perturbaris, quasi perdideris causara tuam, quia nullius habes defensionem aut testimonium.

Custodi intus innocentiarn tuam, ubi nemo opprimit causam tuam. Praevaluit in te falsum testimonium, sed apud nomines: numquid apud Deum valebit, ubi causa tua diceda est? Quando Deus iudex erit, alius testis quam conscientia tua non erit. inter iudicem iustum et conscientiam tuam noli timere nisi causam tuam: si causam malam non habueris, nullum accusatorem pertimesces, nullum falsum testem refelles, nullum verum requires. He is so in heaven that he abandons what he has on earth. From there he looks and sees us. Sometimes, according to life, our feet are moved and slide into some sin; then the evil voices of the enemies are raised. From this we understand what they were looking for when they were silent. In such circumstances, the inhumans speak harshly, rejoicing at having found what they should mourn. And I said: Let not my enemies be wet with me. I said this, and perhaps you allowed them to speak haughtily of me for my correction when my feet were moved; That is to say, they became arrogant and spoke many bad things about me when I was moved. They should have pitied the weak, not insulted them; For thus says the Apostle: Brethren, if any man has been caught in any crime, you spiritual ones correct such a one in a spirit of meekness. Because I am prepared for punishment. With all nobility he exclaims, as if to say: For this I was born, to endure punishment. I was born of Adam, to whom calamities are due. Aliquando enim, ut est ista vita, commoventur pedes nostri, et labuntur in aliquo peccato: ibi exsurgunt linguae nequissimae inimicorum. Hinc ergo intelligimus, etiam cum tacebant quid quaerebant. Such were the Jews; Christ came to them with goods, they returned evils for goods. Avoid this evil, oh brothers! For it soon enters the heart. Because we said that such were the Jews, let no one of you think that he is very far from pro peccato meo, faciam omnia quaecumque facienda sunt, ad abolendum et sanandum peccatum meura. Avoid, then, such a great evil, such a subtle sin. 26 fv.21]. Those who return evil for good speak ill of me, because I followed justice. For this (last they returned me) evils for goods. What does persecutus sum iustitiam (I went in pursuit of justice) mean? That I didn't abandon him. So that you may not understand that the word persecution is always taken in a bad sense, he said persecutus (I persecuted), that is, I followed what was right: because I followed justice. Hear our Head lament in passion: I, the chosen one, was thrown away as a detestable dead. It was not enough to be dead. Why was he abhorred? Because he was crucified. In fact, death on a cross was considered an abomination by those who did not understand what was prophesied: Cursed is every man who hangs on a tree. He did not introduce death, but found it here coming from the curse of the first man; but, taking our very death, which came from sin, he hung it on the tree. So that no one might think, as certain heretics do, that our Lord Jesus Christ apparently had flesh and did not truly die on the cross, the prophet pays attention to this and exclaims: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree. Then he showed that the Son of God also died a true death, which was due to mortal flesh, so that you would not think that the uncursed did not really die. Since that death was not feigned, but came from the propagation derived from the curse intimated by God when he said: With
