death you will die, true death also fully reached Him, so that life could come to us. Likewise, the curse of death also came to Him so that the blessing of life could come to us. And they threw me, the chosen one, as a detestable dead. 27 {v.22j. Do not abandon me, Lord, my God; don't leave me. Let us say in Him and through Him, since He intercedes for us, let us say: Do not abandon me, Lord, my God. However, He had said: My God, my God, why did you abandon me? and he also says: My God, do not depart from me. If it didn't move away from the body, did it move away from the head? Whose voice was this if not the first man's? To show that he was carrying the true flesh of this first man, he says: My God, my God, why did you abandon me? God did not abandon him. If I did not forsake you, who believe in Him, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, who is one God, would I forsake Christ? In itself it had transfigured the person of the first man. We know, as the Apostle says, that our old man was crucified with Him. We would not lack old age if it had not been crucified in the weakness of Christ. He came so that we might be renewed in Him, since by desiring Him and imitating His passion, we are renewed. Then it was the voice of weakness, it was our voice that with which it was said: Why did you abandon me? Hence it was also written in another place: the words of my crimes, as if it were said: These words were transfigured in me attending to the person of a sinner. Don't walk away from me.

26 [v.21]. Detrahebant mihi qui tetribuunt mala pro bonis, quoniam persecutus sum iustitiam. Ideo mala pro bonis. Quid est, persecutus sum iustitiam? Non dimisi: ne forte persecutionem sempet in malo intelligas, persecutus dixit, perfecte secutus: Quoniam persecutus sum iustitiam. Et audi caput nostrum eiulans in passione: Et proiecerunt me dilectum, tanquam mortuum abominatum. Parum erat mortuum, quare abominatum? Quia crucifixum. Etenim haec mors crucis magna apud eos abominado erat, non intelligentes in prophetia dictum esse: Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno (Deut 21,23). Non enim ipse attulit mortem, sed hic invenit de maledicto primi hominis propagatam (Gal 3:10): et eamdem mortem nostram suscipiens in ligno suspendit, quae venerat de peccato. Ergo ne putarent aliqui, sicut putant quídam haeretici, Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum falsem carnem habuisse, et non veram mortem in intersection solvisse; intendit hoc propheta, et ait: Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno. 27 [v.22}. Ne derelinquas me, Domine Deus meus, ne discesseris a me. Dicamus in illo, dicamus per illum; ipse enim interpellat pro nobis (Rom 8:34): et dicamus, Ne derelinquas me, Domine Deus meus. Et turnen dixerat, Deus meus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti (Mt 27,46, et Ps 21,2) et dicit, Deus meus, ne discesseris a me. If a corpore does not recedit, recessit a capite? Cuius ergo vox erat, nisi primi hominis. Ex illo ergo se ostendens veram carnem portare, dicit: Deus meus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti? Non illum dimisit Deus. Si te non dimittit credentem in se, Christum dimitteret Pater et Filius et Spiritus sanctus unus Deus? Sed personam in se transfiguraverat primi hominis. Scimus dicente Apostólo, quia vetus homo noster confixus est cruci cum illo (Rom 6,6). Non autem careremus vetustate, nisi crucifigeretur in firmitate. Ad hoc enim venit, ut renovemur in illo: quia desiderando eum et passionem eius imitando renovamur. Ergo vox erat infirmitatis, vox erat nostra, qua dictum est, Quare me dereliquisti? Inde ibi dictum est, Verba delictorum meorum (Ps 21,2): tanquam diceret, Haec verba ex persona peccatoris in me transfigurata sunt. Ne discesseris a me.

28 [v. 23 ]. Come help me, oh Lord of my health! This is health, brothers, about which the prophets spoke, as the apostle Saint Peter says, and those who sought it did not receive it, but they inquired and predicted, and we came and found what they inquired about. But we have not received it yet; After us others will be born, and they will see that not even they will receive it, and yet they will pass away, so that all of us may still receive, at the end of the day, the denarius of salvation with the patriarchs, the prophets, and the apostles. You know, without a doubt, that the day laborers or workers brought to the vineyard at different times received the same salary. Therefore also the prophets, the apostles, the martyrs and we and all those who come after us until the end of the world must receive eternal health at the end of the age, so that praising God and no longer groaning, but, having united ourselves to Him, for whom until the end we have sighed and have rejoiced in hope, already contemplating the glory of God and seeing his face eternally, we will praise Him without decay, without deceit and without sin. Eternally we will live in that city where our good, our light, our happiness and our life is God. Whatever is our good, for which we work as pilgrims on earth, we will find it in Him. In Him will be our rest, which, remembering Him now, we must grieve. Let us remember that Saturday for whose memory so many things have been said, and we must say so many that we never remain silent, but speaking with the heart, not with the mouth, since we must remain silent with the mouth so that we can speak with the heart. 28 [v.23]. Intend in adiutorium metim, Domine salutis meae. Ipsa est salus, fratres, de qua salute exquisierunt Prophetae, sicut dicit apostolus Petrus: et non acceperunt qui exquisierunt; sed inquisierunt et praenuntiaverunt, et venimus nos et invenimus quod illi exquisierunt (1 Petr 1,10.12). Et ecce nos nondum accepimus; et nascentur post nos, et invenient quod nec ipsi accipient et transient: ut omnes simul in fine diei cum Patriarchis, et Prophetis, et Apostolis denarium salutis accipiamus. Etenim nostis mercenarios vel operarios diversis temporibus ductos ad vineam, mercedem tamen pariter acceperunt (Mt 20:9).

Et Prophetae ergo, et Apostoli, et Martyres, et nos, et qui post nos erunt usque in finem saeculi, in ipso fine accepturi sumus salutem sempiternam; ut contemplantes gloriam Dei, et eius faciem intuentes, eum laudemus in aeternum, sine defectu, sine aliqua poena iniquitatis, sine aliqua perversitate peccati, laudantes Deurn, et non iara suspirantes, sed inhaerentes illi, cui usque in finem suspiravimus, et in spe laetati sumus. In illa enim civitate erimus, ubi bonum nostrum Deus est, lumen Deus est, pañis est, vita Deus est: quidquid est bonum nostrum, a quo peregrinantes laboramus, in illo inveniemus. In illo erit quies, quam moda reminders necesse est ut doleamus. Illud enim sabbatum recordamur, in cuius recollectione tanta dicta sunt, et nos tanta dicere debenmus, et dicentes nunquam tacere, non ore, sed corde: quia sic ore tacemus, ut corde clamare possimus.
Deprecation of the troubled righteous

1 fv.l]. The title of this psalm that we have now sung and undertaken to expound is the following: For the end, to Idito; song of David. We must listen and hear the voices or words of a man called Idito. If each one of us could be another Idito, in what he sings, he finds and hears himself. You will know who was called Idito if you know the ancient origin of the names; Let us hear how this name is interpreted, and in the same interpretation let us seek the knowledge of the truth. According to what I have investigated, I have been able to find in these names that were translated from the Hebrew language to the Latin language by men dedicated to the study of the divine letters, Idito is interpreted: the one who crosses or passes them. Then who is this one who crosses?, or who does he cross?, because it was not written briefly about the one who crosses, but rather the one who crosses THEM. Do you sing, then, passing through or singing through? Whether he sings passing through or passes through singing, yet we have recently sung the song of the one who passes through. May we also be passersby, may God see it, to whom we have sung. But if anyone sang while passing through, let him be glad for being what he sang; But if you sang while still attached to the earth, understand that it is good for you to be what you sang. Cuiusdam ergo, qui vocatur ldithun, voices exspectandae et audiendae sunt: ​​et si esse unusquisque nostrum potuerit ldithun, in eo quod cantat invenit se, et audit se. Videris enim quis vocatus fuerit ldithun secundum hominum priscam nativitatem: nos autem audiamus quid interpretetur hoc nomen, et in ipsa interpretatione nominis quaeramus intelligentiam veritatis. Sicut ergo inquirentes reperire potuimus in eis nominibus, quae nobis a studiosis litterarum divinarum ex hebraeo eloquio in latinum interpretata sunt, ldithun interpretatur, Transiliens eos. Quis est ergo iste transiliens? vel quos transilivit? quia, Transiliens, non nude positum est; thirst, Transiliens eos. Transiliendo enim cantat, still singing transilit? Sive transiliendo cantet, sive canto transiliat, transilientis tamen Canticum paulo ante cantavimus: utrum et nos simus transilientes, viderit Deus cui cantavimus. Sed si quis transiliens cantavit, gaudeat se esse quod cantavit: si quis autem terrae adhuc inhaerens cantavit, optet esse quod cantavit. stuck to the earth and hunched towards the ground, who think about the smallest things and put hope in the transitory. Whom then did he pass through but the stragglers? 2. You know that certain psalms are entitled Canticle of degrees or steps. In the Greek language it is evident what ccvafJaOuwv (degrees or steps) means. "Anabazmi" are steps of a ladder, but they go up, not down. The Latin, as he could not express himself properly, spoke in general, and by saying "gradus" (step or step) he expressed an ambiguous concept, without determining whether they were steps that went up or down. But since there are no conversations or speeches in which the voices cannot be heard, the preceding language explains the following, and thus one clarifies what was ambiguous in the other. As there, that is, in that 18th psalm, a man sings going up, so here, in this one, he sings going through. This climb and transit are not executed with feet, nor with stairs, nor with wings; However, if you look inside the man, they are done with feet, with a ladder and with wings. For if they are not carried out with feet, how does the inner man say: Let not the foot of pride be placed on me? If they are not carried out with a ladder, what is the point of the one that Jacob saw, on which the angels went up and down? If they are not carried out with wings, why is it said: Who will give me wings like those of the dove, to fly and rest? In corporeal things, the feet are one thing, the ladder another, and the wings another; In the spiritual, the feet, the ladder and the wings are the affections of good will. Let's go, let's go up, let's fly with them. When someone hears this one who crosses and who rebus transeuntibus spemponentes, transilivit iste qui vocatur Transiliens eos. Quos enim transilivit, nisi remnants? 2. Nostis quosdam psalmos inscribed Canticum graduum: et ibi quidem in graeca lingua satis evidens est, quid dicat ávapaepwv. Anabathmi enim gradus sunt, sed ascendentium, non descendentium. Latinus quia non potuit proprie dicere, generaliter dixit: et quoniam gradus appellavit, ambiguum reliquit utrum ascendentium essent, an descendentium. Sed quia non sunt loquelue ñeque sermones, quorum non audiantur voices eorum (Ps 18,4), exponit sequentem lingua praecedens; et fit certum in alia, quod ambiguum erat in alia. Quomodo ergo ibi ascendens quidam cantat, sic et hic transiliens.

Est autem haec ascensio et ist transilitio, non pedibus, non scalis, non pennis; And also if interiorem horninem atiendas, et pedibus, et scalis, et pennis. Nam si non pedibus, quomodo dicit homo interior, Non venial mihi pes superbiae? (Ps 35,12). Yes non scalis, quid sunt quas vidit Iacob, ubi weret ascendants Angelí et descendants? (Gen 28:12). Pro iniquitate erudisti hominem, et contabescere jecisti sicut araneam animam meam. Multum est quod intelligit iste Idithun: si quis cum illo intelligat, si quis cum illo transiliat. Dicit enim in argutionibus Dei se defecisse, et vult a se amoveri flagella, quoniam ipse est qui fecit illum. Qui fecit, ipse reficiat; et qui creavit, ipse recreet. Sed tamen quod ita

brothers, what was done without reason? You indoctrinated, he says, man against iniquity. All my weakness, my weakness, my cry, which emanates from the depths of the heart, all this is due to iniquity, and in everything you taught me, you did not condemn me. You indoctrinated man against iniquity. Hear it more clearly in another psalm: It is good for me to have humbled myself so that I may learn your justifications. I was humiliated, and it is good for me: it is a punishment and it is a gift. What reserve after the punishment does he who, in response to the gift, inflicted the punishment? He himself said to himself: I was humiliated, and he saved me; and also: It is good for me to have humbled myself, so that I may learn your justifications. You indoctrinated man against iniquity; and likewise what was written: You put or establish pain in the command, could not be said to God except by the one who passes by, because it could not be seen except by the one who passes through. He established, he says, pain in the mandate. You imposed a precept of pain on me. You inform my pain, you do not leave it formless, but you give it form, and, ordered my pain, inflicted by you, constitutes, in order to free me through you, a precept for me. It was said that you establish the pain, not that you simulate it, that you form the pain, that you shape the pain, in the style of 'as the craftsman shapes (fingit) an object, by whose operation it bears the name of figulus, of craftsman. Well, figulus (artificer) is derived from fingendo (the one who forms). Then you indoctrinated man against iniquity. I see myself surrounded by evils, I see myself involved in punishments, and in you I see no iniquity. Therefore, if I am between punishments and in you I do not find iniquity, it only remains that you indoctrinate man against iniquity. defecit, ut velit se et recrean et reformari, isine causa putamus, fratres, factum Fuisse? Pro iniquitate, inquit, erudisti hominem. Totum quod defeci, quod infirmus sum, quod de imo clamo, hoc totum pro iniquitate: et in hoc erudisti, non damnasti: Pro iniquitate erudisti hominem. Audi hoc planius ex alio psalmo: Bonum est mihi, quod humiliasti me, ut discam iustijicationes tuas (Ps 118,71). Et humiliatus sum, et bonum est mihi: et poena est, et gratia est. Quid servat post poenam, who per gratiam exhibit poenam? Ipse enim est de quo dictum est, Humiliatus sum, et salvum me fecit (Ps 114,6): et, Bonum est mihi quod humiliasti me, ut discam iustijicationes tuas.

Pro iniquitate erudisti hominem. Et quod scripturn est, Qui fingís dolorem in praecepto (Ps 93,20), Deo dici nonnisi a transiliente potuit; quia nonnisi a transiliente videri potuit. Fingís, inquit, dolorem in praecepto, de dolore praeceptum mihi facis. Formas ipsum dolorem meum: non eum relinquis informam, sed forma illum: et formatus dolor meus inflictus a te praeceptum mihi erit, ut liberer a te. Fingís enim, dictum est, dolorem, forms dolors, plasmas dolorem, non simulas dolorem: quomodo fingit artifex, unde et figulus dicitur a fingendo. Ergo, Pro iniquitate erudisti hominem. Video me in malis, video me in poena, et apud te non video iniquitatem. Si ergo ego in poena sum et apud te iniquitas non est, nonne restat ut pro iniquitate erudieris hominem?

18. And how did you teach? Show this teaching, oh Idiot! Explain how you were taught. And you consumed my soul like a spider. This is the teaching. What is more consumed than the spider? I'm talking about the same animal. Although also, what is more consumed than spider web? See also the same animal how despicable it is; lightly place your finger on it; It is his ruin. There is nothing more despicable. Such did you do to my soul, he says, teaching me in the face of iniquity. As the teaching made me weak, a certain strength was a vice. I see that some anticipated and understood; But, for the sake of those who walk faster, those who walk more slowly should not be abandoned, so that they may continue the course of the sermon for a long time. I said this; understand this. If the teaching of the righteous God made this weakness, a certain strength was a vice. Man was disliked because of a certain strength, but was indoctrinated by weakness; He was displeased by pride and was indoctrinated by humility. All the proud consider themselves strong. Therefore many, coming from the east and the west, triumphed, so that they will sit with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. Why did they triumph or win? Because they didn't want to be strong. What does it mean they didn't want to be strong? They feared to boast about themselves, that is, they did not establish their justice, in order to submit in this way to that of God. Finally, when the Lord said: Many will come from the east and the west and will sit with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, and the children of the kingdom, that is, the Jews, who did not know the justice of God and who wanted to establish their own, will go to you18. Et quomodo, crudisti? Dic ipsam eruditionem, or Idithun, quomodo eruditus is? Et tabescere jecisti sicut araneam animam mectrn. Haec is eruditio. Quid tabidius aranea? Animal ipsum dico. Hoc dixi, hoc intelligite: Si eruditio iusti Dei hanc infirmitatem fecit, fortitudo quaedam erat vitium. Fortitudine quadam displicuit homo, ut erudiretur infirmitate: quia superbia quadam displicuit, ut erudiretur humilitate. Fortes se esse dicunt omnes superbi. exterior fogs; Remember that faith of the centurion, one of many Gentiles, who was so weak and not strong, that he said: I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof. He who was not worthy of receiving Christ into his dwelling had already received him into his heart. In fact, the Teacher of humility, the Son of man, had already found a place to lay his head on the centurion's chest. The Lord, heeding the words of this centurion, said to those who followed him: Truly I tell you, I found so much evil in no one in Israel. He found this one weak; to the Israelites, strong; So in the midst of them he said: The healthy do not need a doctor, but the sick do. For this reason, that is, for this humility, many will come from the east and the west and will sit with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven; -but the children of the kingdom will go into the outer darkness. See that you are mortal, that you carry flesh that is corrupted, and you will fall like one of the princes: you will die like men and you will fall like the devil. What good does the medicine of mortality benefit you? The proud devil, like the angel that he is, has no flesh; You, on the other hand, who received mortal flesh and who, nevertheless, do not take advantage of it to humiliate yourself for so much weakness, will fall like one of the princes. The main grace of God's benefit consists in forcing us to confess our weakness, so that whatever good we can do, whatever we are capable of doing, we may do so in him, so that he who boasts may glory in the Lord. When I am weak, then, he says, I am strong. You taught man against iniquity and consumed my soul like a spider's web.

19. Yet every living man troubles in vain. Return to what you commemorated shortly before. Although here he advances or progresses, every man who lives is troubled in vain, since he certainly lives in uncertainty. Who is even sure of his good? He is vainly disturbed. Give your cares to the Lord; deposit in Him everything you are worried about; May He sustain you and keep you. What is true on earth if it is not death? Consider, without leaving one, all the things of this life, whether good or bad, or concerning justice or iniquity. What is true here if it is not death? You advanced: you know what you are today, you don't know what you will be tomorrow. You are a sinner: you know what you are today, you do not know what you will be tomorrow. You hope to get money; It is uncertain that you will get it. You hope to have a wife; You don't know if you will have it and what it will be. You hope to have children; You don't know if they will be born to you, and if they are born to you, you don't know if they will live, and if they live, you don't know if they will be good or bad. Wherever you turn, you will encounter uncertainty; only death is certain. You are poor; You don't know if you have to be rich. You are ignorant; You don't know if you have to enlighten yourself. You are sick; You don't know if you have to recover your health. You were born; You know that you have to die, but, having certain death, you do not know the day you will die. Among all these uncertain things, where only death is certain, and its hour uncertain, and of which only one guards with great diligence and in no way avoids it, every man who lives is troubled in vain. 20 [v. 13]. I am a tenant. However, I am also a tenant before my God, next to whom the house must remain received. But what is the house to which one must emigrate starting from this tenancy? He will be resurrected at the end and will be condemned with the devil to eternal fire. So what does it mean I won't exist if it doesn't refer to Idito? What is being and not being? He noticed that end or whereabouts as far as his heart allowed, as far as the insight of his mind was capable, which he desired to be shown to him by saying: Let me know, Lord, my end or whereabouts. He contemplated what was the number of his days; He observed that all the things that exist here below are not in comparison to that being, and that is why he says that he does not exist. The things above remain; those below are changeable, mortal and fragile. Eternal pain, impregnated with depravity, does not end, because it has no end. He contemplated that blessed region, that homeland, that house in which the saints participate in eternal life and the immutable truth, and he fears going outside of there where being is not present, and he desires to be where the supreme being is. Placed in the middle of both mansions, still fearing this comparison, he says: Forgive me so that I may be relieved before I go away and no longer exist. Vero I fear, lest, as the serpent deceived Eve with his cunning, so your followers become depraved, losing their purity towards Christ. This ancient and adulterous serpent tries to violate virginity, not that of the flesh, but that of the heart. As the adulterous man rejoices in his wickedness when he violates the flesh, so the devil rejoices when he violates the mind. As patience was necessary for our elders against the lion, so vigilance against the dragon is also necessary for us. The persecution of the Church never ceases, whether from the lion or the dragon, and it is to be feared more when it deceives than when it is cruel. In another time he incited Christians to renounce Christ; In this he teaches them to deny Christ; then he impelled, now he teaches; then he used violence, now he used tricks; then you could hear him roar; Now, presenting itself meekly insinuating and hovering, it is difficult to notice it. It is known how he then forced Christians to deny Christ. He also tried to attract them to him so that they would renounce Christ; but they, confessing Christ, were crowned. Now he teaches to deny Christ, and, by deceiving them, he does not want to appear to separate them from Christ.

So what do certain heretics say to the Catholic Christian now? Come; be a christian. It is said: Be a Christian, so that it may be answered: Am I not? It is one thing to say come, be a Christian, and another come, deny Christ. The latter is a very clear evil: the lion's roar is heard from afar, and is avoided from afar. The elusive dragon creeps closer, with hidden deceptions, crawling with tenuous steps, whispering with a cunning hiss, and does not say: Deny Christ. For who of the crowned martyrs heard him speak in this way? But it says: Be a Christian. But the Christian, upon feeling or perceiving this strange voice, if the inoculated poison has not yet penetrated him, responds: I am truly a Christian. On the contrary, if he is moved and has been bitten by the dragon's tooth, he responds: Why do you tell me to be a Christian?; So what, am I not a Christian? Then the dragon answers: No. Am I not really? No. Then make me a Christian now if I am not. Come; (I will make you). Therefore, when the (Donatist) bishop asks you who you are, he does not want you to say: I am a Christian or faithful, but rather he wants you to say: I am not, so that you can be. Well, upon hearing the manifestation of the faithful Christian, he will not dare to rebaptize you (because it is prohibited by imperial criminal law). But, if he hears that you are not a Christian, he will provide you with baptism, as if you did not have him, and thus he appears as if he had no guilt, because he acts according to your confession. I ask you, oh heretic, how is it that you consider yourself blameless? What do I hear in this manifestation of yours? That you do not deny, but he is the one who denies? If the one who denies is to blame, what is the fault of the one who teaches the one who denies to deny? Are you perhaps exempt from guilt, since, being a Christian, you do, by teaching, what the pagan did by threatening?

3. How did it help you? What did he do to you? And he brought me out of the abyss of misery and the miry quagmire, and set my feet on the rock, and straightened my steps. And he put a new song in my mouth, a hymn to our God. Our Lord shows us by these things that he is a faithful promiser and a splendid giver. Now what did he do? He brought me out of the abyss of misery. What is the abyss of misery? The chasm of iniquity coming from carnal lust. This is the same as and of the miry quagmire. Where did he get you from? Of a certain abyss. That is why you cried in another psalm: From the depths I cried to you, O Lord! Those who cry out from the depths are not completely in the abyss, since the same cry rises. There are some who are in the depths of the abyss; These are those who do not perceive that they are in it; these are the proud despisers, not the pious suppliants; not the anointed ones who pray, but those who are elsewhere designated by Scripture when it says: The sinner, when he has fallen into the depths of wickedness, despises. Those who think it is not enough to be a sinner and not only do not confess their sins, but defend them, find themselves in a very deep abyss. But he who cried out from the depths, already raised his head from the depths of the abyss to cry out and was heard and brought out of the abyss, from misery and from the miry quagmire. He already has the faith that he lacked, he already has the hope, which he lacked.

Because you are good, I consider that you are just; I love the good and fear the just. Love and fear guide me, because your mercy and your truth sustained me continually. Why do they support them? Why shouldn't we get away from his gaze? Because untold evils surrounded me. Who will count the sins? Who will enumerate the iniquities of others and their own? Under the accumulation of them he groaned who said: Cleanse me from my hidden errors, Lord, and forgive your servant from those of others. As if our own were few, we are burdened with those of others; I fear for myself, I fear for the good brother, I tolerate the bad brother; and under this accumulation, what will become of me if God's mercy ceases? 77/', Lord, do not go away; be close Who is the Lord close to? Of those who troubled his heart. He is far from the proud, he is close to the humble. The Lord is exalted and looks upon the humble. But the proud do not think that they are hidden, for he knows them from afar. From afar he knew the Pharisee who boasted about himself, and from up close he helped the publican who repented. The former boasted of his good works and hid his wounds; He did not boast of his merits, but rather showed his wounds. He approached the doctor and recognized himself as ill; I knew I had to heal; However, he did not dare to raise his eyes to heaven; beat his chest; He did not forgive himself so that God would forgive him, he recognized himself as a sinner so that God would not take his mistakes into account, he punished himself so that God would deliver him. These are the voices heard here; Let us listen to them with religiosity and love with piety. Let us say these things with our hearts, with our tongues and with the most appreciable part of our entire being.

No one believes himself to be righteous, for he who speaks lives, lives and may he live! He still lives in this world, he still lives with the mortal; If (it is true) that the spirit lives by righteousness, (it is no less true that) the body is dead by sin. And the corruptible body depresses the soul, and the terrestrial dwelling aggravates the thought that reconsiders many things. Then you have to cry out, groan, confess, not exalt yourself, not boast, not boast about your merits, because, if you have something that you can boast about, what have you not received? But the precious blood shed served to multiply the Church; The death of the martyrs also constituted the sowing. The death of his righteous is precious in the eyes of the Lord. They multiplied more and more prophetavit quia oportebat Iesum mori pro populo et gente (lo 11,47-51). Tamen illi cum viderent populum post illum iré, dixerunt, Quando morietur, et peribit nomen eius: id est, cum occiderimus eum, iam nomen eius non erit in terra, nec seducet aliquos mortuus; sed ipsa eius interfectione intelligent homínes, quia hominem sequebantur, quia non erat in eo spes salutis; et deserent nomen eius, et non erit. Mortuus est; et non periit nomen eius, sed seminatum est nomen eius; mortuus est, sed granum Fuit, quo mortificato seges continuo exsurgeret (Ib. 12,25). Glorificato ergo Domino nostro Iesu Christo, coeperunt multo magis multoque numerosius credere in illum; et coeperunt membra eius audire quod caput audiebat.

Iam ergo Domino nostro Iesu Christo in cáelo constituto, et ipso in nobis in tetra laborante, dixerunt adhuc inimici eius: Quando morietur, et peribit nomen eius. Hinc enim persecutions diabolus in Ecclesia concitavit ad perdendum nomen Christi. Nisi forte putatis, fratres, quia illi Pagani when saeviebant in Christianos, non hoc sibi dicebant, delere nomen Christi de terra. Ut moreretur iterum Christus non in capite, sed in corpore suo, occisi sunt et martyres. Ad multiplicandam Ecclesiam valuit sanctus sanguis effusus, seminationi accessit et mors marryrum. Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors iustorum eius (Ps 115,15). Multiplicati sunt magis magisque Christiani, et non est impletum quod dixerunt ini-

Defeated twice or, if it doesn't matter to you, three times, since Christ died and his name did not perish; The martyrs died and the Church multiplied more, since the name of Christ spread to all nations. The one who predicted his death and his resurrection, the one who predicted the death of his martyrs and their triumph, is the same one who predicted his future Church; If he told the truth twice, should he lie the third time? In understanding that he emptied himself by taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of man and found in clothing as a man. Rich before the Father, poor before us-

inici, Quando morielur, et peribit nomen eh/s. Adhuc et moda dicitur. others; rich in heaven, poor on earth; rich being God, poor being man. Are you disturbed because you see man, because you contemplate the flesh, because you consider death, because you mock the cross? Does this bother you? Look at the poor and the needy. What does this mean? Understand that where weakness was manifested to you, divinity is hidden there. He is rich because he is; poor, because that's how you were. However, their poverty is our wealth, as their weakness is our strength, as their folly is our wisdom, as their mortality is our immortality. What does poor mean? Attend; do not measure Him by the poverty of others. He who became poor came to fill the poor. Therefore, open the bosom of faith and receive the poor, so that you may not remain poor. 2 [v. 2]. Blessed is he who cares for the needy and the poor; In the evil day the Lord will deliver him. The fateful day will come; It will come whether you want it or not; The day of judgment will come, a bad day if you had not cared for the poor and the needy. What you don't want to believe now will finally become apparent. And you will not flee when it is revealed because you did not believe when it was hidden. You are invited to believe what you do not see, so that you do not blush when you see it. Then take care of the needy and the poor, that is, Christ. Observe the riches that are hidden in Him despite seeing Him poor. In Him are contained locked up all the treasures of wisdom and science. Because he is God, he will deliver you on the evil day; Because he was a man, he resurrected, made the human thing better and ascended to heaven; dives in cáelo, pauper in terra; dives Deus, pauper homo. Hoc te ergo turbat, quod hominem vides, quod carnem intueris, quod mortem respicis, quod cruzem irrides? Hoc you disturbed? Intellige super egenum et pauperem. Quid est hoc? Intellige, quia ubi tibí expósita est infirmitas, ibi latet divínitas. Dives, quia sic est; pauper, quia iam your sic eras. Be tamen paupertas ipsius, divitiae nostrae sunt: ​​quomodo infirmitas ipsius fortitudo nostra est; quomodo stultum ipsius sapientia nostra est; quomodo mortalitas ipsius, immortalitas nostra est (1 Cor 1:30). Quid sit pauper, attend: non eum ex aliorum paupertate metiaris. Implere venit pauperes, qui pauper effectus est.

Propterea aperi sinum fidei; suscipe pauperem, ne pauper remaneas. 2 [v.2]. Beatus who inlelligit super egenum et pauperem, in die mala liberabit eum Dominus. Veniet enim dies mala: velis nolis, veniet; dies iudicii aderit, mala dies, si non intellexeris super egenum et pauperem. Quod enim moda non vis credere, manifestum erit in fine. Sed non fugies, eum fuerit manifestum, quia non credis eum est oceultum. Invitaris ut quod non vides credas, ne eum videris erubescas. Intellige ergo super egenum et pauperem, id est, super Christum; intellige in eo oceultas divitias, quem pauperem vides. In eo sunt enim omnes thesauri sapientiae et scientiae absconditi (Col 2,3). Hinc enim te in die mala liberabit, ex eo quod Deus est: ex eo autem quod homo est, et illud quod in illo humanum erat resuscitavit, et in melius convertit, in caelum levavit. Ule autem

that is in Him. He, who was God, and who wanted to have a single person in man and with man, could not increase or decrease, neither die nor be resurrected. He died because of man's weakness, not because he is God. Do not be surprised because he did not die in that he is the Word of God, since the soul of the martyr does not die either. Did we not recently hear the Lord say: Do not fear those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul? Therefore, if when the martyrs died their souls did not die, when Christ died, would the Word have to die? The Word of God is much more excellent than the soul of man, since the soul was made by God, and if it was made by God, it was made by the Word, since all things were made by Him. Therefore, since the soul, made by the Word, does not die, neither does the Word die, and as we say with complete truth that man has died although his soul does not die, we equally affirm with all truth that Christ died although his divinity did not die. Why did he die? Because (he became) needy and poor. Do not be disturbed by his death and keep you from contemplating divinity. Blessed is he who cares for the needy and the poor. Take care of the poor, the needy, the hungry, the thirsty, the pilgrims, the naked, the sick, the prisoners; Take care of this poor person, because, if you look at him, you take care of the One who said: I was hungry, I was thirsty, I was naked, I was a pilgrim and imprisoned. Thus the Lord will deliver you on the evil day. 3 [v.3j. And you contemplate your happiness. The Lord preserve him. The prophet wishes well the man who cares for the poor and the menesqui Deus est, qui unam personam habere in homine et cum nomine voluit, nec decrescere nec crescere potuit, nec mori nec resurgere. Mortuus est ex infirmitate hominis, caeterum Deus non moritur. Nam quod Verbum Dei non moritur, ne mireris, quando non moritur anima in martyre. Modo non audiebamus ipsum Dominum dicentem: Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere? (Mt 10,28). Ergo mororientibus martyribus animae Martyrum mortuae non sunt, et moriente Christo moriturum erat Verbum? Utique Verbum Dei multo amplius est quam anima hominis: quia anima hominis facta est a Deo; et si facta est a Deo, per Verbum facta est: quia omnia per ipsum facta sunt (lo 1,3). Ergo nec moritur Verbum, cum non moriatur anima facta per Verbum. Sed quomodo recte dicimus, Mortuus est homo, etsi anima ipsius non moriatur; sic recte dicimus, Mortuus est Christus, etsi divinitas eius non moriatur.

Mortuus unde? Quia egenus et pauper. Non te perstringat mors ipsius, et evertat te a contuenda divinitate. Beatas qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem. Réspice et pauperes, egentes, esurientes et sitientes, pilgrims, knots, aegrotos, in carcere constitutos: intellige et super talem pauperem, quia et si super talem intelligis, super illum intelligis qui dixit, Esurivi, sitivi, nudas, peregrinas, aeger, in carcere Fui (Mt 25, 35.36). Ita in die malignant eruet you Dorninus. 3 [v.3]. Et vide beatitudem tuam. Dorninus preserve! eum. Pro-

terous This wish is a promise. Let those who act in this way wait safely. May the Lord preserve him and quicken him. What does it mean to preserve and quicken you? What does le vivific refer to? To the future life. He who died is quickened. But can the dead care for the poor and the needy? It promises us that quickening of which the Apostle says: The body is certainly dead through sin, but the spirit is life through righteousness; If he who raised Christ from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies by his spirit dwelling in you. This is the vivification that is promised to those who care for the needy and the poor. But, as the Apostle says to Timothy, having the promise of the present life and the future, so that those who care for the poor and the needy do not think that they will be received in heaven, but abandoned on earth, and, therefore, only wait for what is to happen in eternity, and, as regards the present time, judge that God does not care for his saints and believers; where he pointed out what we should mainly expect by saying: The Lord preserves him and quickens him, he also attends to this life, for he adds: And he will make him happy on earth. Direct your gaze with Christian faith to this promise. God does not abandon you on earth and promises you something in heaven. Many bad Christians, observers of astronomical tables, inquisitors and contemplators of times and days, when rebuked by us or by some good and excellent Christians and told: Why do you do these things?, respond: Considering temporal life, this is pheta bene optat homini intelügenti super egenum et pauperem. This optatio promissio est; securi exspectent qui hoc agunt. Dorninus preserve! eum, et vivijicet eum. Quid est, conservet eum, et vivijicet eum? Quo pertinet, vivificet eum? Ad Futurem Vitam. Vivificatur enim qui mortuus erat. Numquid autem potest mortuus intelligere super egenum et pauperem? Sed vivificationem nobis illam promittit, de qua dicit Apostoius: Corpus quidem mortuum est propter peccatum, spiritus autem vita est propter iustitiam: si autem qui suscitavit Cbristum a mortuis habitat in vobis, qui suscitavit Cbristum a mortuis vivijicabit et mortalia corpora vestra propter inhabitantem Spiritum eius in vobis (Rom 8,10,11). Haec est ergo vivificatio quae promittitur intelügenti super egenum et pauperem.

Sed quia dicit Apostoius ad Timotheum, Promissionem habens vitae praesenlis et juturae (1 Tim 4:8); ne putarent illi qui intelligunt super egenum et pauperem, recipiendos quidem se esse in caelum, sed negligi in terra; et non sperarent nisi quod futurum est in aeternum, quod autem ad praesens est, putarent Deum non curare in sanctis et fidelibus suis; ubi dixit quod máxime exspectare debenmus, Dorninus conservet eum, et vivijicet eum; respexit ad istam vitam, Et beatum, inquit, faciat eum in terra. Erige ergo oculos in haec promissa christiana fide: non te deserit Deus in terra, et aliquid promittit in cáelo. Multi enim mali christiani inspectores ephemeridarum, et inquisitores atque observatores temporum et dierum, cum coe-

necessary. We are Christians with a view to eternal life, and we believe in Christ to give us eternal life; for this temporary life in which we find ourselves does not belong to his care. It only remains for them to say, in a few words, that God must be worshiped for eternal life, and the devil for present life. To this Christ himself responds: You cannot serve two masters. And you worship one for what you hope for in heaven, and you worship another for what you hope for on earth. How much better would you worship only Him who made heaven and earth! Will he who cared for the earth to exist abandon his image on earth? Then the Lord will preserve and give life to him who cares for the needy and the poor. What's more, even if it gives him life in eternity, it will make him happy on earth.

4. And he will not deliver him into the hands of his enemies. This enemy is the devil. When anyone hears these words, do not understand that it is your enemy, man. Perhaps he was already thinking about his neighbor, the one with whom he was fighting, the one who tried to take away his property, the one who was trying to force him to sell his house. Do not think about these, but think about the enemy of whom the Lord says: The enemy man did this. This is the one who suggests that he be praised for earthly things. Like this enemy, he cannot banish the Christian name, since he sees that he is defeated by the fame and praise of Christ, and that in the death of the martyrs he declared himself victorious, but they were crowned, and he warns that he cannot convince men that

Christ does not exist and who hardly deceives by reviling Christ, tries to deceive by praising Him. What did you say before? Who do you worship? Even a dead Jew, crucified; even a despicable man, who could not keep death from him. When he sees that before his name the human race crowds, when he sees that before the name of the Crucified the (pagan) temples are demolished, the idols are destroyed, the sacrifices are extinguished, and that all these things foretold by the prophets are contemplated by men full of admiration, and who now cease to revile Christ, he puts on the mask of praising Christ and begins to depart from the faith in another way. The Christian law (he says) is excellent, powerful, divine, ineffable; but who will fulfill it? Trample the lion and the dragon in the name of our Savior. Blaming without shame, the lion roared; cunningly praising, the dragon lays in wait. Believe the doubters, do not say: Who will accomplish this? If they boast of their strength, they will not fulfill it. Believe, putting hope in the grace of God; approach with trust; Come to be helped, not to be judged. All the faithful live trusting in the name of Christ. Each one, according to their condition, fulfills the precepts of Christ, whether they are spouses, celibates or virgins. All of them live as the Lord allows them to live, without boasting about their strength, because they know that they should glory in the Lord. What do you have that you haven't received? If you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it? Nomedigas: Who will fulfill this? Fulfills it in me He who came rich to the poor, or rather, poor to the poor,

perint ibi obiurgari a nobis, vel a quibusdam bonis melioribusque christianis, quare ista faciant, responder: Haec propter tempus hoc necessaria sunt; christiani autem sumus propter vitam aeternam; propterea in Christum credidimus, ut det nobis vitam aeternam; nam vita ista temporalis in qua versamur, ad curam ipsius non pertinet. Relinquitur, ut hoc breviter dicant, ut propter vitam aeternam Deus, et propter vitam praesentem diabolus colatur. Respondet illis ipse Christus: Non potestis duobus dominis I will serve (Mt 6:24). Et alium colis propter id quod exspectas in cáelo, et alium colis propter id quod exspectas in terra: quanto melius unum colis, qui fecit caelum et terram? Who curavit ut esset terra, imaginem suam negligit in terra? Ergo, Conservet eum Dominus et vivijicet eum, intelligentem super egenum et pauperem. Insuper quamvis in aeternum vivificet, beatum jaciat eum in terra. 4. Et non tradat eum in manus inimici eius. Inimicus ille diabolus est. Nenio attendat inimicum suum hominem, quando audit verba ista. Iam forte de vicino suo cogitabat, de illo qui eum illo litem in foro habebat, de illo qui illi vult auferre possessionem, qui illum vult premere ut vendet illi domum suam. NoJite ista cogitare; sed illum inimicum cogitate, de quo dicit Dominus, Inimicus homo hoc fecit (Ib. 13,28). Ipse est enim qui suggerit ut propter res terrenas colatur; quia non potest evertere nomen christianum inimicus iste: vidit enim se vietum fame et laudibus Christi, vidit in eo quod occidit martyres Christi, illos coronatos, et se

triumphatum; et coepit non posse hoc persuadere hominibus, quod nihil sit Christus; et quia vituperando Christum, iam difficile decipit; laudando Christum, conatur decipere. Antea quid saybat? but full to the void. Thinking these things, this man, since he looks out for the needy and the poor and does not despise the poverty of Christ, understanding the riches of Christ, became happy on earth, and thus does not fall into the hands of his enemy, who wants to induce him to worship God for heavenly things and worship the devil for earthly things. He will not deliver him into the hands of his enemy. 5 [v.4]. The Lord will help you. Where? Perhaps in heaven, perhaps in eternal life, to let him worship the devil for earthly need, for the needs of this life? There is no such thing. For you have promise of the present life and the future. For you came to earth the one who made heaven and earth. In short, pay attention to what he says: The Lord will help him on the bed of pain. The bed of pain is the weakness of the flesh. Do not say: I cannot contain, endure and restrain my flesh. You will be helped so that you can. The Lord will give you strength in the bed of your pain. The bed supported you, you did not support it. You were paralyzed in it; but he is present who says to you: Take up your bed and go to your house. The Lord will help you on the bed of pain. Now he turns to the Lord as if we were asking him: Why, if God helps us, do we endure so many evils in this life, so many scandals, so much work, so much iniquity on the part of the flesh and the world? He turns to God and tells us the recipe for his medicine saying: In his illness you changed all his trousseau. What does it mean that during his illness you changed all his trousseau? By trousseau or bed we understand something earthly. Every sick soul seeks in this life something earthly in which to rest, because it can hardly continually endure the intensity of work and of the mind directed toward God. Therefore search for super egenum et pauperem, et non aspernatur paupertatem Christi, intelligit divitías Christi, fit beatus in terra: et non traditur in manus inimici sui, volentis ei persuadere ut Deus colatur propter caelestia, diabolus colatur propter terrena. Et ad ipsum Dominum convertít se, tanquam quaereretur, Quare ergo cum opem ferat nobis Deus, mucho mala patimur in ista vita, tanquam scandala, so many labors, so much restlessness in carnis et saeculi? convertit se ad Deum, et tanquam consilium medicinale eius nobis exponens: Totum stratum eius, inquit, vertisti in injirmitate eius. Quid est." Totum stratum eius vertisti in injirmitate eius? Per stratum intelligitur ali-

yes something on earth where you can rest and how to relieve yourself with a short break at work. Even the innocent go in search of this. Now we do not talk about the desires of bad men, many of whom rest in theaters, recreate themselves in the circus, in the amphitheater, in games; others, in drunkenness, in adultery, in plunder, and many others, in deceit and fraudulent schemes. In all these things men recreate and rest. What does it mean to rest? They delight in this. Let us leave all these things aside and consider the innocent man: he rests in his house, in his family, in his wife, in his children, in poverty, in his small estate, in the vineyard planted with his hands, in some building built with his effort; The innocent rest in these things; However, God wants us to love only eternal life, and mixes bitterness with these as innocent delights, so that we may also endure tribulations with them and our entire trousseau or bed may change in our illness. You moved all his trousseau to him during his illness. Do not complain when you endure some tribulations in the things you innocently possess, since you are taught to love the best things through the tribulation of the least. The traveler who walks towards his homeland may not love the inn instead of his home. You changed all his trousseau or bed in his illness. 6 [v.5]. Why does this happen? Because he scourges everyone he receives as a son. And why this? Because, when he sinned, he was called quid terrenum. Omnis anima infirma in hac vita quaerit sibi aliquid terrenum ubi requiescat; quoniam intentionem laboris et mentis extentae in Deum difficile potest perpetuo tolerare: aliquid sibi in terra conquirit ubi requiescat et quodammodo pausetione quadam recumbat, veluti sunt ista quae diligunt et innocentes. Ñeque enim de cupiditatibus malorum nunc loquendum est, quia multi acquiescunt in theatris, multi acquiescunt in circus, in amphitheater, multi acquiescunt in alea; multi in luxuria popinarum, multi in libidine adulteriorum, multi in violentiis rapinarum, multi in dolo et insidiis fraudium: acquiescunt in his omnibus homines. "Quid est, acquiescunt?" Delectantur illic. Sed removeamus haec omnia, ad innocentem hominem veniamus: acquiescit in domo sua, in familia sua, in coniuge, in filiis, in paupertate, in praediolo suo, in novella manibus suis consita, in aedificio aliquo suo studio fabricato: acquiescunt innocentes in his.

Sed tamen Deus volens nos amorem non habere nisi vitae aeternae, et istis velut innocentibus delectationibus miscet amaritudines; ut et in his patiamur tribulationes, et universum stratum nostrum vertit in infirmitate nostra. Universum stratum eius vertisti in infirmitate eius. Non ergo conqueratur, quando in his quae innocenter habet, patitur aliquas tribulationes. Docetur amare meliora per amaritudinem inferiorum: ne viator tendens ad patriam, stabulum amet pro domo sua. Universum stratum eius vertisti in injirmitate eius. 6 [v.5]. Sed quare ista? Quia flagellat omnem filium quem recipit (Hebr 12:6). Quare ist? Quia peccanti homini dictum est: In labore vultus

to man: In the sweat of your face you will eat bread. Therefore man must know that he suffers these punishments because of sin, in which our entire trousseau is changed in our illness. Think back and say what follows: I said: Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, because -I sinned against you. O Lord, exercise me in tribulation; for you, who did not forgive the Only Begotten, determine that everyone whom you will receive as a son must be scourged. He was certainly tormented without having sin; and I say: Lord, have mercy on me; Heal my soul, because I have sinned against you. If he who had no rot was cut, if our own medicine did not reject the medicinal fire, should we impatiently endure the doctor and the surgeon, that is, the one who exercises us in all kinds of tribulations and heals us from sin? Let us surrender ourselves fully into the hands of the doctor, for he is not mistaken, cutting off the healthy instead of the gangrenous; he knows what he listens to; He knows vice, since He created nature. Know what He Himself created and what was juxtaposed due to our lightness. He knows that he gave a precept to the healthy man so that he would not incur illnesses; Well he said in paradise •. Eat this and don't touch that. The healthy man did not listen to the doctor's order not to fall; Let the sick man listen now so that he can get up. I said: Lord, have mercy on me; Heal my soul, because I have sinned against you. I do not say: -I accuse fate of my works and my sins; I do not say: This was due to fate; I do not say: Venus made me an adulterer, Mars a thief, and Saturn a miser. I said: Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, because I sinned contui edes panetn tuum (Gen 3,19) - Ergo quia correptiones istas, in quibus universum stratum nostrum vertitur in infirmitate nostra, agnoscere debent homo propter peccata se pati; convertat se, et dicat quod sequitur: Ego dixi: Domine, miserere mei; sana animam meam, quoniam peccavi tibí. O Domine, in tribulationibus me exerce: flagellandum iudicas omnem filium quem recepturus es, qui nec Unique pepercisti. lile quidem sine peccato flagellatus est: ego autem dico, Miserere mei, sana animam meam, quoniam peccavi tibí. Si secatus est qui putredinem non habebat, si medica ipsa nostra ignem rnedicinalem non respuit; impatienter ferré debenmus urentem medicum et secantem, id est, omnibus tribulationibus nos exercentem, et a peccato sanantem?

Plan committamus nos medid manui; non enim errat, ut sanum pro putri secet: novit quod inspicit, novit vitium, quia ipse fecit naturam; quid ipse condidit, quid de nostra cupiditate accessit, discernit. Scit se healthy homini praeceptum dedisse, ne languorem incureret; dixisse in paradiso: Hoc manduca, et hoc noli (Ib. 2,16.17). Non audivit sanus medid praeceptum, ut non caderet; audit vel aegrotus, ut surgat. Ego said: Domine, miserere mei; sana animam meam, quoniam peccavi tibi. In factis meis, in peccatis meis non accuso fortunem, non dico, Hoc mihi fecit fatum; non dico, Adulterum me fecit Venus, et latronem me fecit Mars, et avarum me fecit Saturnus. Anger you. But did Christ say this? Did our Head, who had no sin, say this? Did the One who paid for what he had not stolen say it? Maybe the only free one among the dead said it? For he was free among the dead because he had no sin, since everyone who sins is a servant of sin. Did this one say it? Yes. He said it for his members; for the voice of his members is his voice, just as the voice of our head is our voice. We were in Him when He said: Sad is my soul until death. For he who had come to die was not afraid to die, nor did he who had the power to take life again refuse to die, but the members spoke for the head, and the head spoke for the members. In Him we find our voice when we say: Heal my soul, for I have sinned against you. We were in Him when He said: My God, my God, why have you abandoned me? In this 21st psalm, at the beginning of which this verse is found, it is said next: the words of my iniquities. What crimes are there in Him but those of our old man, who was crucified with Him so that the body of sin would be annulled so that from now on we would not serve sin? Let us say to Him and in Him: I said: Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, because I have sinned against you, 7 [v.6]. My enemies said evil of me: When will he die and perish his name? I already explained this; This is where I began the exposition of the psalm. In order to speak of other things, I have no need to repeat what was so recently recorded in your ears and hearts. quid hoc Christus? numquid hoc caput illud nostrum sine peccato? numquid ille qui ea quae non rapuit exsolvebat? (Ps 68,5) numquid ille solus in mortuís liber? (Ps 87.6). Liber enim in mortuis, quia sine peccato: quia omnis qui facit peccatum, servus est peccati (lo 8,34). Numquid ergo Ipse? Imo ipse ex membrís suis, quia vox membrorum ipsius vox ipsius; Quia et vox capitis nostri vox nostra. In illo enim eramus, when he said: Tristis_ est anima mea usque ad mortem (Mt 26,38). Non enim timebat mori, qui venerat mori; aut recusabat morí, qui potestatem habebat animam suam ponendi, et potestatem habebat iterum sumendi eam (lo 10,18): sed loquebantur membra in capite, et loquebatur caput pro membris. In illo ergo vocem nostram invenimus: Sana animam meam, quoniam peccavi tibi. In illo enim eramus, cum dixit: Deus meus, Deus meas, utquid me dereliquisti? (Mt 27,46).

In ipso enim psalmo ubi in capite híc versus est, consequenter dicitur Verba delictorum meorum (Ps 21,2). Quorum delictorum in illo, nisi quia vetus homo noster simul crucifixus est cum illo, ut evacuaretur corpus peccati, et ultra non serviamus peccato? (Rom 6,6). Ad illum et in illo dicamus: Ego dixi: Domine, miserere mei; sana animam meam, quoniam peccavi tibi. 7 [v.6]. Inimici mei dixerunt bad mihi: When I die, et penbit nornen eius. Iam ista diximus, et hinc coepimus; et ut alia dicamus, non opus est iterare, quod tam recenti sermone impressum est auribus et cordibus vestris.

8 [v.7]. And they came to see. What Christ suffered, the Church suffers; What the Head suffered, the members also suffer. Is the servant better than his Lord, or is the disciple superior to the Master? If they persecuted me, he says, they will also persecute you. If they called the father of families Beelzebui, how much more so their members. They came to see. Judas was next to our Head; He approached our Head to see, that is, to spy; not to know what he should believe, but to find a reason to deliver him. You see that he came in to see, and this rehearsal took place in our Head. What happened to the members after the ascension of our Head? Does not the apostle Saint Paul say:... because of the false brothers, interfering from the side, who sneaked in to spy on our freedom? Therefore, these who came in to spy are also hypocrites, perverse, malingerers, who adhere with feigned charity; spies of all the movements, of all the words of the saints; who look for hidden motives in everything, and what happens to them? Consider what follows: Their heart spoke vain things, that is, they speak with feigned charity. What they speak is vain, it is not true, it has no consistency. And since they spy to find something to accuse, what does it say? They heaped iniquity against themselves. The enemies, inventing slander, think they are great because they already have something to accuse. They heaped iniquity against themselves.. Against themselves, he says, not against me. Just as Judas accumulated iniquity against himself, not against Christ, in the same way the slanderers of the Church accumulate it against themselves, not against us, because it is also said about them in another place: 8 [v.7]. Et ingrediebantm ut viderent. Quod passus est Christus, patitur et Ecclesia; quod passum est caput, patiuntur et membra. Numquid enim servus est maior Domino suo, aut discipulus super magistrum? Si me, inquit, persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur. If patrem families Beelzebub vocaverunt, how many domestic magis eius? (Mt 10,24, et lo 15,20). Ingrediebantur ut viderent. ludas ille ad caput nostrum erat, ad caput nostrum ingrediebatur ut videret, id est ut exploraet: non ut haberet quod crederet, sed ut inveniret quod proderet. Ecce ingrediebatur ille ut videret, et hoc exemplum in capite nostro propositum est. Quid illa membra post assumptionem capitis nostri?

Nonne dicit apostolus Paulus: Propter subintroductos false fratres, qui subintroierunt proscultare libertatem nostram? (Gal 22,4). Ergo et isti ingrediebantur ut viderent, sunt enim hypocritae, simulatores mali adiungentes se ficta charitate, tumbantes omnes motus, omnia verba sanctorum, in ómnibus laqueos inquirentes. Et quid illis fit? Videte quid sequitur: Vana locutum est cor eorum: id est, loquuntur quasi ficta dilectione; vanum est quod loquuntur, verum non est, solidum non est. Et quia capitant unde inveniant accusationem, quid ait? Congregaverunt iniquitatem sibi. Parantes enim slanders inimici, quasi magni sibi videntur, quia habent quod accusent. Sibi congregaverunt iniquitatem. Sibi, inquit, non mihi. Quomodo ludas sibi, non Christo, sic et simulatores Ecclesiae sibi, non nobis: quia de illis et alibi dicitur: Et mentita est iniquitas

Iniquity lied against itself. They heaped up iniquity against themselves. And when they came in to spy, they went outside and talked. The one who came in to spy came out and spoke. If only he had stayed inside and spoken true things, because he would not have gone outside, where he speaks false things! He is a traitor and a persecutor; having gone out, speak. If you belong to the members of Christ, enter within, join the Head. If you are wheat, tolerate the tares; If you are wheat, tolerate the chaff; If you are a good fish, tolerate the bad fish that are inside the net. Why did you fly through the air before the time of the fork? Why did you pluck the wheat with you before the time of harvest? Why did you tear the nets before reaching land? They went outside and talked. 9 [v. 8]. All my enemies whispered against me together. Unite all my enemies against me. How much better would you have spoken to me together! What does tina mean against me? You conspired by forming a council, entering into a conspiracy. Christ speaks to them: You conspired against me, think with one accord with me. What do you have against me? Why aren't you with me? If you were always all together, you would not see each other in schism. The Apostle says: I beseech you, brothers, that you all say the same thing and that there be no schisms among you. All my enemies murmured against me together; They plotted evil against me. Rather they plotted against them, because they accumulated evils against themselves; but they accumulated them against me, because they had to be weighed or considered according to their intention. Well, no, because they couldn't do anything, that's why they didn't want to do it. The devil wanted to put an end to Christ, and Judaspre sibi (Ps 26:12). Congregaverunt iniquitatem sibi. Et quia intraverunt ut viderent, Egrediebantur foras, et loquebantur. Ille qui intravit ut videret, egrediebatur foras et loquebatur. Utinam intus esset, et vera loqueretur! non exiret foras ubi false loquitur. Traditor et persecutor est, egressus foras loquitur. Si ad membra Christi pertines, come intro, haere capiti. Tolerates zizania if triticum is; tolerates paleam, if frumentum is (Matt 13:30); tolerates bad pisces intra retia, if pisces bonus is. Quare ante tempus ventilationis avolasti? Quare ante tempus messis etiam frumenta eradicasti tecum? Quare antequam ad littus vinores, retia disrupisti? Egrediebantur foras, et loquebantur. 9 [v.8].

In idipsum adversum? ne whispered omnes inimici mei. Adversum me omnes in idipsum: quanto melius mecum in idipsum? Quid est, adversum me in idipsum? One council, one conspiracy. Christus ergo loquitur eis: Consentítis adversum me, consentite mihi: quid adversum me? quare non mecum? Idipsum si semper haberetis, non vos in schismata divideretís. Apostolus enim dicit: Obsecro vos, fratres, ut idipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata (2 Cor 1,10). In idipsum adversus me whispered omnes inimici mei: adversum me cogitabant mala mihi. Sibi potius, quia congregaverunt iniqttitatem sibi: sed ideo mihi, quia ex animo suo pendendi sunt. Non enim quia nihil faceré potuerunt, nihilíl faceré voluerunt. Nam et diabolus Christum exstingere concupivit, et Iu-

he tried to kill him; but by Christ dying and rising, we were made alive; The devil and Judas were given the reward for their ill will, not for our health. So that you may know that by intention each man must be weighed or appreciated in order to give him the reward or punishment, we found certain men who desired a certain good for a certain man (the blind man at the pool of Siloam), and such good as we long for, and yet they were called cursed. Well, when a little later that blind man, having now regained his sight in body and soul, demonstrated his marvelous healing to the Jews, who saw with their bodily eyes, but not with those of the heart, and he said to them while seeing him: Do you also want to become his disciples?, they, the Gospel writes, cursed him saying: Be your disciple of Him. Let what they cursed come upon us. These words were called a curse because of the perverse intention of those who uttered them, not because of any evil in the words. The one who recorded that they cursed paid attention to the spirit with which they said it, not to what they said. They plotted evil against me. But what evils did they plot against Christ? What evils did they plot against the martyrs? God turned them all into good. 10 [v. 9 }. They decreed a perverse word against me. What wicked word? Pay attention to the Head: Let us kill him and the inheritance will be ours. Fools! How should the inheritance be yours? Why did you kill him? You see that you killed him and the inheritance will not be yours. Has not he who sleeps lain down to rise? When you rejoiced at having killed Him, He slept, for it says in another psalm: I slept. They became angry and wanted to kill me, das Christum occidere voluit; deceased autem Christo et resurgente, nos vivificad sumus: diabolo tamen et Iudae merces malae voluntatis redditur, non nostrae salutis. Nam ut noveritis ex animo quemque pendendum ad retributionem vel praemii vel poenae, invenimus nomines bonum dixisse carem, et such bonum quale nosoptimus, et tamen maledicos appellatos. Quando a caeco illo quondam, iam illuminato et corpore et corde, convincingbantur Iudaei, videntes corpore, caeci corde: ait illis idem iam videns: Numquid et vos discipuli eius vultis esse? Et illi, inquit Evangelium, maledixerunt ei dicet is: Tu sis discipulus eius (lo 9,27 et 28).

Hoc nobis omnibus eveniat, quod illi maledicendo dixerunt. Maledictio is appellata est ex malévolo errore dicentium, non ex aliquo malo verborum: quo animo dixerint, non quid dixerint attendit, qui eos maledixisse narravit. Adversum they caught me bad mihi. Et quae mala Christo, quae mala martyribus? Omnia in bonum vertit Deus. 10 [v.9]. Verbum iniquum disposuerunt adversus me. What verbum iniquum? Ipsum caput attende: Occiiamus eum, et riostra erit haereditas (Mt 21,38). Stutty! quemodo vestra erit haereditas? quia occidistis eum? Ecce et occidistis eum, et vestra non erit haereditas. Numquid qui dormit non adüciet ut resurgat? When you exsultastis occidisse eum, ille dor-

but I slept. Because, if I hadn't wanted to, I wouldn't have slept. I slept, because I have the power to give up my life and to take it back. I slept, and I fell asleep and got up. Then the Jews become angry, hand over the land to the hands of the wicked, hand over the meat to the persecutors, suspend it on the log, pierce it with nails, pierce it with the spear. Has not he who sleeps lain down to rise? Why did he sleep? Adam was a figure of the one who was to come, and Adam fell asleep when Eve was formed from his side. Adam was a figure of Christ, and Eve, a figure of the Church; hence she was called mother of the living. When was Eve formed? SleepingAdam. When did the sacraments of the Church emerge from the side of Christ? When he slept on the cross. Does he who sleeps not lie down to get up? 11 [v. lO J. Who was the cause of your dream? He who came in to see and heaped up iniquity on himself. Indeed, the man of my friendship, in whom I waited; He who ate my bread spread his heel on me. He raised his foot above me; He wanted to trample me. Who is this close friend of yours? Judas. Did Christ trust in him, since he said in whom I waited? Didn't you know him from the beginning? Didn't he know what to do before he was born? Did he not say to all his disciples: I chose twelve of you, and one of you is a devil? How did he hope in him, if it were not because many faithful people trusted through Judas, and the Lord was transfigured in him? Many who had believed in Christ, when they saw Judas walking mivit: dicit ením et in alio psalmo, Ego dormivi. Illi saevierunt, et occidere voluerunt: Ego dortnivi. Nam si noluissem, nec dormissem. Ego dormivi: quia potestatem habeo ponendi animam meam, et potestatem babeo iterum sumendi eam (lo 10,18). Ego dormivi, et sommum cepi, et exsurrexi (Ps 3,6). Saeviant ergo Iudaei, terra tradatur in manus impii (Iob 9,24), caro permittatur manibus persequentium, suspendant in ligno, clavis transfigant, lancea perfodiant: Numquid qui dormit non adüciet ut resurgat? Utquid slept? Quia Adam forma erat futuri (Rom 5,14): et Adam dormivit, quando de latere eius Eva facta est (Gen 2,21). Adam in figura Christi, Eve in figura Ecclesiae: unde est appellata mater vivorum. When is Eva factory? Dum dormeret Adam.

When latere Christi sacramenta Ecclesiae proluxerunt? Cum dormeret in intersection. Numquid qui dormit non adüciet ut resurgat? 11 [v.10]. Where did you sleep? Ex illo qui ingressus est ut videret, et congregavit iniquitatem sibi. Etenim homo pacis meae in quem speravi, qui edebat panes meos, amplificavit super me calcaneum. Erexit super me pedem: conculeare me voluit. Quí est iste homo pacis ipsius? ludas. Et in illum Christus speravit, quia dixit, In quem speravi? Nonne illum ab initio noverat? nonne antequam nasceretur futurum sciebat? nonne omnibus discipulis suis dixerat, Ego vos duodecim elect, et unus ex vobis diabolus est? (lo 6.71). Quomodo ergo in illum speravit, nisi quia in membris suis ipse est, et quod multi fideles de luda speraverunt, hoc in

Among the twelve disciples they trusted him because he was one of many. But Christ, who was among the waiting members, just as He is among those who hunger and thirst, just as He said: I am hungry, He said: I waited. Therefore, if we say to him: Lord, when did you wait?, as it was said to him: Lord, when "were you hungry"?; as he told us there: When you did it to one of my little ones, you did it to me, so it can be said here: When one of my little ones waited, I waited. Who did I wait for? The man of my friendship was the one I waited for; in which he ate my bread. In what way did he declare it in the passion with these same prophetic words? Let's see it. He made him known by the morsel of bread, as Saint John says, so that it is evident that it was said of him: He who ate my bread. Also when Judas approached to hand him over, he kissed him; In this is also fulfilled what was said in this psalm: The man of my friendship. 12 [v. l l }. But you, Lord, have mercy on me. He says this considering the nature of a servant, the nature that he has taken from being poor and needy. Blessed is he who cares for the poor and the needy. Take pity on me and resurrect me, and I will give them what they deserve. Notice when it was said, and that it is already fulfilled. The Jews killed Christ so as not to lose the place; by killing him they lost the place; driven out of the kingdom, they scattered. As soon as he was resurrected, he sent them tribulations: he sent them to correct them, not to condemn them. That city, in which the people roared like a lion that casts its paw and roars, shouting: Crucify, crucify, is Dominus transfigured? Quando enim videbant Iudam multi qui crediderant in Christum, atribulare Inter duodecim disciples, sperabant in illum aliqui; quia talis erat, quales et caeteri: Christus autem quia in membris suis erat hoc sperantibus, quomodo in illis est esurientibus et sitientibus; quomodo dixit Esurivi, sic dixit Speravi. Proinde si sic illi dicamus, Domine, when sperasti? Quomodo illi dictum est, Domine, quando esuristi? Quomodo nobis ibi dixit, Cum uni ex minimis meis fecistis, mihi fecistis (Mt 25,37.40); sic potest dicere: Cum unus ex minimis meis speravit, ego speravi. In quem speravi? Homo pacis meae, in quem speravi, qui edebat panes meos. Quomodo ipsum otendit in passione, de istis verbis prophetiae?

Per buccellam illum designavit (lo 13,26), ut appareret de ¡lio dictum, Qui edebat panes meos. Rursus quando venit ut traderet eum, osculum illi dedit Mt 26,49), ut appareret de illo dictum, Homo pacis meae. 12 [v. l l ]. T» autem, Domine, miserere mei. Hoc ex forma servi, hoc ex forma inopis et pauperis. Beatus enim qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem. Miserere mei, et resuscita me, et reddam illis. See when dictum est, iam factum est. Occiderunt enim Christum Iudaei, ne perdiderunt locum (lo 11,48): illo occiso perdiderunt locum; eradicati a regno, dispersi sunt. Suscitatus reddidit illis tribulationem: reddidit ad admonitionem, nondum ad damnationem. Civitas enim illa in qua fremuit populus, tanquam leo rapiens el rugiens, exclamans, Qrucifi^e, crucifige

When the Jews were expelled from there, it was occupied by the Christians, and now no Jews live in it. The Church of Christ was planted in the place where the thistles of the Synagogue were uprooted. Therefore, truly their fire was kindled, as it is kindled in thistles. The Lord was like a green log. He said this same thing when some women cried for Him when He was going to death on the way to Calvary: Do not cry for me; Cry, yes, for yourselves and for your children. From this it follows that it was predicted: Resurrect me and I will give them what they deserve. Because if these things are done on the green tree, what will not be done on the dry tree? When can the green tree be consumed by the fire of thorns? However, the Jews caught fire as fire catches fire in thorns or thistles. Fire consumes the thorns, and when applied to any green tree, it hardly ignites it, since the sap of the tree resists the slow and tenuous flame; However, this is suitable for reducing thorns to sparks. Resurrect me and I will give them what they deserve. Do not think, brothers, that the Son is less powerful than the Father because he said: Raise me, as if He had not been able to resurrect Himself. We must keep in mind that he resurrected what could die; that is, the flesh that died, the same was resurrected. However, lest you think that God, Father of Christ, could have resurrected Christ, and Christ himself, being the Word of God equal to the Father, could not have resurrected his flesh, listen to the Gospel: I will tear down this temple and in three days I will raise it up; And so that we would not doubt, the Evangelist adds, he said this of the temple of his body. Resurrect me and I will give them what they deserve.

(Le 23,21, et lo 19,6), eradicatis inde Iudaeis, Christianos habet, a Iudaeo nullo inhabitatur. Plantata est ibi Ecclesia Christí, unde eradicatae sunt spinae Synagogae. Proinde veré ignis eorum exarsit, sicut in spinis (Ps 117,12): Dominus autem tanquam lignum viride erat. Hoc ipse ait, quando plangebant quaedam mulleres veluti moriturum Christum, Nolite flere super me, sed super vos ipsas freight, et super filias vestros: ex hoc praedicens, Suscita me, et reddam illis. Si enim in viridi ligno haec faciunt, in arid quid fiet? (Le 2.3,28.31). When did I possit viride lignum did I consume ab igne spinarum? Exarserunt enim velut ignis in spinis. Ignis spinas consume, et cuicumque viridi ligno adhibetur, difficile accenditur, humor enim ligni resistit flammae slowe et marcidae, tamen idoneae ad consumendas spinas. Et suscita me, et reddam illis. Ne forte sane, fratres, minus potcntem Filium, quam Patrem putetis, ex eo quia dixit, Suscita me, quod ipse se suscitare non possit. Hoc enim suscitavit quod mori poterat: id est, caro mortua est, caro suscitata est. Ne tamen putetis, quia Deus Pater Christi potuit suscitare Christum, id est carnem Filii sui; et ipse Christus, cum Verbum sit Dei aequale Patri, non poterat carnem suam suscitare: audite ex Gospel, Solvite templum hoc, et in triduo suscitabo illud. Hoc autem Evangelista, ne etiam inde dubitaremus, dicebat, inquit, de temple corporis sui (lo 2,19.21), et resuscita me, et reddam illis.

13 [v. 12]. By this I knew that you loved me, that my enemy will not rejoice over me. The Jews rejoiced when they saw Christ on the cross, because they thought that their desire to kill him was fulfilled. They saw the fruit of their cruelty when they contemplated Christ hanging on the cross; They shook their heads saying: If he is the Son of God, let him come down from the cross. He who could descend did not descend; He did not show power, but rather taught patience. If he had descended from the cross when they had spoken the above words, it would have appeared that he had given in to their reproaches and that, defeated, he could not tolerate their insults. He preferred to remain on the cross in the face of those outrages, to remain nailed to those head movements. They shook their heads because they were not united with her. He clearly taught us patience. Because he did the most formidable thing who did not want to do what the Jews invited him to do, since it is much greater to be resurrected than to come down from the cross. For my enemy will not rejoice over me. They were glad then; but Christ was resurrected, he was glorified. Now they see that the human race is converted to their name; insult now, shake your head.
